Influence of Soil Particle Size, Shape, and Mineralogy on Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation
abstract: Microbially induced calcite precipitation (MICP) has gained increasing attention as a potential sustainable ground improvement technique. This study investigates the influence of soil particle size, shape, and mineralogy on the MICP process and on the evolution of shear-wave velocity (Vs) in biocemented soil columns. MICP experimental soil column tests were conducted using three silica sands (Ottawa 20/30, F-75, and F-110), a naturally carbonate-rich silty sand (Blessington soil), and artificially graded carbonate–silica sand mixtures (75% silica sand and 25% Iceland spar). Vs and chemical measurements were performed during MICP experiments, and biocemented samples were preserved for scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses. Results showed that the amount of precipitated calcite in carbonate-rich Blessington soil columns was up to twice that observed in the silica sand columns, highlighting the strong influence of soil mineralogy on the MICP process. The Vs profiles showed an overall trend of decreasing Vs with an increase in median particle size tested, which indicated the dominant effect of the number of particle contacts on the evolution of Vs with cementation. Furthermore, carbonate–sand mixtures exhibited increased calcite precipitation, but reduced Vs compared to their pure silica sand counterpart columns, demonstrating the combined effects of soil mineralogy and particle shape on both calcite precipitation and stiffness development. SEM observations revealed a distinct change in the morphology of precipitated calcite on the surfaces of carbonate soil particles (Blessington and Iceland spar) forming closely packed, uniform calcite crystals resembling the growth of a preexisting carbonate phase, which suggested that carbonate soil particles offered a lower energy barrier that facilitated a more extensive calcite precipitation compared to silica sands. Furthermore, the nature of cementation bonds evolved from contact cementation to cementation matrix and ultimately to pore filling as the median particle size of the tested soils decreased, implying that the formation, morphology, and extent of cementation bonds are governed by the specific surface area of soil. Based on these insights, a new model is proposed that relates Vs to normalized calcite content, which effectively captures the variation of Vs with cementation across different soil types tested in the present study, as well as within a broader dataset compiled from the literature.

title: Operational Interface Governance, Digital Capability, and Resilience Support in Cross-Border Critical Infrastructure: A Capability-Pathway Perspective
abstract: Cross-border critical infrastructure operations depend on aligned information, authorization, and coordination interfaces across organizations and jurisdictions. This study examines operational interface governance scenario (OIGS) as an upstream condition associated with digital capability and its translation into resistance and recovery support. Resilience support denotes the focal operating organization’s perceived support role rather than overall system resilience. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities perspective, a between-subjects scenario-based survey of 371 practitioners was analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) and bias-corrected bootstrapping. Enhanced OIGS was positively associated with digital capability, which was positively associated with strategic sensing, timely decision-making, and change implementation capabilities. Direct paths from digital capability to both resilience-support dimensions were supported; timely decision-making had the strongest supported direct path to recovery support. Change implementation capability was not supported as a direct predictor of recovery support because its 95% bias-corrected bootstrap confidence interval included zero, whereas the OIGS–digital capability–change implementation capability–recovery support chain pathway was supported. The findings characterize cross-border infrastructure resilience support as a governance and capability process and support pairing interface governance with digital investment.

title: In mice, a population of male germ cells show characteristics of nonapoptotic cell death during G0 arrest.
abstract: In mammals, a small population of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is established shortly after birth. These cells self-renew and produce sperm for the male's reproductive lifespan, passing the genome on to the next generation. Establishment of a population of SSCs with high genomic integrity is essential. SSCs are derived from a much larger precursor population of male germ cells (MGCs) that differentiate during fetal life. During the last third of gestation, MGCs undergo a prolonged period of G0 cell cycle arrest during which they sustain high levels of transcription and acquire epigenetic programming for SSC fate. Although these differentiation steps can cause cellular and genomic damage, it has been unclear whether selection for germ cell quality occurs during G0 arrest since no classic markers of cell death have been detected. In this study, we used a mouse model to characterize a population of MGCs that begin to accumulate markers of cell death, such as AnnexinV (AnV) and propidium iodide (PI), at E16.5. The AnV- and PI-positive MGC population is characterized by low expression of the RNA-binding protein, Dead End 1, and exhibits dsDNA breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction. Interestingly, we do not see evidence of an active cell death cascade until the time of birth, when phosphorylation of MLKL, a hallmark of necroptotic cell death, occurs. Based on these findings, we propose that variable cellular health is an important basis for selection of SSC precursors.

Did You Hear That? Detecting AI Voice Agents by Exploiting Their Robustness
abstract: AI voice agents enable scalable vishing and impersonation attacks, yet existing detection methods face practical limitations. Artifact-based detectors degrade as synthesis quality improves, challenge–response tests are socially awkward, and adversarial jamming must often be loud or continuous to disrupt modern automatic speech recognition (ASR). We introduce HEARD, a detection framework built on a new principle: instead of perturbing the AI while remaining imperceptible to humans, HEARD applies brief, conspicuous distortions that humans notice but robust ASR systems largely ignore. A human caller is likely to comment on the disturbance, misunderstand the utterance, or request repetition, whereas an AI agent continues coherently from the recovered transcription. We map fifteen audible distortions into three families and evaluate them across six ASR models spanning multiple architectures and five years of development, as well as an experiment involving 41 human volunteers. Using semantic similarity and an LLM-based conversational-legibility metric, we find that across 2,421 LibriSpeech and TED-LIUM utterances, modern ASRs preserve a mean legibility of 97.8%, while the best distortion keeps every model at or above 98.3%. Moreover, performance improves with model recency, making stronger ASR systems easier, not harder, to distinguish from humans.

title: Active Acoustic Probes for AI Voice Call Detection
abstract: AI voice calls are making it increasingly practical to impersonate people during live audio conversations, whether through voice cloning, real-time conversion, or autonomous voice agents. Current defenses remain mostly passive: they inspect received audio for artifacts created by current generators, which locks defenders into an arms race structurally favoring the attacker. Active defenses invert this dynamic by injecting fresh evidence during the call, but they typically require the remote speaker to cooperate by performing a challenge task. We propose an active acoustic probe that requires no such cooperation: it verifies whether the returned audio traversed a genuine physical speaker-to-microphone path. During a call, the verifier sends a brief high-frequency acoustic challenge and checks whether it survives in the returned audio. Normal physical paths preserve the challenge, whereas the tested voice-conversion paths suppress it. This yields a simple, explainable signal-processing rule calibrated only on normal physical-path recordings. The probe is correctly detected in 99% of trials across diverse consumer audio form factors, from open laptop/phone playback to ear-worn headphones and earbuds, while all 200 outputs from four tested speech-to-speech and voice-conversion configurations fail the detector.

Building an Evaluation Harness for Oil & Gas AI Agents
abstract: While operators and service companies are aggressively deploying AI agents for various oil and gas use cases, methods to evaluate their outputs and behaviors remain rarely discussed. Existing publications focus mostly on the accuracy of the final outputs, neglecting important metrics like consistency and efficiency. The objective of this project is to build an evaluation harness and use it to measure the performance of agents against drilling data analysis tasks. DrillingGPT (DGPT), a drilling data AI agent, is one of 100+ agents deployed in Occidental's internal agent platform. We developed an evaluation suite consisting of 19 tasks of varying difficulties, curated and verified by subject matter experts. Each task was run 5 times (i.e k=5) to compute pass@k and pass^k metrics to measure success rates and consistency. Additionally, tool call precision, recall, and redundancy rate were measured to assess the agent's behaviors. Traces were then examined to provide additional details about potential failure modes. In one pilot execution, DGPT achieved pass@k of 63%, pass@1 of 48%, and pass^k of 37%, which indicated that the agent can often reach correct answers but did not do so consistently. Performance was somewhat satisfactory on easy and medium tasks, while hard tasks showed a pronounced decline in all metrics. Trace analysis identified key failure modes that include partial errors in multi-well responses, compounding mistakes in multi-table aggregations, and failure to refuse out-of-scope requests. From tool-calling perspective, DGPT appeared to act more conservatively with high precision and lower recall. We also observed cases where DGPT skipped necessary tools to achieve its goals. The harness offers significant improvement over a simple accuracy metric for evaluating agent performance. These insights offer valuable guidance for developers and engineers in identifying areas and methodologies for further iteration. This project introduces a quantitative and systematic approach to evaluate AI agents built specifically for oil and gas use cases, providing a more holistic framework that goes beyond simple output accuracy by also considering factors like consistency, efficiency, and tool usage in real-world scenarios.

title: When Does Randomized Oversight Align AI Agents That Can Conceal?
abstract: Oversight changes the evidence it relies on. We ask when randomized audits and scoring align AI agents that can conceal misconduct and alter records. Stronger auditing makes undeterred violations better hidden. Because the provider writes the agent's objective, sanctions need not stop at forfeiture, and rare audits deter every type of agent if evidence survives concealment and audit draws cannot be learned in advance. When evidence can be erased, deterrence must come from lower gains from violation, such as credit for stopping, or from costlier or fewer ways to conceal. These conditions identify what failed when agents in OpenAI's cybersecurity evaluations compromised parts of Hugging Face's infrastructure in July 2026.

title: Hierarchical cross-modal spatiotemporal attention network for crop yield prediction in complex Himalayan agroecosystems
abstract: Introduction Accurate crop yield prediction is essential for precision agriculture, climate-resilient farm management, and timely decision-making. However, yield prediction remains challenging because of complex, nonlinear, and multi-scale interactions among crop physiology, soil conditions, weather variability, and management practices. Conventional statistical, machine learning, and deep learning approaches, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, often have limitations in capturing long-range temporal dependencies, hierarchical spatial relationships, heterogeneous data modalities, and predictive uncertainty. Methods This study proposes a Hierarchical Cross-Modal Spatio-Temporal Attention Network (HCM-STAN) for crop yield prediction using a unified attention-based framework for integrating heterogeneous agro-environmental data. The architecture incorporates four principal components: (i) hierarchical spatio-temporal attention operating across tree, block, orchard, and regional scales; (ii) a cross-modal attention module for adaptive fusion of IoT-based soil sensor observations, weather data, plant physiological measurements, and drone-based multispectral imagery; (iii) a soil-aware attention head that explicitly models soil memory, hysteresis effects, and root-zone dynamics; and (iv) an uncertainty-aware prediction module combining Monte Carlo dropout and quantile regression to generate calibrated prediction intervals. The framework was evaluated using a multi-source dataset collected from Himalayan apple orchards during 2023–2026, comprising 1,247 monitored trees across three commercial orchards. Results The proposed HCM-STAN achieved an R 2 of 0.89 for four-week-ahead crop yield prediction, representing a 15.6% improvement over the CNN-LSTM baseline. Furthermore, zero-shot transfer to mango orchards achieved an R 2 of 0.67, corresponding to approximately 75% of the performance obtained under full training. Discussion The results demonstrate that integrating hierarchical spatio-temporal representation learning, cross-modal attention, soil-aware modelling, and uncertainty estimation can effectively address the heterogeneous and dynamic nature of crop yield prediction in complex mountain agroecosystems. The observed zero-shot transfer performance further indicates the potential of HCM-STAN to generalize across crop systems without crop-specific retraining. Overall, the proposed framework provides a promising foundation for reliable, uncertainty-aware yield forecasting and can support precision agriculture, climate-smart farm management, and data-driven decision-making in heterogeneous agroecosystems.

title: Tourism Demand Prediction With Tourist‐Generated Images and Text: An Ensemble Sparse ELM Approach
abstract: This study examines the predictive value of tourist‐generated images and text for daily tourism demand forecasting. Building on established L 0 ‐regularized extreme learning machine (ELM) formulations and ADMM‐based sparse optimization, we construct an ensemble forecasting framework, termed ES‐ L 0 ‐ELM, that combines image‐derived and textual predictors with numerical variables. The framework integrates sparse output‐weight estimation with model selection and weighted aggregation. Experiments on Jiuzhaigou and Mount Siguniang show that ES‐ L 0 ‐ELM achieves lower forecasting errors than the evaluated benchmarks. On the Jiuzhaigou dataset, it reduces MAPE by 18.66% and 14.33% relative to recent tourism forecasting models BERT‐ELM and TFIDF‐Tran‐ELM, respectively. Image features provide greater predictive gains than text features, whereas their combination yields the best performance. This study provides a sparse ensemble forecasting framework and empirical evidence of the complementary value of tourist‐generated images and text.

title: Genomic prediction of single cross families of perennial ryegrass under two nitrogen managements.
abstract: The performance of a single cross is determined by the additive effects of the parents and their interactions, which can be estimated through general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA). With genome-wide marker information, it is possible to predict GCA for new parents and the genetic value of unrealized crosses. Several studies in crops such as maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.) have demonstrated the potential of genomic prediction for single-cross performance. However, no study to date has explored its relevance in perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne L.), an obligate allogamous species bred in genetically heterogeneous families. In this study, we estimated genetic parameters and evaluated genomic prediction models for dry matter yield and nutritive quality traits in F2 family bulk. Data were obtained from a large partial diallel involving 104 parents from two genetically distinct subpopulations identified by admixture analysis. Families were evaluated across multiple environments under two nitrogen conditions. Genotyping-by-sequencing generated 42,145 high-quality variants used to estimate genomic relationships. Variance component analyses revealed limited GCA and SCA interactions with environment and nitrogen management. Predictive abilities of parental models exceeded 0.60 and often 0.70 for most traits, whereas including nonadditive effects did not improve predictive ability. Genome-wide association analyses identified six quantitative trait locus regions and 45 candidate genes within linkage disequilibrium intervals averaging 92 kb. Our results demonstrate that genomic prediction of single crosses in perennial ryegrass can achieve high accuracy, particularly when both parents are represented in the training population.

Some generalizations of the tornado model
abstract: A possible mechanism of tornado generation is associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability. The supercooled cloud-air mixture near the axis starts to descend and, due to the super adiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated near-surface air mass rises. The complete system of equations for full model includes equations for the stream function, for the azimuthal velocity component, and for the change in density. The refined model considers rotating convection within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics. The simplest model uses a separate equation for the stream function and can be applied to the initial stage of vortex generation. Within the framework of the simplest model, an analytical solution is combined from 8 linear dependencies by height. Rotation increases due to the conservation of angular momentum. Within the framework of the refined model, some unidirectional differential rotation arises, but it depends on boundary conditions (can be local). The full model studies the tornado development as rotating convection from the very beginning to the quasi-stationary stage. Velocity components increase in a coordinated manner. Two cases are considered: a single whirlwind and a two-eyed tornado. Radial flows converge towards the central part of the tornado near the earth surface, and there is an outflow from the "wall" to the axis and to the periphery near the top of the tornado. The maximum vertical velocity component is achieved at a certain radial distance at a certain height. The maximum azimuthal velocity component is achieved in the tornado "wall". Tornado generation criteria are discussed.

Uncertainty-Aware Semi-Supervised Framework with Supervised Contrastive Learning for Sugarcane Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Sugarcane leaf diseases severely impact crop yield and quality, making accurate and timely detection critical for sustainable agriculture. Conventional deep learning models for plant disease detection depend on large annotated datasets, which are expensive to obtain and challenging to prepare due to challenges commonly observed across crop disease detection tasks, including (i) high intra-class variation caused by diverse symptom expressions across growth stages, (ii) subtle inter-class similarities between diseased and healthy tissues, and (iii) the risk of noisy labels degrading model reliability. To handle these challenges, we presented an Uncertainty-aware Mean-Teacher based Semi-Supervised Learning Disease Detection Network (U-SSDNet) that leverages unlabeled data while maintaining robustness. First, discrete wavelet transform preprocessing is applied to enhance lesion visibility and reduce intra- class variation. Subsequently, the KL divergence is employed to refine the pseudo-labels and reduce the impact of confirmation bias. At the same time, supervised contrastive learning is applied to make the features more distin- guishable and improve the separation among different classes. Experimental evaluations on sugarcane leaf disease datasets, considered a representative case study, demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves performance close to that of fully supervised models while requiring far fewer annotated samples and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised approaches.

title: SentiAgent: An agentic LLM framework for context-aware and explainable sentiment analysis.
abstract: Sentiment analysis has become a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) due to the rapid growth of user-generated content across social media, e-commerce, healthcare, education, and customer feedback platforms. Despite the success of transformer-based models and Large Language Models (LLMs), existing approaches often struggle with contextual ambiguity, implicit sentiment, sarcasm, commonsense reasoning, and limited explainability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes SentiAgent, a novel Agentic LLM framework for context-aware and explainable sentiment analysis. The framework employs multiple autonomous agents that collaboratively perform contextual understanding, external knowledge integration, sentiment reasoning, and explanation generation. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets-SST-2, IMDB Reviews, Sentiment140, and Amazon Product Reviews-demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. SentiAgent achieved 97.43% accuracy, 97.18% precision, 96.95% recall, 97.06% F1-score, and 0.99 AUC, consistently outperforming conventional machine learning, deep learning, transformer-based, and standalone LLM models. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each autonomous agent, while qualitative analyses highlight the framework's ability to produce transparent and interpretable sentiment predictions. The proposed framework provides a scalable and trustworthy solution for next-generation explainable sentiment analysis.•Introduces SentiAgent, a collaborative Agentic LLM framework for context-aware and explainable sentiment analysis.•Combines contextual understanding, external commonsense knowledge, and autonomous reasoning to improve sentiment prediction and interpretability.•Achieves state-of-the-art performance on four benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior accuracy, robustness, and transparency over existing approaches.

Using AI-powered modelling for drought forecasting in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea
abstract: Context The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is vulnerable to drought due to monsoon-driven variable precipitation that affects agricultural production and water security. Reliable multi-timescale drought forecasting aids risk mitigation; however, nonlinear non-stationary drought signals are hard to capture indata-scarce regions. Aims This study developed and validated a Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise-Long Short-Term Memory (CEEMDAN-LSTM) hybrid Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) drought forecasting model. Its performance is systematically compared against a standalone LSTM for multiple SPEI timescales under DPRK climatic conditions. Methods Monthly meteorological records from 10 stations collected over a period of 60 years were used to derive SPEI time series. CEEMDAN decomposed SPEI into intrinsic mode functions for noise reduction and trend extraction as LSTM inputs; hyperparameters were optimised by Bayesian optimisation. Model performance was assessed with Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Key results CEEMDAN-LSTM generally outperformed standalone LSTM with timescale-dependent skill. Short-term SPEI predictions had inherent accuracy limits (NSE < 0.5) yet reduced relative errors. Medium- to long-term SPEI yielded large accuracy gains (max NSE = 0.95 for SPEI-12), with residual-distribution analysis showing effective suppression of extreme prediction errors. Spatial heterogeneity existed; complex terrain at stations such as Chongjin limited decomposition-driven improvements. Conclusions CEEMDAN-LSTM improves forecast skill by processing non-stationary drought signals. Without complex external predictors, this hybrid method enables reliable medium-long-term drought monitoring and extreme-event detection. Implications This single-variable time-series method enables data-efficient drought early warning for data-scarce regions, supporting drought response and adaptive water management without large-scale remote-sensing or global datasets.

title: The dynamic relationship between inclusive leadership, job crafting towards strengths and employees’ career calling: the moderating role of core self-evaluation
abstract: Drawing on the Work as Calling Theory (WCT), we developed and tested a longitudinal model of how employees’ career calling develops over time. Specifically, we examined the dynamic relationships among job crafting towards strengths (JCS), inclusive leadership, and career calling, as well as the moderating role of core self-evaluation (CSE). This study employed a three-wave longitudinal survey design with data collected from 309 Chinese employees at three-month intervals and analyzed the data using cross-lagged panel modeling (CLPM), supplemented by random-intercept cross-lagged panel modeling (RI-CLPM). CLPM results showed that JCS and career calling positively predicted each other from T1 to T2, whereas only career calling predicted subsequent JCS from T2 to T3. Perceived inclusive leadership and career calling showed reciprocal positive associations across both time intervals. Supplementary RI-CLPM analyses further suggested that these interrelationships partly reflected stable between-person differences, although T2 career calling positively predicted T3 JCS and perceived inclusive leadership at the within-person level. Furthermore, moderation analyses showed that the association between JCS and subsequent career calling became more positive at higher levels of CSE across both time intervals, whereas CSE weakened the positive association between perceived inclusive leadership and subsequent career calling from T2 to T3. This study extends Work as Calling Theory by advancing a more dynamic understanding of career calling and offers practical insights into how organizations can foster employees’ career calling through proactive job crafting, supportive leadership, and differentiated developmental support.

title: Lean tools and Industry 4.0 technologies: a multidimensional analysis of firm performance
abstract: This study aims to examine how Lean/Lean Six Sigma (LSS) tools and Industry 4.0 (I4.0) technologies relate to firm performance across multiple dimensions and time horizons. Prior research has focused predominantly on productivity; the authors extend this view to profitability, capital structure, financing conditions and internationalization, distinguishing between short- (2020–2022) and long-term (2012–2022) performance effects. Using survey data from 140 industrial firms in inland Portugal, Lean/LSS and I4.0 constructs were modeled through a parcel-based measurement approach and estimated using Structural Equation Modeling with robust maximum likelihood. Performance indicators were derived from secondary accounting data, expressed as short- and long-term deltas. The structural model incorporates a theoretically grounded performance cascade linking productivity, return on assets, indebtedness, interest rate and internationalization. Lean/LSS and I4.0 technologies exhibit strong complementarity, yet neither shows direct effects on short- or long-term financial performance indicators. Instead, performance evolves through a powerful internal propagation mechanism: productivity improvements drive increases in return on assets, which in turn reduce indebtedness. This cascade is significant in the short term and substantially stronger over the long term, explaining up to 91.5% of long-term return on assets variance and 62% of long-term indebtedness variance. Downstream effects on interest rate and internationalization remain non-significant. By combining a multidimensional performance framework with explicit temporal differentiation and a performance to-performance cascade, this study clarifies how operational improvements translate, or fail to translate, into financial outcomes. Results show that the impact of Lean and I4.0 is indirect and unfolds primarily through internal financial propagation rather than direct effects on top-level accounting metrics. This contributes new empirical evidence on the temporal and structural mechanisms linking operational and digital transformation to firm performance and suggests that firms should adopt a long-term perspective, combining Lean and digital transformation initiatives while monitoring performance across multiple dimensions.
journal: International Journal of Lean Six Sigma

title: Life cycle environmental and cost analysis of a building insulated with different insulation materials: a British case study
abstract: To evaluate the whole-life environmental and economic performance of four insulation materials used in the UK, hemp fibre, wood fibre, glass wool and extruded polystyrene (XPS), by comparing their embodied and operational impacts within a consistent regulatory and modelling framework. A like-for-like assessment was conducted for a representative British single-family dwelling by integrating dynamic energy simulation with life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle costing (LCC) within a cradle-to-grave framework aligned with EN 15978 and EN 15804. Operational energy demand (Module B6) was simulated using DesignBuilder/EnergyPlus. Embodied impacts across Modules A1–A5 and end-of-life Modules C1–C4 were calculated in One Click LCA using Environmental Product Declarations and aligned generic datasets. Whole-life costs were evaluated over a 70-year study period using discounted cash-flow analysis. Operational energy dominates whole-life impacts for all insulation options, with annual energy use ranging from 11,598 to 11,833 kWh and minimal variation due to equivalent regulatory U-value targets. Whole-life global warming potential is similarly close (≈2,342–2,418 kgCO2e/m2, excluding Module D), with hemp fibre and glass wool showing slightly lower values. Embodied impacts (A1–A5) differ more clearly, favouring hemp fibre and glass wool over wood fibre and XPS. LCC results are tightly clustered (NPV ≈ £49.2k–£49.4k; ≈ £1.89k/year), suggesting cost is not a key differentiator. The study offers a UK-specific integrated comparison combining dynamic simulation, LCA and LCC, highlighting that while insulation choice affects embodied carbon, major carbon reductions depend primarily on reducing and decarbonising operational energy.

title: Dynamic Interpolation for Training-Time Prediction Reshaping in Low-Light Image Enhancement
abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is an important image/video processing problem for reliable visual systems under poor illumination, yet it remains challenging due to the strong coupling among insufficient illumination, noise amplification, and structural degradation. Existing methods typically rely on sophisticated network architectures or engineered objective functions. While effective, the former increases model complexity and deployment burden, whereas the latter relies on empirically tuned loss weights. We revisit supervised LLIE from a training-dynamics perspective and observe that brightness-related errors tend to converge early, while residual noise and structural artifacts often remain insufficiently optimized in later stages. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic Interpolation Training-only Module (DITM), which introduces no additional learnable parameters and adaptively reshapes the model prediction for supervised feed-forward LLIE training. Specifically, DITM employs brightness-aware interpolation, in which the model prediction is combined with a mean brightness-aligned image constructed by rescaling the model prediction according to the mean brightness of the ground-truth image. By reducing the relative dominance of global brightness discrepancy, DITM makes residual local errors more influential during backpropagation after global luminance has largely stabilized, thereby facilitating artifact suppression and fine-detail restoration in later training stages. DITM is used only during training and is fully removed at inference, introducing no additional inference cost. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based LLIE backbones show that DITM consistently improves fidelity and perceptual quality while preserving the inference-time architecture and introducing no additional inference-time computation.

title: From Using AI to Building AI: Construct Your Personal Intelligent Platform
journal: Singapore University of Social Sciences - World Scientific Future Economy Series

title: Does Retrieval Relevance Matter for AI-Generated Book Introductions? A Matched-Random Memory Evaluation
abstract: Digital libraries are exploring LLMs for reading-promotion services such as automatically generated book introductions. A tempting design is to retrieve relevant accumulated reader feedback at generation time. We test this in a zero-human-subject controlled experiment: a librarian agent generates introductions for 32 held-out test books under three conditions (No Memory, a composition-matched random-memory control, and Relevant Memory, operationalized through embedding similarity and genre matching), judged on four criteria by a separate-model LLM (GPT-4o). The key methodological device is the composition-matched random-memory control, which isolates retrieval relevance from mere context presence. Lexical uptake checks confirm that retrieved memory is incorporated into generated introductions. Relevant Memory shows no LLM-judged advantage over No Memory on the composite outcome, but outperforms Matched-Random Memory on hook quality (Δ = 0.125, 95% CI [0.023, 0.250]). This pattern suggests that retrieval selection may matter when additional memory is introduced, rather than providing a general improvement over a strong no-memory baseline. We frame the study as pipeline validity evidence rather than evidence of improved human-perceived quality.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries

title: Applications of Generative AI for Advancing Scientific Content Production, Evaluation and Dissemination
abstract: Generative AI is becoming part of how scientific content is being produced, evaluated and communicated. Large language models (LLMs) can write science news, simulate readers, retrieve evidence, generate scientific hypotheses, write code, and execute research workflows. These capabilities create opportunities for accelerating scientific discovery and broadening access to scientific information, but they also introduce risks related to hallucination and trustworthiness. This doctoral dissertation studies how generative AI can support scientific content production and dissemination, while preserving trust, comprehension, and replicability. The completed work includes three components: (1) detecting LLM-generated science news through SANews and GFS, (2) evaluating science communication through reader learning using KnowledgeGain and LLMSim, and (3) benchmarking LLM agents for research replication with ReplicatorBench and ReplicatorAgent. The proposed work extends these directions toward learning-optimized science news generation, MESH for multimodal evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, and MERIT, a simulation-grounded framework for evaluating autonomous AI co-scientists and hypothesis testing in computational materials discovery. The overarching goal is to develop evaluation methods and AI systems that make scientific outputs not only fluent and scalable, but also grounded, useful, and interpretable.
journal: Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries

title: Towards Automated Analysis of Scientific Limitations and FutureWork
abstract: Scientific progress relies on acknowledging epistemic boundaries and charting forward directions. However, limitations and future work are systematically omitted or hedged to improve publication prospects. With escalating submission volumes, reviewers increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs), yet zero-shot models generate superficial, hallucinated, or author-echoing feedback. This thesis presents a unified framework to discover, evaluate, recommend, and generate scholarly limitations and future work. First, we introduce LimTopic and FutureScope, using hybrid BERTopic, LLM pipelines to uncover thematic limitation patterns and model thirteen years of NLP future work trajectories. Second, to resolve metric inflation from surface metrics, we establish BAGELS and FutureGen, introducing atomic Limitation Units (LUs) for fine-grained PointWise evaluation and RAG-based future work generation with iterative critique loops. Third, we construct citation knowledge graphs with GraphSAGE to recommend paper-specific limitations. Finally, SciLimAgents couples intrinsic (LimitAgents) and novelty (NovAgents) specialist agents over a 120K-paper shared memory, aligned via on-policy preference optimization and composite process rewards. Across extensive benchmarks, our frameworks demonstrate substantial gains over frontier baselines, establishing a principled foundation for AI-assisted scientific quality assurance.

title: Understanding the wildfire adaptation communications landscape in the western United States: examining actors, media type, and geographies
Machine learning-guided leaf margin classification and discovery that BcPHB promoter selection rewires a BcPHB–BcLMI1 module to shape leaf margins in Brassica campestris
abstract: The morphological diversification of leaf margins reflects the evolutionary reshaping of conserved developmental programs. However, fully deciphering the underlying molecular basis remains challenging due to difficulties in phenotype quantification and the incomplete characterization of complex regulatory networks. In this study, we established a computer-vision framework to decode leaf lobe trait and identified the HD-ZIP III factor PHABULOSA (BcPHB), combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and selective sweep analysis in Brassica campestris. We found that promoter variation defines two major haplotypes, BcPHBHapI and BcPHBHapII, driving divergent expression levels associated with entire and lobed leaves. Functionally, BcPHB knockdown lines (BcPHBami) exhibited lobed margins, whereas complementation of lobed accessions with the BcPHBHapI promoter partially restored the entire-leaf phenotype. Similarly, overexpression of LATE MERISTEM IDENTITY 1 (BcLMI1), a conserved regulator of leaf lobation, phenocopied the BcPHBami lines. Mechanistically, BcPHB and BcLMI1 form a reciprocal negative feedback loop that stabilizes margin patterning. Furthermore, domestication-driven selection of BcPHBHapI facilitated the transition from ancestral lobed leaves to cultivated entire forms. This study reveals a pivotal developmental module and illustrates how regulatory evolution drives morphological diversification in crops.

title: Routine laboratory data are decoupled from symptom phenotype and prognosis in Long COVID: within-cohort variation is dominated by age
Dominant Source Identification in the Propagation of Ocean Observation Uncertainty to Underwater Detection Performance: A Differentiable End-To-End Framework
abstract: Underwater detection performance is constrained by ocean observation uncertainties that propagate nonlinearly through sound speed profile (SSP) inversion, acoustic transmission-loss (TL) prediction, and sonar performance estimation. We develop a differentiable end-to-end framework that traces observation uncertainty through SSP inversion, acoustic propagation, and passive sonar detection probability (Pd), enabling a quantitative ranking of the dominant uncertainty sources. The framework comprises a Bayesian deep ensemble for SSP inversion, a physics-constrained Fourier neural operator for acoustic propagation, and an analytic sonar-equation module, all implemented in PyTorch with automatic differentiation. Applied to the eddy-active northern South China Sea using the SCSORA reanalysis and validated against independent glider observations, bias-corrected Sobol' first-order indices show that satellite SST observation uncertainty dominates detection-performance uncertainty in deep water (S1 ≈ 0.38–0.52, conditional on the upper-200 m water column), exceeding the acoustic model structural error (S1 ≈ 0.10–0.19). The ranking is robust to a factor-of-two variation in the assigned acoustic structural-error variance and to the choice of attribution scheme (Sobol' vs. Shapley). A paired bootstrap test of a cross-training experiment indicates a small but significant sensitivity of the SST index to the training configuration (ΔS1 = 0.052; 95% CI [0.018, 0.086]), which does not alter the qualitative ranking. In shallow-shelf environments, seabed geoacoustic uncertainty prevails (S1 ≈ 0.41). The framework operates entirely on publicly available data and provides a quantitative basis for prioritizing environmental-observation resources in naval environmental support. Limitations include the absence of independent winter glider observations and the use of a 200-m SSP truncation in deep-water regimes; both are discussed in the paper.

title: Deep Learning–Based Rapid Prediction and Optimization of Outdoor Wind Environment for Campus Buildings
abstract: Courtyard-style campus buildings often suffer from poor outdoor wind environments affecting pedestrian comfort. This study proposes a deep learning-based rapid prediction and optimization framework to bypass the computational expense of traditional numerical simulations. A parametric dataset of 216 pedestrian-level wind fields is constructed via CFD simulations, varying building width-to-height ratio and wind incidence angle. A pix2pix conditional generative adversarial network is trained as a surrogate model to learn the direct mapping from building geometry to wind speed distribution. Unlike conventional regression networks that produce over-smoothing, the adversarial training preserves sharp velocity gradients and local extremes—features critical for comfort assessment. The model achieves a single-case inference time of 1.4 seconds. Results reveal that summer comfort coverage reaches 98.4%, while winter coverage drops sharply to 19.5%, identifying winter as the critical season for intervention. Parametric analysis shows that wind incidence angle exerts a pronounced effect: comfort area increases from 12.9% at perpendicular incidence to 24.1% at 45°. The optimal design is W/H = 1.4 and θ = 45°. The framework has been implemented as a prototype software system. This study provides a valuable reference for climate-adaptive design of campus courtyard buildings.

title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
abstract: I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.

title: EthnoPulse: A Multi-Task Deep Learning Framework for Traditional Music Emotion Recognition and Online Engagement Prediction
abstract: Traditional-music emotion recognition and online engagement are usually studied separately, although both depend partly on acoustic structure. EthnoPulse formulates the two problems as a partial-label multi-task setting in which disjoint affect and engagement corpora can share an encoder without imputing missing labels. The model combines dual-resolution log-Mel inputs, a multi-scale residual encoder, squeeze-and-excitation recalibration, task-specific gates, uncertainty weighting, an emotion–valence/arousal consistency term, and CORAL alignment. CTIM and FMA define the raw-audio tasks, with composition-and artist-disjoint splits used to reduce identity leakage. CCMED and WCMED provide an independent feature-level test of the evaluation protocol. Under composition-grouped five-fold validation, the lowest arousal MAEs are 0.286 on CCMED and 0.282 on WCMED, and the strongest rank correlations are 0.773 and 0.806, respectively. Random excerpt splitting raises CCMED valence correlation from 0.318 to 0.527. Cross-domain arousal transfer reaches ρ = 0.808, whereas valence transfer is weaker and the effect of CORAL depends on both direction and target. The results underline the importance of group-disjoint evaluation and dimension-specific reporting in cross-cultural music analysis.

title: Mathematical modelling of sequential DRM and catalyst regeneration in a fixed-bed reactor
abstract: Dry reforming of methane is an attractive route for syngas production because it enables the simultaneous utilisation of methane and carbon dioxide. However, its practical application is limited by high energy demand, catalyst deactivation and, in particular, carbon deposition on the catalyst surface. In this work, a mathematical model of sequential dry reforming of methane and CO2-assisted catalyst regeneration in a fixed-bed reactor is proposed. The carbon formed during the reforming stage is treated not only as a deactivating deposit, but also as a reactive intermediate that can be converted into carbon monoxide during the subsequent regeneration step. The axial distribution of carbon obtained from the DRM model is used as the initial condition for the transient regeneration model. To avoid dependence of the total carbon mass on the spatial discretisation adopted for regeneration, the carbon distribution from the DRM stage is recalculated into the mass of carbon assigned to reactor intervals ΔmC, and then transferred to the regeneration grid using a local linear carbon-mass density reconstructed by cubic spline interpolation and integrated numerically over the new grid intervals. The regeneration model describes transient changes in CO2 and CO concentrations and in the local mass of deposited carbon along the reactor. A thermodynamic constraint based on the reaction quotient and the equilibrium constant of the reverse Boudouard reaction is introduced to limit carbon gasification to conditions favourable for CO formation. The resulting system ofmequations is solved numerically using the method of lines and a stiff ODE solver. The influence of spatial grid discretisation is analysed, and a discretisation level is selected to strike a balance between numerical accuracy and computational cost. Regeneration simulations are performed over a temperature range of 973 to 1270 K. The results show that the proposed model enables the local course of catalyst regeneration to be followed, preserves the carbon mass balance when the regeneration grid is changed, and provides a basis for assessing CO2-assisted regeneration as part of cyclic DRM–regeneration operation.
journal: Chemical and Process Engineering: New Frontiers

title: Semiempirical Quantum Chemistry in the Age of ab initio Data and Differentiable Programming: II. Parameter Optimization
abstract: Semiempirical quantum chemistry (SQC) represents an invaluable asset in the toolbox of molecular and materials modeling. Thanks to their explicit quantum-mechanical treatment of electrons, they allow to capture an array of local and non-local interaction mechanisms and offers access to electronic structure properties, which can be of crucial importance in order to better understand and design molecular systems and materials. In a previous publication, we presented our recent advances within the PySEQM package, enabling rapid gradient evaluations for SQC parameters and thus developing an efficient and reliable back-end for SQC parametrizations. In this work, we detail our implementation of this parametrization procedure, SQCFit, and its features. Offering a high degree of automation, SQCFit implements a suite of tailor-made tools for the optimization of SQC parameters. Specifically, we present local versus global parametrization schemes, the use of train-validation splits and early stopping to avoid overfitting, and advanced scoring/loss functions including appropriately standardized quantitative error measures as well as more qualitative measures such as the performance in ranking candidate systems according to a given molecular property. Based on a set of test applications, we highlight how SQCFit allows to obtain performant parametrizations tailor-made for the modern use cases of SQC.

title: Semiempirical Quantum Chemistry in the Age of ab initio Data and Differentiable Programming: III. Differentiable Complete Active Space Configuration Interaction
abstract: We present an efficient, differentiable complete-active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) framework for GPU-accelerated electronic-structure calculations. The approach is integrated into the PyTorch-based PYSEQM package together with orthogonalization-corrected OM2 and OM3 semiempirical Hamiltonians and floating-occupation molecular orbitals. By combining determinant-based direct CI with matrix-free eigensolution and custom reverse-mode differentiation, the method retains the memory efficiency of the forward calculation while providing derivatives with respect to continuous model parameters and molecular coordinates. Its modular formulation separates the CASCI treatment from the underlying one-and two-electron quantities, facilitating use with different electronic-structure backends. The resulting framework provides state energies, density and transition density matrices, transition properties, and analytic response information for multiconfigurational electronic states. In combination with semiempirical effective Hamiltonians, it offers a computationally economical route to differentiable multireference electronic structure for bondbreaking processes and electronically excited systems. We illustrate this formalism studying minimum-energy conical intersections, solvent effects on the intersection seam energetics, and a proof-of-concept inverse design problem of excitation energies in an external electric field.

title: INTEGRATED HYDROLOGICAL ASSESSMENT FOR THE DESIGN OF A MULTIPURPOSE SMALL RESERVOIR IN THE SIRBA RIVER BASIN, NIGER
abstract: Water scarcity and increasing hydroclimatic variability represent major constraints to sustainable development in the Sahel, where rural livelihoods depend largely on rain-fed agriculture and seasonal water availability. In southwestern Niger, the Sirba River watershed experiences recurrent floods during the rainy season and severe water shortages during the prolonged dry season, highlighting the need for efficient water storage infrastructures. This study assessed the hydrological feasibility of constructing a multipurpose small dam in the Sirba River watershed using an integrated hydrological and geomorphological approach. Long-term rainfall and hydrological data (1960-2020), a 30-m Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and regional empirical hydrological methods (ORSTOM, CIEH and Gradex) were employed to characterize the watershed, estimate design floods and evaluate the reservoir water balance. Rainfall frequency analysis using the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution indicated design rainfall depths ranging from 210 mm for the 5-year return period to 289 mm for the 100-year return period. Morphometric analysis showed that the watershed covers 39091 km², with an elongated geometry (Gravelius coefficient = 2.04) and a low drainage density (0.06 km km⁻²), characteristics that contribute to moderate flood concentration. The estimated 10-year design flood reached 100.04 m³ s⁻¹, while the mean annual runoff volume was estimated at 86.12 × 10⁶ m³, decreasing to 40.36.10⁶ m³ under 10-year dry conditions. Although evaporation and sedimentation constitute the principal water losses, the reservoir water balance remained positive under average hydrological conditions, indicating sufficient water availability to satisfy projected domestic, livestock and agricultural demands. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed small dam is hydrologically feasible and could significantly enhance water security, support irrigated agriculture, reduce flood risks and strengthen climate resilience in the Sirba River watershed. Future studies should incorporate physically based hydrological modelling, sediment yield assessment and climate change scenarios to optimize reservoir design and long-term operation.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Integrated Electrochemical Process Modelling and Techno-Economic Assessment of Micro-Mesh Alkaline Seawater Electrolysis for Green Hydrogen Production
abstract: This study couples an experimentally calibrated electrochemical model with a techno-economic assessment of expanded nickel micro-mesh electrodes for alkaline electrolysis of seawater (M-SWELT). A zero-gap cell model with explicit thermodynamic, kinetic, bubble and ohmic terms is anchored to commercial alkaline performance, checked against published resistance measurements and calibrated to a like-for-like two-electrode comparison of micro-mesh and woven Ni-mesh cells in natural seawater with 5 M KOH. Because one operating point cannot separate kinetic from resistive contributions, the transferred voltage saving at 0.4 A cm⁻² and 80 °C is bounded at 20–187 mV (central 89 mV). The model is coupled to two seawater feed routes, reverse-osmosis (RO) desalination and direct feed with softening and a chloride bleed, and to a cost model of a 10 MW plant. The RO-fed micro-mesh plant reaches a levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of £4.35 kg⁻¹, against £4.51 kg⁻¹ with woven mesh, and the micro-mesh breaks even at an electrode premium of up to £950 m⁻² (range £217–1,985 m⁻²). Even without chloride oxidation and with electrodes that last as long as the stacks, direct feed costs £4.95 kg⁻¹, because the chloride bleed discards KOH and forces a dilute electrolyte; crediting the chloride’s conductivity narrows the gap to RO feed without closing it, and short electrode life widens it. Across 10,000 Latin-hypercube Monte Carlo samples, the RO-fed micro-mesh plant averages £4.72 kg⁻¹ (P5–P95 £3.95–5.59 kg⁻¹); it is cheaper than woven mesh at equal electrode cost, and direct feed is dearer than RO feed, in every sample.

title: Benchmarking time-series foundation models for multitask predictive maintenance in digital twins
abstract: Digital twins provide a comprehensive virtual representation of physical assets, distinguishing themselves from traditional control systems through long-term diagnostic and prognostic capabilities. However, current digital twin architectures face a critical scalability barrier: they rely on dedicated, single-purpose models for every distinct query, task, physical scale, and operating context, resulting in unsustainable engineering overhead. To address this limitation, there is an urgent need for flexible, general-purpose analytical backbones capable of interpreting diverse time-series data without constant reconfiguration. While time-series foundation models (TSFMs) offer a potential solution through large-scale pre-training, their capacity to generalize beyond forecasting to the complex, multi-objective downstream requirements remains largely unverified. Addressing this challenge, this study utilizes the Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) dataset to benchmark three representative multi-task TSFMs (MOMENT, UniTS, and FFTS) across four downstream tasks (imputation, anomaly detection, classification, and regression) within a predictive maintenance context. We frame this evaluation as a rigorous test of generalization, assessing whether architecturally distinct TSFMs can adapt to distinct downstream tasks such as regression for remaining useful life estimation. Our benchmark reveals that although TSFMs generalize across all evaluated tasks, they do not yet match specialized baselines trained only on the C-MAPSS dataset. We further find that the three backbones separate most clearly when adaptation is restricted to a small set of parameters, where the model combining channel-mixing with explicit task tokens adapts best to multi-objective use, including regression, a task absent from all three pre-training objectives; in the zero-shot regime no single backbone leads across tasks. Because the models differ simultaneously in architecture, capacity, pre-training corpus, and patch size, we report these as patterns observed under one shared benchmarking framework rather than as isolated causes. The evaluation is conducted on raw sensor series alone, without the semantic or physics-based components of a mature digital twin, so these findings provide an empirical baseline for the analytical layer such a system would host rather than an evaluation of digital twin integration itself.

title: PySkyLumos: A Python-Based Polarized Skylight Simulator
abstract: This paper presents PySkyLumos, an open-source Python framework for simulating skylight polarization measurements and metadata. It implements the Rayleigh, Berry, and Pan models, covering single scattering, the splitting of the neutral points caused by multiple scattering, and the elevation-dependent motion of these points. Benchmarks show a fivefold overall speed-up and up to two orders of magnitude faster Stokes-parameter image formation than a recent open-source simulator. Validation against real polarization-camera images shows close agreement between the simulated and measured polarization patterns, supporting its use in algorithm development for bio-inspired computer vision, navigation, robotics, and sensing.

title: Dual-Domain Fusion for Small-Object SAR Ship Detection in Complex Scenes
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection is essential for maritime surveillance, yet coherent speckle can obscure tiny offshore vessels, while high-response coastal structures can produce target-like responses. Repeated downsampling further weakens sparse vessel signatures, whereas a separate high-resolution prediction head increases dense prediction costs. We propose a dual-domain detector that embeds spatial–frequency encoding, multiscale refinement, and high-resolution feature transfer within the backbone–neck–pyramid representation. Scharr-derived boundary cues are coupled with learned frequency context and remain discriminative as features are fused across scales, while sample-preserving space-to-depth transformation and global–local receptive-field modeling integrate shallow detail into semantically stronger P3 features without introducing a separate P2 prediction head. Coordinated FSEM, MSFE, and SOEP modules preserve fine vessel structure and reduce clutter-induced ambiguity throughout the detection hierarchy. Experiments on SSDD, HRSID, and RSDD-SAR evaluate detection accuracy, cross-dataset transfer, limited-data behavior, sensitivity to controlled perturbations, and edge deployment. Across 30 seed-matched SSDD runs, the method improves mAP50:95 over the baseline by 2.70±0.34 percentage points. It achieves 69.3% and 71.5% mAP50:95 on HRSID and RSDD. On the Atlas 200I platform, the compiled FP16 model retains 69.3% mAP50:95 while running at 101.8 frames/s.

title: A comparative review of machine learning models and deep learning architectures for pregnancy progression prediction
abstract: Monitoring the course of pregnancy is of paramount importance, enabling the identification of negative outcomes and clinically significant changes. Although parity status may contribute to information needs, status as first-time mothers is not considered as a causal determinant. This paper presents a structured scoping review comparing conventional and deep learning approaches to pregnancy-related prediction tasks. The reviewed machine learning models include logistic regression; random forest; Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost); Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and their gated variants, long short-term memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs); Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs); transformers; and hybrid architectures. The analysis employs six dimensions: performance; ability to encode temporal data; model interpretability; data requirements for training; computational costs; and clinical relevance. As primary studies report outcome-specific performance results, the findings are presented across outcome domains rather than aggregated rankings of model architectures. In a study on predicting preterm-birth outcomes, a transformer achieved a test-set Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) of 0.792, compared to 0.78 for logistic regression, 0.751 for random forest, and 0.717 for a Support Vector Machine (SVM). In predicting preeclampsia, a CNN achieved an AUC of 0.85 on holdout validation and 0.81 on an external test set, with an AUC of 0.98 for early-onset preeclampsia. CTGFusionNet, which employs a hybrid architecture of convolutional, recurrent, and attention layers applied to Cardiotocography (CTG) and clinical records, reported 97.85% accuracy for the task of fetal-distress classification. The findings highlight the complementary strengths and weaknesses of conventional and deep learning models for the analyzed tasks. The choice of an architecture should be informed by the target outcome, data type, volume, and quality, calibration and validation strategies, requirements for interpretability and fairness, and computational costs rather than a singular emphasis on performance.

title: Non-contact lens metrology from optical flow and differentiable ray tracing
abstract: Accurate lens surface metrology is essential to determine the manufactured geometry of refractive optical elements and their deviation from the specified design. We demonstrate a transmission metrology method that reconstructs refractive lens surfaces from the displacement of a wavelet-noise-patterned mask. Lens-induced distortion is represented by a dense displacement field. A differentiable ray tracer fits the lens geometry using a calibrated near-telecentric camera model with an effective finite ray origin. We validate the method on commercial lenses. The recovered geometries agree with nominal specifications, and the plano-aspheric reconstruction is compared with chromatic confocal profilometry.

title: Discovery or Memorization? A Faithful Benchmark for Real-World Business-Logic Vulnerability Discovery
abstract: The rapid advancement of cybersecurity agents in vulnerability discovery has increased the need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities accurately. However, synthetic benchmarks lack realism, real-life benchmarks are prone to contamination, and many existing benchmarks have already been saturated by current models. We therefore set out to develop a benchmark that is realistic, reproducible, resistant to contamination, and challenging. Our key insight is that real-life business-logic vulnerabilities are subtle and exercise complex application interactions, making them naturally demanding. The difficulty lies in specifying evaluation criteria precise enough to faithfully measure model capabilities while keeping the tasks free of data-leakage. We introduce AnonVul, a cross-language benchmark of 132 application-level business-logic vulnerabilities, built by a semi-automated pipeline that anonymizes each task, injects oracles from expert-written specifications, and differentially verifies proof-of-concept exploits. The benchmark spans nine languages, with two evaluation tracks on black-box and grey-box settings, where each task runs in a sandbox with specialized oracles embedded in key exploitation steps. We evaluate six state-of-the-art vulnerability-discovery agents on the AnonVul benchmark, measuring discovery success, cost-effectiveness, anonymization sensitivity, oracle validity, and failure modes. Our results show that AnonVul remains challenging, with the best agent succeeding in only 23.11% of attempts. On a matched cohort of 20 vulnerabilities, restoring software identity increases discovery from 21.25% to 40.83%, highlighting the importance of controlling recognizable software knowledge when evaluating vulnerability discovery.

title: Sulphur-bearing molecule survey towards prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus molecular cloud
abstract: Sulphur is drastically depleted from the gas phase in dense starless and prestellar cores, creating the long-standing "missing sulphur problem". Observations of sulphur-bearing molecules are crucial to understanding sulphur chemistry, core-environment relationships, and the physical evolution of star-forming regions. We present a survey of four sulphur-bearing molecules, HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO, towards 15 starless and prestellar cores in the Perseus molecular cloud using the Yebes 40m telescope. The HCS+ 1-0, OCS 3-2 and 4-3, H2CS 1_{0,1}-0_{0,0}, and SO 3_2-2_2 transitions were observed, fitted with Gaussian profiles, and column densities were calculated assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). We also compare these with observations of CS, CCS, and CCCS from a previous study. HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO are detected in 100%, 93%, 100%, and 73% of the sample, respectively. Derived column densities are (2.2-17.0)x10^11 cm^-2 for HCS+, (1.9-25.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for OCS, (1.0-15.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for H2CS, and (0.3-17.0)x10^13 cm^-2 for SO, spanning over an order of magnitude. HCS+ and SO abundances strongly correlate (inversely and directly, respectively) with core volume density, reinforcing their early- and late-type status. Correlations indicate a differentiation between carbon and oxygen chemistry for sulphur-bearing molecules, with CS showing the strongest correlations as expected. Cores in protostellar outflow paths do not show consistently higher abundances. The chemical age (SO/CS) correlates with physical age (volume density), except for Per752, an outlier likely linked to an enhanced cosmic ray ionization rate. These results provide a robust observational baseline constraining chemical models of sulphur chemistry in early star formation.

title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.

title: Smartphone-Based, Field-Deployed AI Inspection System for Power Distribution Infrastructure
abstract: Routine inspection of power distribution infrastructure remains challenging for utilities operating geographically dispersed networks, where conventional manual inspection can be difficult to perform consistently and at scale. This work presents a smartphone-based AI inspection system for assessing targeted distribution-infrastructure conditions from images captured by field personnel. The proposed workflow integrates image-quality and viewing-perspective validation with AI-assisted assessment of pole lean, crossarm and top-cleat tilt, voltage level, vegetation-clearance risk, and distribution-transformer (DTR)-ground clearance. The system integrates deep-learning models with monocular depth estimation, geometric analysis, and rule-based processing within a common multi-stage inspection workflow designed for practical field operation. The system was pilot deployed across five selected distribution feeders within the Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Ltd. (APEPDCL), where 1,222 defect instances were identified across the assessed categories and subsequently tracked through a rectification and verification workflow, with 84 defect instances recorded as rectified during the study period. Feeder-level interruption records were also examined over the study period; however, the available observations do not provide sufficient evidence to establish a reliability improvement attributable to the proposed system. A curated multi-module field-captured dataset, PD-Defect, is also publicly released to support reproducible research in distribution-infrastructure inspection. The field deployment demonstrates the practical integration of smartphone-based AI-assisted inspection into field inspection and maintenance activities, providing a mechanism for systematic identification, documentation, rectification tracking, and verification of targeted distribution-infrastructure defects.
