Deep-learning for improving prognostication and therapy prediction in breast cancer
abstract:
Treatment decisions in early breast cancer depend on accurate prognostication and on therapy-relevant biomarkers, both of which rely largely on examination of routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. Manual assessment, however, is subject to observer variability and cannot exhaustively quantify tissue features or detect complex morphological associations. Advances in artificial intelligence have therefore prompted the development of computational tools that extract additional information from routine sections. This thesis investigates whether deep learning applied to H&E whole-slide images (WSIs) can improve prognostication beyond established clinicopathological factors and enable inference of therapy-relevant biomarkers in breast cancer. Four studies are presented, addressing (i) the design of a general modeling framework, (ii) the interchangeability of models for assessing an immune biomarker (i.e., tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes), (iii) the inference of molecular alteration from morphology, and (iv) the direct modeling of patient survival.

In the first study, we developed a model-agnostic, multiresolution multiple-instance learning (MIL) framework for WSI analysis, that aggregates features across magnifications independently of the underlying encoder or classifier. Nine MIL models were evaluated with both a domain-specific and an ImageNet-pretrained feature encoder on grade, TP53 mutation status, and survival prediction. Aggregating high- and low-magnification features by concatenation or a learnable linear transformation consistently outperformed single-resolution baselines across models and tasks, indicating that multiresolution representation is broadly beneficial rather than tied to a particular architecture.

The second study examined whether independently developed models for automated tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) scoring can be used interchangeably in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Ten machine-learning and deep-learning approaches were compared against pathologist-read stromal TILs for analytical and prognostic validity. Agreement with pathologist scoring varied across models and declined from internal to external validation. Despite this variability, eight of ten models retained significant and overlapping prognostic associations. The findings indicate that model choice affects the scores themselves, cautioning against treating such models as interchangeable in the absence of a common benchmark.

In the third study, we developed a model to infer TP53 mutation status directly from H&E WSIs, with the aim of providing a histology-based surrogate marker with prognostic value. On a held-out test set, the model discriminated mutated from wild-type tumors with an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.88), while in an independent, endocrine-treated ER+ cohort, the image-derived score was associated with overall survival (HRadj = 3.88, 95% CI 1.37-10.99; p=0.011). The results provide proof-of-concept for a histology-based TP53 marker that carries independent prognostic information.

Building on the third study, the fourth study modeled overall survival directly from H&E WSIs, rather than through a molecular proxy. After adjustment for established prognostic factors, the resulting risk score stratified patients into high- and low- risk groups in the internal test set (adjusted HR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.09-4.33; p = 0.028) and in two external cohorts: Stockholm (adjusted HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.23-2.62; p = 0.003) and PANTHER (adjusted HR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.22-2.32; p = 0.001). The score also retained prognostic value in the ER+/HER2-subgroup and for recurrence endpoints. These findings suggest that a survival-trained H&E biomarker can provide risk stratification beyond established clinicopathological factors.

Taken together, these studies show that deep learning applied to routine H&E WSIs can recover prognostic and molecular information relevant to breast cancer, and they address this question at several levels, from framework-level design choices to task-specific biomarkers. They also identify methodological factors that condition the reliability of such models. The clinical role of these approaches, including any bearing on therapy selection, remains to be established through head-to-head comparison with existing tools and prospective validation.

Equivalence of measurement properties of the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) across 13 European countries
abstract: The Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) is the most widely used tool to measure burden of skin diseases and assess intervention effectiveness. It is embedded in national guidelines and disease registries in > 45 countries and available in > 138 translations. This study examined psychometric properties of the DLQI across 13 European languages. 3,408 patients had completed the DLQI questionnaire with no missing data. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was performed using datasets of each country and multigroup CFA (MGCFA) across all countries. Known-group analysis was performed of DLQI sum-score against physician-assessed severity by country. All countries’ DLQI data showed essential unidimensionality with good fits to a 1-factor CFA model with CFI, TLI unscaled values all > 0.97 (COSMIN criteria). MGCFA indicated different country translations of the DLQI conceptualize the same construct and showed equality of factor loadings. Although, scalar invariance was not seen, meaning that direct comparison of mean DLQI scores across 12 countries is not supported by the current results, partial scalar invariance was achieved after constraining one threshold for DLQI item 7. Known-group analysis of DLQI versus disease severity was significant for every country (all p < 0.025). Good psychometric properties were present across all 13 languages examined with essential unidimensionality confirmed. The DLQI differentiated between levels of disease severity and EQ-5D-3 L levels across all these languages. This adds further confidence in the appropriateness of using the DLQI with this range of languages.

title: A systematic mapping of goal-oriented requirements engineering: reflections, impact, and the way forward
abstract: Goal-oriented Requirements Engineering describes the body of work which focuses on goals as the driving force motivating and capturing requirements, often using graphical goal models. A proliferation of work in this area inspired the study: “Goal-oriented requirements engineering: an extended systematic mapping study” first available in 2017, covering 246 publications in GORE up to 2015. In the current article, we have the pleasure of reflecting on this original mapping study. Using bibliometrics, we examine the study’s visibility, although such a quantitative view gives us only an approximation of real impact. The bibliometric view shows us that most citations are relatively recent: 85% of the citations have occurred since 2020. Unsurprisingly, the work has primarily been cited in requirements engineering venues, but also related venues such as the Conceptual Modeling conference (ER) and the Information and Software Technology Journal (IST). The work has been cited by a wide variety of authors. We estimate that roughly 40% of the publications citing the original SLR actually focus on goal models (have some variant of “goal” in the title), but that only roughly 53% of citing papers which are not themselves systematic reviews emphasize some form of empirical evaluation, 10% lower than the presence of empirical studies found in the original mapping study. Turning to trends and future directions, we reflect on the limitations of GORE uptake in industry, along with recommendations for continued use in education. We highlight new developments in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate goal models, including limitations, and reflect on what opportunities may be lost via full automation of goal model generation. We reflect on the potential role of GORE in the rising field of intent-driven engineering with AI, and the disconnect between much of this work and requirements-focused goal-oriented foundations. Finally, we consider the rising popularity of agentic AI, describing conceptual challenges and opportunities for GORE in terms of monitoring, capturing, and driving agentic system design. Overall, our reflection emphasizes that in the rise of LLMs and Agentic AI, the expressive power of GORE has great potential, and we invite the research community to explore and harness goal modeling for this purpose.

A multitask tamil speech framework for ASR, TTS, and intelligent conversational agents
Context aware multimodal plant disease diagnosis using agro ecological metadata and explainable inference
abstract: Plant disease detection is a major aspect of precision agriculture, directly impacting crop productivity and food security. Recent deep learning approaches have achieved high accuracy in disease classification from images, but most rely heavily on visual features and remain ill-posed to general changes in illumination, background complexity, image quality, and field conditions. They also have limited agro-ecological information and insufficient interpretability, limiting their practical reliability and users’ trust. This study proposes to overcome these drawbacks by leveraging a multimodal deep learning framework, ContextLeafXAI, inspired by LeafContextReasonNet. The framework considers visual phenotypic aspects alongside agro-ecological information (weather, soil, and geographical information). The proposed reliability-aware gated fusion mechanism adaptively combines information from various sources, and the dual-level explainability strategy, using Grad-CAM and contextual feature attribution, guides lesion localisation and understanding of the role of the environment. Experimental results demonstrate that ContextLeafXAI attains 96.2% accuracy, 95.2% Macro-F1 score, and 0.98 ROC-AUC, which is superior to the unimodal and multimodal baselines evaluated. The framework also shows good cross-dataset generalisation, explanation consistency and moderate computational load. The results suggest that ContextLeafXAI offers a powerful and understandable decision-support solution for plant disease diagnostics across various agricultural scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/zakeeya12/ContextLeafXAI_Full_Implementation. Not applicable.

title: Challenges in Accommodating Talker Variability in Lexical Tone Perception Among Autistic Adults: Implications for Talker Adaptation.
abstract: PURPOSE Successful speech perception requires listeners to accommodate acoustic variability arising both across talkers and within a single talker. This challenge is especially pronounced in tone languages, where fundamental frequency (F0) simultaneously encodes lexical meaning and talker identity. The present study investigated how between-talker and within-talker variability affects lexical tone perception in Cantonese-speaking adults with and without autism spectrum disorder (ASD). METHODS Twenty-five adults with ASD and 25 neurotypical (NT) controls completed a speeded word identification task involving minimal word pairs differentiated by level tones. Between-talker variability was manipulated by presenting words produced by either a single talker or multiple talkers, and within-talker variability was manipulated by using either a single exemplar or multiple exemplars from each talker. Performance was assessed using identification accuracy, response time (RT), and a composite efficiency measure. RESULTS Both groups demonstrated reliable processing costs associated with between-talker variability, reflected in lower accuracy, longer RTs, and reduced efficiency, with no group difference in the magnitude of this effect. In contrast, only the ASD group exhibited reduced efficiency under within-talker variability. Furthermore, within-talker and between-talker processing costs were not significantly correlated in either group. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that autistic adults may experience greater difficulty accommodating subtle within-talker acoustic variability during lexical tone perception, consistent with a more detail-focused processing style. Such difficulty may have implications for everyday speech understanding in socially diverse listening environments while highlighting the importance of distinguishing between-talker normalization from within-talker stabilization in models of speech perception.
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: 3D modeling for crop applications in precision agriculture: a review
abstract: Background Advances in data acquisition and information processing have strengthened the role of precision agriculture (PA) in enhancing agricultural productivity and sustainability. Among emerging technologies, 3D crop modeling offers detailed representations of agricultural scenes, supports crop phenotyping, and enables autonomous operations such as harvesting, fertilization, and pruning. However, despite the rapid development of hardware and software for 3D modeling, a comprehensive synthesis of the available approaches and their applications in PA remains limited. Purpose This review aims to examine the broad range of 3D modeling approaches used in PA, focusing on their methodological characteristics, practical applications, advantages, and limitations to support the selection of suitable solutions for different agricultural requirements. Methods A total of 168 publications, identified through a Scopus literature search covering studies published up to March 2026, were reviewed. The analysis examines 3D data types and sensing technologies, sensor platforms and application environments, and data processing methods, including data registration techniques and methods for insight extraction. Applications of 3D models to agricultural crops were also analyzed and classified into three main categories: crop phenotyping, machinery navigation, and field operations. Conclusions The review highlights the widespread adoption of LiDAR, RGB, and RGB-D sensors deployed on Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles, Uncrewed Ground Vehicles, and robotic platforms, alongside increasing use of AI-based processing methods. Challenges related to sensor robustness, multisensor interoperability, and large 3D datasets remain. Future research should focus on overcoming these limitations to facilitate the transition towards reliable, large-scale implementation of 3D modeling technologies in practical agricultural operations.

Acute Ultra Low Dose THC Attenuates Anxiety-Like Behavior in a Mouse Model for Major-Depressive Disorder
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent psychiatric disorder, and is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments for MDD entail many side effects, and include a lag until the onset of therapeutic effects. The current hypotheses as for the etiology of MDD revolve around the monoamine hypothesis and the plasticity and neurodegeneration hypothesis. According to the latter, employing a neuroprotective treatment may help ameliorate depressive symptoms. Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is the primary psychoactive component of the cannabis sativa plant. THC interacts with the endocannabinoid system, which was shown to be involved in the regulation of emotional states (e.g. anxiety) and stress through modulation of synaptic plasticity. Here, we show the potential of acute, ultra-low dose (0.002 mg/kg) THC in ameliorating anxious behavior in a chronic mild stress mouse model for MDD. We utilize next generation sequencing techniques to show the treatment’s effect on neuronal differentiation and synaptic plasticity-related mRNAs, and specify Elmo domain containing 1 (Elmod1) as a molecular mediator of the observed anxiolytic effects. Moreover, we show the involvement of glucocorticoids-related mRNAs in the observed anxiolytic effect of acute, ultra-low dose THC.

title: Enhanced crop yield estimation in smart agriculture via AI and IoT using the GODL geo-optimized algorithm
abstract: Precision agriculture is one of the major breakthroughs which has been adopted to counteract some of the major challenges facing contemporary agriculture, such as maximizing crop yield, maximizing resource efficiency, and sustainability. The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) technologies can go a long way in enhancing crop yield prediction through data obtained from multiple sources, including satellite images, ground sensors, and weather stations. This research paper proposes a next-generation crop yield prediction system called Geo-Optimized Deep Learning (GODL) algorithm. The GODL algorithm integrates geospatial information with deep learning algorithms for crop yield analysis and prediction. This combination of deep learning and geospatial data allows accurate and scalable crop yield predictions using geospatial and sensor information. In order to ensure model optimization in terms of accuracy and efficiency, the GODL Algorithm makes use of advanced hyperparameter optimization methods that include Adam and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). The research paper highlights the efficiency of the GODL Algorithm by conducting extensive experiments that compare the algorithm’s performance with other crop yield prediction models like Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and other machine learning techniques. The evaluation takes into consideration important metrics such as accuracy, Jaccard Index, Fowlkes-Mallows Index (FMI), and G-mean, as well as IoT data delay and its effects on the prediction accuracy. In future research, the use of blockchain technology to facilitate data sharing and edge computing to process the data will be considered.

title: Externalizing Epistemic Governance from Stateless Clinical LLMs: Why It Is Necessary and Why It Must Be Constrained
abstract: Large language models are increasingly embedded in clinical decision support, but they are stateless. They preserve no epistemic commitments across contexts, identical cases can yield divergent outputs, and fluent generation can acquire de facto authority over what counts as evidence without any matching structure of responsibility. We argue that whether clinical AI can be trusted and held accountable depends on where epistemic authority sits and who governs it, not on how well the model performs or how fluently it generates. From this it follows that epistemic governance has to be externalized from the model. It also has to be constrained, because relocating authority into a second generative layer reproduces the original problem. We make the claim concrete with a non-agentic, constraint-based architecture, instantiated in oncology. Context classification, evidence authority, and truth-state assignment are settled by dedicated, inspectable layers before any generation occurs; the language model is confined to bounded extraction and summarization. The central move is to keep deontic authority, what is permitted and reimbursed, distinct from epistemic authority, what the evidence supports, so that a reimbursement or jurisdictional constraint is represented as an allocation decision rather than collapsed into an apparent clinical fact. Uncertainty, disagreement between authoritative sources, and clinician overrides are preserved as explicit, inspectable states. By settling authority before generation and keeping it inspectable, the architecture restores the structure of responsibility that fluent generation erodes: the exercise of authority becomes attributable, and the resulting recommendation can be contested rather than absorbed as plain clinical fact.

title: Conceptualising Health Economic Models Using a Graph Retrieval-Augmented, Agentic AI Framework with Human-in-the-Loop Validation: Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Health economic models (HEMs) are crucial for assessing the cost-effectiveness of healthcare interventions, informing policy decisions and guiding reimbursement strategies. This study examines the feasibility of employing generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) for the conceptualisation of HEMs. Two proof-of-concept studies were conducted, implementing a first-of-its-kind agentic Gen-AI-augmented approach for model conceptualisation. METHODS An agentic Gen-AI framework was developed, incorporating the chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning algorithm through advanced prompt engineering, compounded with self-consistency, executed in an external Python programming environment. Within this framework, an agentic execution layer (the 'agent') autonomously orchestrated a multi-step retrieval-reasoning-generation task. Additionally, a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technique was implemented by linking the large language model (LLM) to an external database curated with user-selected data specific to HEM. Two case studies were explored: breast cancer, representing a data-rich disease area, and transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN), exemplifying a data-sparse rare disease. RESULTS The agentic Gen-AI framework successfully generated two key outputs that were subsequently validated against published literature and expert review from health economic (HE) modelers and clinicians: (1) a disease concept diagram illustrating the progression of the disease and its associated health states, and (2) a model structure diagram depicting patient transitions between various health states. CONCLUSIONS The findings suggest that Gen-AI-augmented methodologies can enhance multiple aspects of HEM conceptualisation, including problem definition, disease and treatment effect pathway development, model structure recommendations, and drafting of model specification plans. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to integrate cutting-edge Gen-AI techniques such as human-in-the-loop (HITL), chain of thought-self-consistency (CoT-SC), and graph-based RAG for HEM conceptualisation or broader health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) applications.

title: Evaluating intra-urban thermo-hygrometric variability through in situ observations and MLUCM BEP + BEM: A case study in Lecce (Italy)
abstract: This study evaluates the capability of the MLUCM BEP + BEM to reproduce intra-urban variability of air temperature and relative humidity in Lecce (Italy) during summer 2025. A network of six measurement sites representing contrasting urban morphology, vegetation cover, and land-use conditions was used to characterize the thermo-hygrometric structure of the city and evaluate model performance. Site-specific simulations were driven by identical upper-boundary meteorological forcing, allowing the contribution of the explicit urban representation to spatial variability to be isolated, while ERA5 fields were spatially interpolated to each measurement site. Observations showed warmer and generally drier conditions in more densely urbanized areas and cooler, more humid nocturnal conditions in greener and less compact districts. Although ERA5 generally yielded lower pointwise errors, MLUCM BEP + BEM generated substantially greater site-to-site differentiation. The model reproduced about 18% and 31% of the observed mean intra-urban temperature and relative-humidity ranges, respectively, compared with near-null spatial variability in ERA5. Pairwise analysis further showed a markedly improved representation of maximum-temperature contrasts, although the magnitude of spatial differences, particularly at night, remained underestimated. These results indicate that the main contribution of MLUCM BEP + BEM lies in representing differentiated responses among urban configurations, supporting its application to urban heat exposure, thermal comfort, and climate-adaptation studies.
journal: Bulletin of Atmospheric Science and Technology

title: Spatio-temporal estimation of soil erosion risk in Upper Dir, Eastern Hindu Kush, Pakistan
Global advances in Generative AI for renewable energy and implications for sustainable energy transitions in Africa
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being investigated for renewable-energy forecasting, optimisation, predictive maintenance, synthetic-data generation, and infrastructure planning. This study reviews global advances and critically assesses their implications for Africa's sustainable energy transition. It aims to: (i) map GenAI applications in renewable-energy systems; (ii) distinguish demonstrated results from proposed African opportunities; (iii) evaluate evidence quality, transferability, and deployment feasibility; and (iv) identify context-specific research and policy priorities. A systematic review was reported using PRISMA 2020, with the PRALSMA AI-assisted workflow used to support, but not replace, researcher-led screening and synthesis. OpenAlex records published from 2020 to May 2026 were screened, yielding 75 included studies. Manual analysis was triangulated with ChatGPT Project and NotebookLM, and findings were weighted by methodological quality, evidence maturity, and relevance to African data, grid, infrastructure, institutional, and cost conditions. The corpus remains geographically imbalanced: five of the 75 included studies report an African institutional affiliation (Morocco, Nigeria, and South Africa, with further co-affiliations in Tunisia and Gabon), and most quantitative outcomes still derive from non-African simulations, prototypes, or case studies. Consequently, reported error, cost, emission, and accuracy improvements are treated as source-specific rather than directly transferable African effects. Near-term priorities are controlled pilots of lightweight, explainable, offline-capable decision support and synthetic-data methods; compute-intensive diffusion, agentic, digital-twin, and imitation-learning applications require further validation. GenAI may support African renewable-energy transitions, but benefits depend on local datasets, reliable fallback procedures, lifecycle environmental assessment, workforce capacity, governance, and staged field validation.

title: Explainable deep learning framework for real-time insect pest detection in smart agriculture
abstract: Global losses of crop production due to insect pest infestations are estimated to be around 20–40% annually, which represents one of the highest threats to agricultural productivity, farmer livelihoods and food security. Current manual scouting is labor intensive, subjective and non-scalable, and many automated scouting methods suffer when they come to deal with different field conditions and offer little insight into decision making. To tackle these challenges, this study proposes Crop Protection in Smart Agriculture—Real-time Insect Pest Detection using Continual Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (CPSA-RIPD-CSTGCN), a unified and interpretable deep learning framework that combines the four synergistic components: (i) the Ensemble Transform Schmidt–Kalman Filter (ETSKF) for image preprocessing, including resizing, normalization, and noise suppression; (ii) data augmentation using rotation, flipping, scaling, shearing, and contrast adjustment, which enhances generalization and reduces overfitting; (iii) the Continual Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (CSTGCN) that jointly models the spatial dependency across crop regions and temporal evolution of pest dynamics to achieve robust feature extraction and classification; and (iv) the Revolution Optimization Algorithm (ROA) for hyperparameter optimization of CSTGCN weights to adaptively adjust the network. Further, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization is introduced to give post-hoc explainability as it shows regions that are relevant to the biological process and areas that are affected by pests. This framework was tested on IP102 benchmark dataset with 60%-40%-split train-test with 10 economically important classes of pests with 97% accuracy, 98% precision, 98% recall and 98% F1 score, mean ± 0.32% accuracy, across 5-fold cross validation. Among other baseline models, these results consistently outperform VGG16 (82%), InceptionV3 (85%), MobileNetV2 (87%), DenseNet121 (88%), EfficientNetB0 (89%) and task-specific models like EDCP-DIA-RNN(Early Disease and Crop Pest—Diagnosis/Detection using Image Analysis RNN) (94%), EPCY-TPA-ANN (Efficient Prediction of Crop Yield—Through Parameter Analysis ANN) (91%) and ICPM-ESA-CNN (Interactive Crop and Pest Management Enhanced Soil Analysis CNN) (90%). The results of ablation studies showed the solitary effects of each module of the Ensemble Transform Schmidt–Kalman Filter pre-processing and Revolution Optimization Algorithm optimization, and the confusion matrix analysis demonstrated high per-class reliability and only a small amount of misclassification, implying that the proposed method could be applied to real-time, large-scale smart agriculture deployments.

title: Energy constraints in large scale artificial intelligence and insights from human cognition for efficient large language models
abstract: Large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) systems, especially large language models (LLMs), face growing constraints related to energy use, power delivery, memory traffic, experimentation, and infrastructure capacity. These pressures are often studied separately, which makes it difficult to understand how they interact across the full AI lifecycle. This review develops a cross-layer framework that brings these constraints together and examines whether resource-allocation strategies observed in human cognition can inform more sustainable AI design. We compare human and artificial systems by function rather than anatomy, focusing on how each allocates limited resources to learning, search, memory, external support, optimization, and inference. Using a systematized narrative-review approach, we identified 6284 records, screened 898 at the full-text stage, and selected an initial set of 150 focal studies for detailed synthesis. We organize the evidence into seven interacting regimes covering scaling, experimentation, hardware power limits, data movement, infrastructure, evaluation incentives, and inference allocation. The framework extends Green AI by linking these layers and translating insights from human cognition into testable design hypotheses and measurable evaluation criteria. The strongest near-term opportunities include data selection, energy-aware experimentation, hardware-supported low-precision computation, and demand-adaptive inference. However, most reported gains are based on proxy measures such as operations, memory, latency, or data volume rather than direct end-to-end energy measurements. Near- and in-memory computing show longer-term promise, while retrieval, tool use, distributed experts, and multi-agent systems may shift or increase energy costs through communication and repeated inference. These findings support cross-layer co-design and end-to-end evaluation at matched capability, reliability, latency, and service quality.

title: Integrating human and artificial intelligence for conducting scoping reviews on ecosystem services in mixed forests
abstract: This study proposes and evaluates a methodology for adapting a Large Language Model (LLM) using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to support scientific scoping reviews. As a case study, we focused on mixed-species forest plant functional traits and their influence on ecosystem service provision. The LLM (GPT-4o), implemented via Microsoft Copilot, was adapted using contextual information, a meta-prompt, and a curated knowledge base. The contextual layer consisted of well-established knowledge from reputable authors and publishers, while the knowledge base was constructed from cutting-edge scientific literature retrieved from leading academic databases. By combining AI-based agents specifically designed for scoping review tasks with a human-guided inquiry approach, the methodology produced insightful outputs relevant to identifying effective plant trait combinations. The proposed approach is transferable to other scientific domains. Finally, we emphasize the need for interdisciplinary collaboration to develop accessible, domain-specific AI tools that can effectively support scientific research.

title: Changes in pedestrian and bicyclist crash severity before and after COVID 19 using machine learning models
abstract: Pedestrians and bicyclists are among the most vulnerable road users and account for a substantial share of traffic injuries and fatalities. The COVID 19 pandemic altered mobility patterns and driving behavior, potentially affecting crash severity. This study examines pedestrian and bicyclist crash severity in Florida by comparing 2017–2019 with 2021–2023, excluding 2020 as a transition year. Classification models included LDA, QDA, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost, with severe injury specified as the positive class. Model performance was comparable and modest relative to the majority class baseline, with severe injury recall ranging from 18.6 to 31.0%. A likelihood ratio test rejected parameter stability between periods (χ² = 44.07, df = 21, p = 0.002). However, differences between pedestrian and bicyclist models were substantially larger (χ² = 978.54, df = 21, p < 0.001), indicating that road user mode was a stronger source of variation than study period. Permutation importance identified posted speed limit, time of day, and non-motorist age as important severity predictors, while sex and weather contributed relatively little. Severe injury share increased above pre-pandemic levels in 2021 before declining to 21.5% by 2023. Mode specific analysis showed similar effect directions but different magnitudes. Posted speeds of 40 MPH and above were associated with severity increases of approximately 28% points for pedestrians and 13% points for bicyclists. The findings support context specific countermeasures, with speed and nighttime treatments emphasized for pedestrians and roadway treatments differentiated by road user mode where supported by evidence.

title: Agentic AI-driven human digital twins for personalized healthcare: a comprehensive survey
abstract: Human Digital Twins (HDTs) are an innovative concept in the field of personalized medicine, relying on real-time models of a human body formed via collection and analysis of physiological, clinical, behavioural, and environmental data. Research on HDTs gives evidence to a considerable promise in terms of disease predictions, patient management, therapy optimization, and clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, existing technologies suffer from incomplete multimodal data integration, low-level of independent intelligence, missing reasoning possibilities, and non-adaptive decision making, which are vital for the development of sophisticated smart healthcare systems. Technological advancements are bringing in a new incorporating idea of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI) and Multimodal Foundation Models (MFMs), which may help to solve the outlined limitations and to bring autonomous reasoning, multimodal learning, and intelligent support to clinical practice. This survey aims to review Agentic AI-led HDTs for personalized medicine, concentrating on the interrelation between HDTs and Multimodal Foundation Models, Large Language Models, Vision-Language Models, and autonomous artificial intelligence agents Our study discusses the history, models, supporting technologies, multiple data sources, and clinical uses of HDTs, along with the analysis of Agentic AI approaches that can be applied for flexible decision-making, continuous patient monitoring, and individualized treatment development. Besides, this survey consists of comparative analysis of existing research works where methods, advantages, disadvantages, and research challenges are specified. There are also serious issues discussed, like interoperability, justification, confidentiality ensuring, safety, ethical regulation, clinical testing and legal compliance, etc. And finally, we specify prospects of research within the fields of self-adaptive digital twins, reliable autonomous health agents, federated intelligence, edge AI and multimodal foundations focused on healthcare.

title: From coordination to selective intervention: an on-demand coordination method for adaptive traffic signal control, dynamic speed regulation, and route guidance.
abstract: Coordinating multiple traffic interventions does not necessarily lead to safer or more efficient traffic operations, because redundant or poorly timed interventions may introduce additional disturbances. This study moves beyond the conventional focus on how multiple interventions should cooperate by formulating coordination as a hybrid decision-making problem that determines whether additional interventions are needed, which interventions to activate, and how to implement them. Accordingly, an on-demand coordination method is proposed to selectively coordinate adaptive traffic signal control, dynamic speed regulation, and route guidance in emerging mixed traffic comprising human-driven vehicles and connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). The method employs two functionally differentiated deep reinforcement learning agents to decouple primary signal control from auxiliary intervention selection while jointly optimizing safety and efficiency. To support risk-aware decision-making, extreme value theory (EVT) is integrated into the control framework to characterize approach-specific tail crash risk. Specifically, a non-stationary generalized extreme value model is developed to capture extreme traffic conflicts and derive value-at-risk estimates, enabling the controller to identify and prioritize severe risk states that may be overlooked by average or instantaneous safety measures. The proposed method is evaluated at two signalized intersections through simulations across various CAV market penetration rates. Compared with non-coordinated and coordinated benchmarks, the proposed method consistently reduces average waiting time and generally reduces upper-tail crash risk. These safety and efficiency benefits are accompanied by a moderate increase in fuel consumption, with the trade-off becoming less pronounced as CAV penetration increases. The findings of this study support a shift from indiscriminate multi-intervention control toward selective coordination and highlight the potential to extend EVT-based safety analysis from post hoc risk assessment to active control decision-making.

Bioactive compounds from the annonaceae family in aging-associated prostate cancer: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: Aging is a complex biological process characterized by progressive molecular and cellular changes that increase susceptibility to chronic diseases, including cancer. Prostate cancer (PCa) is strongly associated with advanced aging and is the second most frequently diagnosed cancer in men worldwide, with an estimated 1.5 million new cases annually. Aging-related processes such as oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metabolic reprogramming are closely involved in PCa. Therefore, elucidating the biological mechanisms underlying aging and identifying factors capable of modulating them are essential for the development of preventive and therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing the impact of age on PCa. The Annonaceae family has been recognized as a potential source of bioactive compounds capable of modulating cellular and molecular pathways involved in aging-associated PCa. This narrative review summarizes current experimental evidence regarding the nutritional composition, phytochemical profile, and biological activities of underutilized species of the Annonaceae family, with emphasis on Annona muricata, Annona crassiflora, Annona squamosa, Annona vepretorum, Annona globiflora, and Anonidium mannii. Preclinical evidence, primarily from in vitro and animal studies, indicates that these compounds have antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, and oxidative stress-modulating effects in PCa experimental models. Based on the available evidence, underutilized species of the Annonaceae family appear to exhibit modulatory potential in aging-associated PCa and provide a scientific basis for future mechanistic investigations.

title: Humanin attenuates neuronal cellular senescence and preserves neurotransmitter release in differentiated PC12 cells.
Immunosenescence as a modifiable driver of neurodegenerative diseases: Pathways and multidimensional emerging strategies for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases.
abstract: Immunosenescence represents a core upstream driver of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), exerting its pathological effects through four mechanistically interconnected cascades: chronic inflammatory imbalance mediated by the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), oxidative stress arising from immune-metabolic reprogramming, protein homeostasis dysfunction caused by autophagy-lysosomal failure, and disrupted neuro-immune crosstalk secondary to breakdown of central nervous system (CNS) immune privilege. Current clinical practice remains largely constrained to neurotransmitter-based symptomatic management, which can neither arrest upstream pathological progression nor restore lost neuronal populations. Emerging intervention strategies targeting immunosenescence, including senolytic agents, antioxidant and metabolic modulators, autophagy restoration, and precision-targeted nanocarrier delivery, have demonstrated substantial capacity to delay disease progression in preclinical and early clinical investigations. These strategies act through selective clearance of senescent immune cells, remodeling of the neuroinflammatory microenvironment, and restoration of cellular quality-control mechanisms. The multidimensional treatment strategy approaches from the perspectives of artificial intelligence (AI) guided target discovery, nanocarrier engineering, and gut microbiota intervention to simultaneously address multiple nodes in the immunosenescence network, thereby overcoming the inherent limitations of single-target strategies. This review consolidates current mechanistic evidence and translational data to establish immunosenescence as an actionable therapeutic target and to provide a conceptual framework for precision disease-modifying therapy in AD and PD.

Stomatal biology meets multimodal foundation model-driven AI.
abstract: Stomata regulate plant growth and environmental responses through their control of gas exchange and transpiration. However, high-throughput stomatal phenotyping and the integration of phenotypic, genetic, and multiomics data remain major challenges for biological discovery and for understanding stomatal function in plants. Here, we review emerging imaging technologies and foundation models for stomatal biology and discuss how advances in AI could transform plant stomatal research. The rapid accumulation of large-scale phenotypic, genetic, and omics datasets requires systematic integration of heterogeneous data and their interpretation to uncover mechanisms of stomatal regulation within a unified reasoning framework. Therefore, we propose a stomatal phenotyping and analysis agent framework that connects these pipelines to accelerate hypothesis generation, phenotype-genotype analysis, discovery of biological function, and crop improvement.

title: Bi-allelic EPHA2 mutations cause dysosteosclerosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and enhancing osteoblastogenesis
abstract: Erythropoietin-producing hepatocellular (EPH) receptors, the largest receptor tyrosine kinase family, have been shown to play a crucial role in normal physiological processes and pathologies. EPHA2, encoded by EPHA2 gene, a member of the EPH receptor family, has been implicated in cataracts and various bone tumors, including osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and bone metastases of breast cancer. However, no association between the EPHA2 gene and genetic skeletal disorders has been reported to date. Here, we identified a Chinese family with a diagnosis of dysosteosclerosis, presenting with significant increase in lumbar spine bone mineral density, multifocal sclerotic lesions throughout the body, sclerotic skull, platyspondyly and sandwich vertebrae, and demonstrated compound heterozygous mutations in EPHA2 gene (c.890 C > T, p.Thr297Met; c.988dupT, p.Ser330PhefsX51). We observed a reduction in numerous sclerotic lesions in patients during the five-year follow-up. To systematically investigate the molecular mechanisms of pathogenesis, we employed a range of methodologies, including in vitro cellular assays, genome-wide association studies analysis, induced pluripotent stem cells models and Epha2 knockout mice models. We have determined that loss-of-function mutations in EPHA2 gene lead to dysosteosclerosis through enhancing mesenchymal stem cells osteogenic differentiation and downregulating the p38-MAPK pathway, leading to decreased osteoclast differentiation. Consequently, we proposed and validated EPHA2 as a viable therapeutic target for osteoporosis by constructing femoral fracture mice models and ovariectomized mice models. In summary, this study identifies bi-allelic loss-of-function mutations in EPHA2 gene lead to dysosteosclerosis and its underlying mechanisms, and suggests EPHA2 as a potential therapeutic target for osteoporosis.

title: Coordinating structure-guided design and cis-regulatory optimization to engineer elite herbicide-tolerance alleles in crops.
Gene regulation at the early human maternal-fetal interface.
PUS7 pseudouridylation of 7SK orchestrates human somatic cell reprogramming into iPS cells.
abstract: Reprogramming human somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells) provides huge potential for regenerative medicine but its molecular regulation remains incompletely understood. In this study, we identify PUS7 as an RNA modification checkpoint that promotes acquisition of pluripotency. PUS7 loss markedly impairs reprogramming, whereas its overexpression accelerates reprogramming efficiency and kinetics. Mechanistically, PUS7 pseudouridylates U250 of the chromatin-associated noncoding RNA 7SK, enhancing its interaction with the BRG/BRM-associated factor (BAF) complex. Loss of this modification disrupts 7SK-BAF association, reduces BAF chromatin occupancy and decreases global chromatin accessibility. We further establish PSKM (PUS7, SOX2, KLF4, MYC) reprogramming, which generates iPS cells with faithful imprinting, robust lineage potential and improved developmental fidelity. PSKM-iPS cells differentiate efficiently toward neural and hematopoietic lineages and undergo gastrulation-like morphogenesis. These findings link 7SK pseudouridylation to chromatin remodeling and establish PSKM as a framework for generating high-quality human iPS cells for modeling and regenerative medicine.

title: Hybrid transformer and CNN for hyperspectral image classification with spectral band selection
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSI) play a vital role in remote sensing applications such as surveillance and precision agriculture, yet they face challenges including limited labeled samples and class imbalance. This paper presents a new method for HSI classification by integrating spectral band selection with advanced deep learning techniques. First, we propose an optimized band selection method alongside data augmentation using crop-and-resize transformations to enhance feature diversity. Second, we introduce a hybrid convolution-transformer framework that combines Vision Transformer (ViT) and 2D-CNN architectures, supplemented with a sequence aggregation layer to mitigate overfitting on small datasets. This hybrid model effectively captures both spatial and spectral features while preserving critical spectral details. Finally, we employ a support vector machine for robust classification. Extensive experiments on three widely used HSI datasets demonstrate that our proposed ViT-CNN-BS framework achieves superior classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art few-shot learning methods and traditional approaches. Beyond achieving higher accuracy, our approach also reduces computational complexity, making it suitable for resource-constrained applications. The findings highlight the potential of hybrid deep learning frameworks for advancing remote sensing analytics, with possible extensions to environmental monitoring, disaster management, and precision agriculture.

title: FAP adipogenesis drives early spinal muscle loss in dysferlinopathy and reveals a therapeutic target
abstract: Dysferlinopathy (Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophy R2/LGMD2B) causes progressive weakness of limb-girdle muscles. Although gait abnormalities are common, the contribution of spinal muscles to disease symptoms remains poorly understood. Using cross-sectional MRI in patients and longitudinal analyses in a dysferlinopathic mouse model, we identify early-onset, progressive adipogenic degeneration of spinal muscles as a previously unrecognized hallmark of dysferlinopathy. Multiple spinal muscles, including the iliocostalis, longissimus, and spinalis, are affected, with degeneration preceding pathology in limb muscles. In mice, early spinal muscle loss is associated with altered posture and gait, implicating axial muscle degeneration as a functional driver of disease. Mechanistically, spinal muscle degeneration is accompanied by an intrinsic increase in adipogenic differentiation of spinal fibroadipogenic progenitors (FAPs). Transcriptomic profiling implicated HDAC and Wnt/ß-catenin signaling as the main regulators of FAP adipogenic shift. Pharmacological inhibition of either pathway suppressed adipogenic differentiation of dysferlinopathic FAPs in vitro, with in vivo inhibition of GSK3 reducing adipogenic degeneration in spinal and injured limb muscles. These findings establish early spinal muscle degeneration as a key pathological feature of dysferlinopathy and identify GSK3 signaling as a promising therapeutic target. Early degeneration of spinal muscles, rather than limb muscles, emerges as a key driver of gait dysfunction in dysferlinopathy, revealing axial muscle pathology as a previously overlooked disease feature and identifying GSK3 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists
abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level “Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy.” We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

title: Agrivoltaics with row crops as a pathway to solar farming on cropland
abstract: Utility-scale solar expansion on Midwestern cropland in the US is intensifying food–energy land-use conflicts. Agrivoltaics, which co-locates solar panels with food/feed (row) crops, could ease community opposition by maintaining agricultural production while generating electricity. However, row-crop agrivoltaics remains difficult to scale because of yield tradeoffs, higher solar costs, and institutional barriers. Wider adoption will require new business models and community-centered land-use practices.

title: Advancing vascularization with VEGF-bound hydrogels in tissue engineering.
Boundary Performance Enhancement Monitoring Based on Smart Bearing Service Performance Indicators
abstract: Boundary-condition anomalies in continuous girder bridges redistribute support reactions and internal forces, yet long-term reaction monitoring is seldom connected to field intervention and assessment. We developed a support-reaction monitoring workflow for force-measuring adjustable bearings. Here, smart refers to continuous sensing, remote transmission, and controllable in situ height adjustment rather than autonomous diagnosis or actuation. Three long-window indicators, normalized reaction time mean (NRTM), normalized reaction time variance (NRTV), and reaction time correlation coefficient (RTCC), were derived from statistically steady traffic windows to suppress individual-vehicle effects. Simulations of a 60-m + 80-m + 60-m variable-section girder showed convergence after 6 h, with NRTM, NRTV, and RTCC errors of 0.00%, 1.06%, and −1.34%, respectively. The indicators were only weakly affected by changes in traffic parameters, while NRTV and RTCC recovered stable values at signal-to-noise ratios of at least 30 dB. Up to 30°, a simplified skew influence-surface check yielded small NRTM, NRTV, and RTCC deviations of 0.18%, 0.87%, and −1.19%, respectively. This supports the use of resultant reactions within the tested skew range. Field implementation involved an in-service, skewed, variable-section, continuous steel box-girder bridge equipped with 12 force-measuring adjustable spherical bearings. Indicators were calculated using a 9-h sliding window with 10-min steps. Under open traffic conditions, the bearing height underwent four stages of adjustment (1–2 mm each), during which the monitored time series of indicators changed accordingly. The postadjustment shift toward finite-element targets provided a relative assessment of the intervention outcome. These results support the use of indicators with engineering records and finite-element analysis to assess boundary anomalies, staged adjustment, and relative postadjustment changes under routine traffic.

title: Measuring Station-Area Functional Profiles of High-Speed Rail Stations through a Node-Place Approach: Nationwide Evidence from China
abstract: High-speed rail (HSR) stations are critical interfaces between national transport networks and urban systems, shaping both regional accessibility and local development. Yet, previous studies seldom offer a nationally comparable assessment of HSR station-area functional profiles, defined here as the combined performance and balance of transportation-related node functions and surrounding urban place functions within station areas. It remains unclear how railway-level attributes and city-level contexts jointly influence these profiles. This study proposes an integrated evaluation framework grounded in the node-place approach to quantify, classify, and explain the functional characteristics of HSR station areas. The framework combines a set of multidimensional indicators capturing transportation connectivity (node) and urban development attributes (place) through a weighted multicriteria evaluation to derive overall functional performance and incorporates an interpretable machine learning model to uncover nonlinear effects and interaction mechanisms among key determinants. A case study is conducted using 90 major HSR stations in China within the 15-min walking zone. Results show that the station-area function evaluation index is low on average but highly heterogeneous across space. Stations in eastern and northeastern China more often exhibit balanced node-place profiles, whereas stations in western regions more frequently display functional deficiencies. A common structural pattern is that node-related functions exceed place-related functions, indicating that network accessibility is not consistently matched by surrounding urban development. Railway-level attributes explain more variance than city-level factors, with station built time emerging as the most influential determinant. Its interactions with distance to the city center, station building area, and urban population shape distinct station-area functional profiles within threshold ranges. These findings provide an evidence base for differentiated station-area planning and targeted investments, supporting the transformation of HSR stations into integrated, multifunctional urban nodes.

title: Methods and Models in Forecasting
abstract: This chapter presents the theoretical and methodological foundations of time series forecasting. It distinguishes between forecasting methods and forecasting models, emphasizing the role of probabilistic structure, conditional expectations, and model-based optimality in generating forecasts. The chapter develops key concepts such as minimum-variance forecasting, forecast unbiasedness, and the impact of parameter uncertainty. It examines the role of stationarity and non-stationarity in shaping forecast behaviour, highlighting the consequences of model mis-specification for forecast bias and variance. Extensions to multivariate time series are introduced through vector autoregressive frameworks, with particular attention to causality, co-movement, and forecasting gains from incorporating additional information. The chapter further discusses model selection strategies, smoothing techniques, and forecast averaging, alongside formal methods for ex-post forecast evaluation. Throughout, emphasis is placed on benchmarking, practical implementation, and the connection between theoretical properties and real-world forecasting performance.

title: Applications of Automatic Time Series Modelling and Forecasting
abstract: In this chapter, the reader is introduced to estimating first order autoregressive time series models, with outlier estimation and structural break estimation of US real gross domestic product and the unemployment rate. The US leading economic indicators, LEI, are used as input to estimate transfer function and Granger causality models. The purpose of this chapter is to test for the statistical significance of inputs, such as the LEI, in reducing forecast errors in the transfer function estimations, relative to no-change benchmark and first order autoregressive models, AR1. The highly statically significant LEI inputs significantly reduce the mean-square forecasting errors of the no-change and AR1 models.

title: Portfolio Selection and Measurement
abstract: In this chapter the reader is introduced to the Markowitz efficient frontier, where we examine the portfolios with the maximum returns for a given level of risk and the minimum risk for a given level of return. The total risk of the portfolio is measured by the portfolio standard deviation. The systematic or market risk of the portfolio is measured by the stock beta, or accessed by the betas, or factor exposures, of the portfolio returns relative to the multi-factor risk models. The risk-return trade-off of mutual funds is analysed. One of the most important findings reported is the effectiveness of modelling analysts’ corporate earning per share forecasts in creating portfolios significantly outperforming the portfolio universe benchmark. The corporate exports model previously introduced greatly enhances portfolio performance. Analysts’ forecasts and corporate exports push out the efficient frontier.

title: The impact of the dimensions of digital maturity in Industry 4.0 on the performance of industrial companies in Portugal’s Dão Lafões region
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between individual dimensions of digital maturity in the context of Industry 4.0 and financial and operational performance outcomes. Moving beyond aggregate maturity measures, the analysis adopts a dimensional perspective to capture the differentiated and potentially asymmetric performance effects of specific digital capabilities in industrial firms operating in a low-maturity regional context. The empirical analysis is based on a cross-sectional sample of 140 industrial companies located in Portugal's Dão Lafões region. Digital maturity was measured using a structured questionnaire grounded in the IMPULS model, which covers six core dimensions. Financial and operational performance indicators were obtained from the SABI database. Robust multiple linear regression models were employed to assess the relationships between digital maturity dimensions, overall digital maturity level, firm size, and five performance indicators: Return on Assets, Internationalization, Indebtedness, Interest Rate and Productivity. The results confirm a generally low level of digital maturity across the sample (mean = 1.13 on a 0–5 scale), alongside substantial heterogeneity among firms. Despite this low maturity context, several digital maturity dimensions exhibit statistically significant associations with performance. Positive effects are observed mainly for productivity and Return on Assets, while specific dimensions are associated with lower levels of indebtedness. However, these effects are neither uniform nor linear across performance indicators, revealing short-term trade-offs and asymmetric relationships. The impact on internationalization is heterogeneous and appears to be more pronounced among smaller firms. For managers and policymakers operating in SME-dominated and less digitally mature regions, the results highlight the importance of prioritizing targeted digital capability development over broad, undifferentiated digital transformation strategies. The findings demonstrate that digital maturity should not be interpreted as a homogeneous driver of firm performance. Instead, performance outcomes depend on the specific configuration of digital capabilities adopted by firms, as well as on organizational and contextual characteristics such as firm size.

title: Determinants of rice farmers' market participation and marketing channel choice in Côte d'Ivoire: evidence from a Multinomial Conditional Logit Model
abstract: This study identifies the determinants of rice farmers' market participation and the choice of paddy rice marketing channels in Côte d'Ivoire. A two-stage sampling method was used to randomly select 588 rice farmers from seven rice-growing areas. Unlike previous studies, we consider the characteristics related to the use of various marketing channels by using a Multinomial Conditional Logit Model. Results show that rice-farmer-specific variables, such as age, education, paddy yield, rice farming system, membership in farmer-based organizations, access to credit, and off-farm income, are crucial determinants of rice farmers' participation in the paddy market. Marketing channel-specific characteristics, such as cash payment, contractual arrangements, access to information, price per kilogram of paddy, and distance, are key determinants of marketing channel choice. Future research could be extended to other food crops and could make use of panel data. The study demonstrates the importance of considering the characteristics of rice farmers and marketing channels together to enhance rice farmers' integration into the paddy rice market in Côte d’Ivoire. It enriches the existing literature on the integration of smallholder farmers into food crop markets in developing countries.

title: Innovation meets destruction: how leadership 4.0 and destructive leadership interact with participative safety to influence job satisfaction
abstract: This study examines how aggregated team perceptions of Leadership 4.0 (L4.0) and destructive leadership (DL) are associated with individual job satisfaction and whether team-level participative safety moderates these relationships. While L4.0 has been introduced as a resource-oriented response to the challenges of digital and hybrid work, empirical evidence concerning its role at the team level remains limited. A longitudinal multilevel design was applied using data from 78 German-speaking teams (N = 253) collected across five measurement waves. L4.0, DL, and participative safety were aggregated and modeled as team-level predictors, whereas job satisfaction was modeled as an individual-level outcome. The hypotheses were tested using linear mixed models. Aggregated team perceptions of L4.0 were positively associated with individual job satisfaction, whereas aggregated team perceptions of DL were negatively associated with job satisfaction. Participative safety neither showed a significant direct association with job satisfaction nor moderated the L4.0–job satisfaction relationship. However, it strengthened the negative association between DL and job satisfaction. This study provides initial multilevel evidence that aggregated team perceptions of L4.0 are positively associated with individual job satisfaction. By examining L4.0 and DL jointly within a single analytical framework, it offers a more differentiated under-standing of how constructive and destructive leadership tendencies relate to employee well-being. Moreover, it highlights the contingent role of participative safety, which may intensify the negative association between DL and job satisfaction rather than function as a uniformly protective team resource.

title: Phenological Flexibility in Nesting Grassland Birds Over a Half Century Informs Timing of Management
abstract: The timing of biological events for wildlife species reflects and influences ecological and evolutionary processes and helps guide management actions to meet conservation objectives. Climate change may cause phenological shifts across trophic levels and ecosystems, which can have broad ecological impacts. Shifts may also result in mistiming between management practices based on historical conditions and current biological events, reducing the effectiveness of natural resource management and conservation efforts. We analyzed nesting phenology patterns over recent decades across North America for 44 species of grassland‐nesting birds, including waterfowl, upland gamebirds, shorebirds, and passerines, many of which have experienced precipitous population declines. Understanding nesting phenologies of these species is important to their conservation, as grassland management activities often conflict with reproductive periods leading to high nest and young mortality. We compiled a dataset of over 172,000 nest records spanning five decades and evaluated environmental factors influencing long‐term shifts and short‐term flexibility in nesting phenology. We found considerable variation in responses among species, with differences in both direction and magnitude of spatiotemporal effects on nest initiation dates. Notably, the community‐level nesting season lengthened over time, but shifts exhibited spatial heterogeneity within this community of grassland birds. Nesting dates shifted asymmetrically across the breeding season with differential changes in early, peak, and late nesting dates whereas long‐term changes were mediated by weather and geographic gradients. For example, nest initiation was earlier in warmer and wetter years. By applying a quantile‐based analysis, we provide estimates of the full nesting period that could serve as a flexible tool for scheduling monitoring efforts and balancing management and human activities with periods of reduced nesting activity. Our collaborative effort illustrates the challenges and opportunities of collecting long‐term data on avian communities necessary for answering questions across large regions but highlights the value of research coordination for bird conservation.

title: Nonlinear Modelling Estimates Potassium Sufficiency Ranges for Quinoa ( Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) Under Salinity Stress
abstract: Salinity is a major environmental constraint limiting crop productivity, particularly in arid and semi‐arid regions. Quinoa ( Chenopodium quinoa Willd.), a facultative halophyte, demonstrates remarkable tolerance to salinity; however, its potassium (K) nutrition dynamics under salt stress remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the role of K in alleviating salinity‐induced stress and estimated model‐derived K sufficiency ranges associated with quinoa's physiological and agronomic performance under contrasting salinity conditions. Field experiments were conducted over two consecutive years (2022–2023) using a split‐plot design with three salinity levels (10, 80, and 160 mM NaCl) imposed by irrigation treatments and seven K concentrations (5–11 mM). A suite of physiological (photosynthesis (Pn), transpiration (E), stomatal conductance (Gs), chlorophyll a ( Chl a), ) and chlorophyll b ( Chl b )), biochemical (proline, malondialdehyde (MDA)), ionic traits, and seed yield (SY) and relative seed yield (RSY) were measured. Linear, linear‐plateau, tent‐shaped, and negative exponential decay (NED) regression models were applied to the trait data to characterize response patterns and determine key K thresholds. Model robustness was assessed using leave‐one‐out cross‐validation (LOOCV), and the resulting validation statistics were compared with the calibration metrics. For the majority of traits, the LOOCV statistics supported the calibration results, confirming the robustness and predictive reliability of the selected models. Across the evaluated traits, the model‐derived responses generally supported an approximate K sufficiency range of ~8–10 mM under the experimental conditions. Physiologically, increasing K improved quinoa's photosynthetic performance, gas exchange, and chlorophyll content, with response patterns and K thresholds varying among traits and salinity levels. Under mild salinity, several physiological traits exhibited linear‐plateau responses with thresholds of approximately 8.4–9.2 mM K, whereas under moderate salinity, thresholds generally increased to approximately 9.4–10.7 mM K, and some traits, such as stomatal conductance, responded linearly across the tested K range. Increasing K also improved ionic homeostasis by increasing tissue K + and suppressing Na + accumulation. The decline in leaf and shoot Na + concentrations with increasing K supply was well described by negative exponential models, indicating that K supply was strongly associated with reduced tissue Na + accumulation and improved ionic balance. Both SY and RSY exhibited tent‐shaped responses under severe salinity: they peaked at an optimal K (~9–10 mM) and then declined at ~11 mM, indicating a supra‐optimal K threshold beyond sufficiency. The corresponding model‐derived RSY point estimates were 8.8, 9.8, and 9.2 mM K under 10, 80, and 160 mM NaCl, respectively; because confidence intervals were not available for these fitted optima, the values should be interpreted collectively as indicating an approximate 9–10 mM response range rather than as precisely distinct physiological thresholds. Most nonlinear models showed good predictive performance within the experimental dataset and captured the observed plateau and peak response patterns, thereby providing quantitative working estimates of K sufficiency and supra‐optimal response ranges under the salinity conditions evaluated. Moderate K enrichment within an approximate range of ~8–10 mM was associated with improved quinoa performance under the salinity conditions evaluated, whereas further K generally provided little additional benefit or was associated with declining responses in some traits. These model‐derived ranges represent experimentally derived working estimates that require independent validation across cultivars, environments, and management conditions before broader agronomic application.

title: Increased Pupil Constriction Latency in Immunoglobulin G4-related Ophthalmic Disease.
abstract: PURPOSE To examine the pupillary light reflex (PLR) in Immunoglobulin G4-related ophthalmic disease (IgG4-ROD) compared with healthy controls using virtual reality-based infrared pupillometry. DESIGN Cross-sectional matched case-control study. PARTICIPANTS Twenty-five eyes from 25 biopsy-proven IgG4-ROD patients without a history of optic neuropathy and 50 eyes from 50 age-, sex-, and smoking-matched healthy subjects were included. METHODS Participants underwent PLR assessment using a virtual reality head-mounted display with integrated infrared pupillometry. Pupillary responses to three progressively increasing white-light stimuli were recorded at 120 Hz. Twenty-seven PLR parameters were extracted across response latency, constriction, and redilation phases. Group differences were analyzed using paired t-tests, multinomial logistic regression, and backward stepwise variable selection. Machine learning classifiers were evaluated using accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Main Outcome Measures Pupil constriction latency, constriction amplitude, velocity, redilation parameters, and machine learning classification performance metrics. RESULTS Pupil constriction latency at the third (highest intensity) stimulus (LAT3rd) was significantly prolonged in IgG4-ROD eyes compared with controls (P < 0.05), while other PLR parameters were comparable between groups. LAT3rd remained a significant differentiating feature on multinomial logistic regression and backward stepwise selection. Machine learning models using all features showed good performance, with Random Forest achieving an accuracy/AUC of 0.875/0.900. When using bootstrapped LAT3rd-only data, K-nearest neighbors, decision tree, and random forest models also demonstrated good classification performance. CONCLUSION IgG4-ROD eyes exhibit prolonged pupil constriction latency, suggesting subclinical involvement of the pupillary light reflex pathway. Virtual reality-based infrared pupillometry may serve as a useful non-invasive tool for detecting neural or autonomic dysfunction in IgG4-ROD.

Constraints and opportunities in cluster-based farming in Ethiopia
abstract: In many developing countries, smallholders play a central role in the agricultural sector, and holding significant potential for agricultural growth and rural development. In Ethiopia, agriculture contributes about 37.57% to Et GDP and supports the livelihoods of most of the population. However, recent agricultural growth has not efficiently addressed persistent challenges of food insecurity, malnutrition, and rural poverty among smallholder farmers. To improve productivity and promote commercialization, the Agricultural Transformation Agency introduced cluster-based farming approach aimed at transforming subsistence farming into market-oriented production system. Despite its potential benefits, the adoption and expansion of cluster farming remain limited due to several constraints. Therefore, this study reviews the opportunities and constraints of cluster-based farming in Ethiopia from social, economic, ecological/environmental, institutional, and political perspectives. This study employed a systematic literature review methodology. Relevant studies were identified through digital libraries, web sources, Ethiopian public university repositories, ATA government website and other academic databases. A keyword-based search strategy was used to identify relevant publications mainly covering the period from 2015 to 2026. Based on relevance to study objective, a total of 23 empirical studies were selected and analyzed. The findings indicate that cluster-based farming in Ethiopia provides several opportunities across multiple dimensions. Social opportunities include enhanced farmer-to-farmer interaction, knowledge sharing, and collaboration. Economic opportunities involve improved productivity, economies of scale, better market access, and increased bargaining power. Ecological opportunities include improved natural resource management and the potential adoption of climate-smart agricultural practices. Institutional opportunities arise from stronger partnerships and coordination among farmers, government agencies, and development organizations, while political support through national agricultural development strategies further promotes cluster initiatives. However, several constraints also affect the implementation of cluster-based farming. These include farmers’ resistance to collective approaches, limited economies of scale among smallholders, unfavorable agro-ecological conditions, weak institutional coordination, and political instability. Cluster-based farming has the potential to transform smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia by improving productivity, commercialization, and rural livelihoods. However, its success depends on addressing key social, economic, ecological, institutional, and political constraints. Prioritize should be given to improving rural infrastructure to better connect cluster farms with markets. Expand agricultural research, strengthening farmer training, and securing financial support for cooperatives are also essential. In addition, promoting pro-poor agricultural strategies, extending extension services and ensuring continuous government monitoring and evaluation are necessary to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cluster- based farming in Ethiopia.

title: Star-ov: satellite-oriented trusted authorization and responsibility with stratified model encryption and ownership verifications
abstract: With the increasing adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs) in remote sensing interpretation and on-orbit intelligent processing, protecting the intellectual property of deployed models faces new challenges, including limited onboard computational resources, constrained satellite–ground communication bandwidth, differentiated multi-user services, and difficulty in ownership attribution after model leakage. Existing model protection approaches mainly rely on either active encryption or passive watermarking mechanisms, which are insufficient to simultaneously satisfy the requirements of access control, service continuity, and post-leakage accountability in satellite-based scenarios. In this paper, we propose STAR-OV, a stratified and controllable model protection framework tailored for satellite deployment. By introducing a two-stage reversible parameter perturbation mechanism, STAR-OV enables progressive degradation of model performance from the original high-accuracy state to an intermediate-accuracy state and finally to a fully unusable state. The perturbations introduced at different stages are organized into distributable hierarchical keys, thereby supporting differentiated service access for users with varying authorization levels. Furthermore, after the model is fully restored to its original accuracy, a latent watermark is embedded. The watermark remains inactive during normal inference without the activation key, while producing stable and verifiable responses on a trigger set once the corresponding key is applied, enabling reliable ownership verification in the event of model leakage. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the usability of unauthorized models by modifying an extremely small fraction of parameters, while maintaining strong robustness against fine-tuning, pruning, and weight noise attacks. Owing to its low computational overhead and flexible deployment capability, STAR-OV provides a practical solution for resource-constrained satellite-based onboard intelligent inference scenarios.
