title: Proteomic landscape of IGF-I gene transfer in osteoarthritis-derived human bone marrow stromal cells undergoing chondrogenesis
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive joint disease marked by the breakdown of cartilage and impaired repair capacity. Gene therapy applied to human bone marrow-derived adherent stromal cells (BM-MSCs) with recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors represents a promising strategy for cartilage regeneration. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects remain largely unexplored. In this study, we investigated the proteomic changes induced by rAAV-mediated insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) gene transfer during the chondrogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs derived from OA patients. BM-MSCs from OA donors were transduced with recombinant rAAV vectors encoding either IGF-I or the lacZ gene (β-galactosidase) as a control and cultured in three-dimensional micromass systems under chondrogenic conditions for 21 days. Histological, immunohistochemical (IHC) and immunofluorescence (IF) analyses were performed to characterize the chondrogenic phenotype of the model and to provide orthogonal validation of selected proteomic findings. Mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling identified protein detection patterns and quantitative changes associated with IGF-I overexpression. Pathway and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were carried out to explore the functional implications of differentially expressed proteins. A total of 4,284 proteins were identified, of which 112 showed notable changes in detection patterns or abundance associated with IGF-I. Functional enrichment analyses showed involvement of pathways related to metabolism, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis, apoptosis regulation, cell proliferation, glycosylation, and the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) machinery. Histological and IHC analyses provided supportive evidence of cartilage-related matrix deposition. Orthogonal validation by IHC and IF confirmed the IGF-I-mediated upregulation of β-catenin and exportin-1 (XPO1). Further analyses provided exploratory evidence of increased active β-catenin and predominantly extranuclear distribution of sirtuin-1, a known XPO1 substrate, in IGF-I-transduced micromasses. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of rAAV-mediated IGF-I gene therapy in OA-derived BM-MSCs undergoing chondrogenesis. The IGF-I gene transfer was associated with broad proteomic changes involving metabolic and protein processing pathways, and enhanced cartilage-specific matrix deposition, highlighting molecular mechanisms of potential relevance to cartilage repair in OA.

title: Smart farms, virtual mirrors: AI-powered digital twins reshaping modern agriculture
Modelling the Structural Determinants of Households’ Indebtedness among Agricultural Households: An ISM-MICMAC Approach
abstract: Background: Agricultural households’ indebtedness is influenced by interconnected farm, financial and household conditions, making it important to understand relationships among its structural elements rather than examining them independently. This study develops a systemic representation of these interrelationships using literature-derived structural elements. Methods: Seven structural elements were assessed through expert judgement using interpretive structural modelling (ISM) and MICMAC analysis. 40 experts were contacted, 38 responded and 37 responses were considered valid. Three senior experts subsequently reviewed and consolidated the pairwise judgements. Twenty-one unique pairwise relationships were assessed and used to construct the Structured Self-Interaction Matrix, reachability structure and hierarchical model. Result: The final structure comprised two levels. Landholding Size occupied Level 2 and had driving and dependence powers of 7 and 1, respectively. Production capacity, cost burden, access to formal credit, farm income, borrowing level and household indebtedness occupied Level 1, each with driving and dependence powers of 6 and 7. The findings indicate an interconnected structure in which Landholding Size forms the foundational element.
journal: Agricultural Science Digest - A Research Journal

title: Nutritional Status of Soils Under Cassava Cultivation Using the Diagnosis and Recommendation System (DRIS) in the Savanna Zone of the Central African Republic
abstract: Cassava is an important crop that ensures food security for the population in the Central African Republic (CAR). It also significantly contributes to improving farmers' incomes. Unfortunately, there is no specific data on soil nutrient status that would allow for informed management of the crop’s nutritional condition and yield improvement, despite existing potential. The Diagnosis and Recommendation Integrated System (DRIS) is an approach used to interpret plant tissue analysis results and helps assess the nutritional status of crops. It focuses on comparing paired nutrient ratios and concentrations of nutrients in leaf tissues with norms developed from high-yielding crop populations. The objective of this study is to apply the DRIS model to determine the nutritional status of cassava cropping systems in the savanna forest zone of CAR. In total, 126 leaf samples were collected from cassava fields in the region. Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), Calcium (Ca), Magnesium (Mg), and Zinc (Zn) contents were analyzed. Root yields were also recorded. Significant differences (p = 0.001) were observed between the root yields of the low and high-yielding sub-populations. Based on the Nutritional Balance Index, nutrient requirements for cassava in this savanna zone were ranked as: Ca > Mg > N > K > P > Zn. The study recommends the implementation of Integrated Soil Fertility Management (ISFM) technologies in cassava cultivation systems in each zone, with emphasis on Nitrogen and Calcium supplementation.

title: From Detection to Investigation: A Survey of Foundation Models and Agents for Financial Fraud and Financial Crime
abstract: Foundation models are extending research on financial fraud and financial crime from isolated risk detection to document understanding, relational analysis, and investigative workflows. A gap nevertheless separates model outputs from candidate evidence and actionable conclusions. This survey examines advances in six families of foundation models: language, vision, speech, temporal, graph, and tabular models. It compares their roles and limitations along two dimensions: the risk-control lifecycle and the directness of the supporting evidence. Existing studies show that pretraining can support representation reuse and the processing of unstructured information, with direct validation in some financial tasks. Cross-modal identity binding, information availability over time, report faithfulness, and case-level benefits require separate evaluation. Evidence on investigative agents spans prototypes, controlled tasks, expert assessments, and industry disclosures, which establish different aspects of workflow feasibility, task performance, and user assessment. Establishing gains in investigative efficiency and reductions in financial losses requires case-level comparative evidence. We examine entity and temporal alignment, the organization of candidate evidence, constrained tool execution, and investigative benchmark design, together with the implications of adversarial threats, privacy, fairness, and model risk governance. Research priorities should shift from expanding system functionality toward factual traceability, sufficient evidence for decisions, and reviewable actions.

title: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for Fixed Wing Aerial Pursuit with Differentiable Decision Trees and Curriculum Learning
abstract: Neural policy networks can achieve effective control in dynamic pursuit tasks, but their decisions are difficult to audit. This study replaces the actor in proximal policy optimization with a full binary differentiable decision tree and uses a two-stage curriculum to stabilize learning. The policy was trained in a JSBSim six degree of freedom fixed wing simulation with a 15-dimensional observation, eight discrete maneuvers, a 0.2 s simulation step, and 100 million interaction steps. The learned tree has five decision levels and 32 leaves, and it is discretized after training into feature-threshold rules and deterministic leaf actions. Across 1,000 evaluation episodes covering ten initial pursuit geometries, the combined tree policy and curriculum achieved a 98.8 percent success rate, compared with 96.2 percent for neural PPO, 90.0 percent for soft actor-critic, 50.7 percent for deep Q-learning, and 0 percent for decision tree policy optimization under the reported configurations. Mean inference time was 0.26 ms per decision for the tree policy and 0.63 ms for neural PPO. In 100 direct matches against neural PPO, the tree policy won 57. The final policy can be inspected as 32 rules, although the present results are limited to one simulator, one discrete action design, and evaluations without reported variability across independent training seeds.

title: Phenology-driven multisensor unsupervised crop mapping in data-scarce irrigated agriculture: a case of Adea District in Ethiopia
abstract: Accurate irrigation planning, water allocation, and agricultural productivity assessment are frequently constrained in data-scare regions where reliable ground-based crop information and spatial coverage data are limited. This study addresses these gaps using a phenology-driven, multisensor unsupervised crop-mapping framework implemented within Google Earth Engine (GEE). The approach integrates monthly normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) profiles from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1VV backscatter, and digital elevation model–derived terrain slope into unsupervised K-means clustering algorithm. Adea District, Ethiopia, served as a demonstration site to evaluate and interpret the phenological signatures of key irrigated crops. The identified crop types were mapped to estimate spatial coverage and compared with the ground truth observations of irrigated wheat and tomato fields. The approach successfully distinguished irrigated wheat and tomato fields with an overall classification accuracy of 91%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.82, and estimated cultivated areas of 666.93 and 812.35 ha, respectively. Combining phenological profiles with multisensor satellite observations significantly enhance unsupervised classification performance in heterogeneous, smallholder-dominated agricultural landscapes. The cloud-based framework offers a computationally scalable and cost-effective solution for crop mapping, and water productivity monitoring in data-scarce agricultural regions.

title: AI-Enabled Sustainable Precision Farming Using Raspberry Pi and Coral Edge TPU with Cloud-Based Model Training
abstract: Precision Agriculture requires intelligent, adaptable and efficient technology that is capable of making decisions in agriculture at the right time, based on the condition of the plants and the environment. This paper proposes the development of an AI-based sustainable precision farming system based on computer vision, cloud based model training, Raspberry Pi, Coral Edge TPU and the Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. The proposed architecture's sensing layer, edge processing layer, cloud intelligence layer, and application layer enables a complete data processing pipeline from the field to real time decision support. Crop photos are collected for AI condition classification and agricultural conditions such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity and light intensity are collected by built-in sensors. After the above preprocessing, normalisation, image resizing and augmentation, the dataset is divided into training, validation and test sets. The trained deep learning models in a cloud environment are then quantized and converted to be optimized for the edge, following this step. Following this step, the trained deep learning models are quantized and converted for optimization on edge. The optimized model achieves an exemplary accuracy of 94.82%, precision of 94.47%, recall of 94.05% and F1-score of 94.26%. Deploying with the Coral Edge TPU reduces inference latency to approximately 38ms compared to Raspberry Pi-only processing, increases processing throughput to 26.3 pictures per second and reduces CPU usage. The edge-assisted architecture reduces the need for constant connection to the cloud, giving local decision making a leg up. Illustrative sustainability study estimates that condition based monitoring can save 22% of the irrigation water used every day. The findings indicated that the introduction of the edge AI and cloud intelligence in precision agricultural systems that are responsive, scalable, and resource-efficient is technically possible.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Energy-Efficient Smart Agriculture Management Framework Using IoT and Ensemble Machine Learning for Intelligent Crop Health Monitoring and Resource Optimization
abstract: Context: Smart agriculture plays an important role in addressing the challenges of food security, environmental sustainability, and sustainable farming through IoT. Farmers are facing many issues in traditional farming, such as inefficient monitoring and poor crop health detection. Traditional farming has a negative impact on crop production and sustainability. In this regard, the development of intelligent and energy-efficient agricultural monitoring systems has become crucial for contemporary precision farming applications. Objective: This study aims to monitor crop health and optimize resource use using machine learning techniques. Our proposed system intends to monitor crop conditions in real time, enhance agricultural management, and minimize unnecessary sensor utilization and communication overhead. Material/methods : In this paper, we used five machine learning classifiers to monitor crop health using sensor data. The agricultural sensor data (soil moisture, soil temperature, soil pH, humidity, air temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, NDVI index, and 5G latency) were used for crop health monitoring. The models, such as RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, and soft voting were used for crop health classification into the Healthy, High_Stress, and Moderate_Stress categories. The experimental observation revealed that soft voting achieved the highest accuracy of 94.5%, macro-F1 score of 0.945, weighted F1 score of 0.945, and AUC-ROC score of 0.988 compared to the other models. The cross-validation results further validated the robustness and stability of the proposed framework. The IoT-enabled intelligent agriculture management system offers an efficient, scalable solution for real-time crop health monitoring
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Engineering a multifunctional bioactive coordination polymer nanoplatform for inflammation-responsive bone regeneration
abstract: Inflammatory bone diseases are closely associated with impaired osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and excessive inflammatory signaling. Sinomenine (SIN) exhibits anti-inflammatory activity; however, its therapeutic application is limited by poor bioavailability. In this work, a multifunctional nanoplatform (CS-1@CP1@SIN) was constructed for SIN delivery and electrochemical sensing applications. The nanocomposite exhibited a mesoporous structure, structural stability, and improved electrochemical response characteristics. In a TNF-α-induced inflammatory MSC model, CS-1@CP1@SIN improved cell viability, reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6), and enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers (Runx2, ALP, and OCN). In addition, the CS-1@CP1@SIN-modified electrode exhibited enhanced electrocatalytic activity toward tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), enabling sensitive and reliable electrochemical detection. These results demonstrate that the proposed nanoplatform integrates anti-inflammatory therapy and electrochemical sensing functions, providing a multifunctional strategy for inflammatory bone disease treatment and food antioxidant monitoring.

title: Women at the Helm: Female Top Managers and Business Process Innovation in Ecuadorian Firms
abstract: Women’s participation in senior management has increased, yet evidence regarding its relationship with different forms of business innovation remains inconclusive, particularly in emerging economies. This study examines whether formal Ecuadorian firms with a woman as their top manager are more likely to report business process innovation than firms led by men. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional design was applied to firm-level data from 345 enterprises included in the World Bank Enterprise Survey Ecuador; 66 firms (19.1%) reported a female top manager. Process innovation was measured from WBES item H5, which asks whether the establishment introduced a new or improved process during the preceding three years, including production or service methods, logistics/delivery/distribution, or supporting activities. Weighted logit models with firm controls and sector and region fixed effects were estimated. In the main specification (n = 327), female top management was associated with higher odds of process innovation (OR = 3.475; 95% CI [1.570, 7.688]; p = 0.002), and the direction remained positive across robustness checks. No statistically significant association was found with product innovation, R&D expenditure, or green-practice adoption. The findings therefore support a differentiated interpretation: female top management is associated with internal process change, but not uniformly with every innovation outcome. Because the data are cross-sectional and the female-manager group is comparatively small, the estimates are associational, their precision and heterogeneity are limited, and generalization is restricted to the formal non-agricultural private-sector population represented by the WBES sampling frame.

title: Predicting Lentil Seed Yield from Agronomic Traits Using a Foundation-Augmented Machine Learning Ensemble
abstract: Accurate agricultural yield prediction is crucial for crop management and data-driven decision-making. This study proposes a machine learning framework for predicting total lentil seed yield using 264 observations collected during a single growing season at one location in Sivas, Türkiye. Seven regression models and the tabular foundation model TabPFN were evaluated through nested cross-validation. The fixed post hoc Foundation-Augmented Averaging Ensemble (FAAE) combined TabPFN, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost using equal weights, while the primary fully nested evaluation selected the four ensemble members within each outer training fold. The fully nested FAAE achieved R2 = 0.891 ± 0.045, comparable to the strongest individual models, while the fixed post hoc FAAE yielded R2 = 0.897 ± 0.038. Split conformal prediction produced well-calibrated uncertainty intervals at 80%, 90%, and 95% coverage. SHAP and LOCO identified pods per plant and biological yield as the dominant predictors of lentil yield. Overall, these findings indicate that FAAE can provide competitive predictive performance within a leakage-controlled framework while also supporting uncertainty quantification and biologically meaningful interpretation. Because the dominant predictors, pods per plant and biological yield, are measured at or near physiological maturity, the proposed framework is more suitable for end-of-season yield estimation than for early-season forecasting. The framework therefore shows potential for within-trial yield assessment, although validation using replicated material across additional years and locations is required before broader generalization.

title: Reliability-Aware Evaluation of TabPFN for Small-Sample Crop Classification in Mountainous Agricultural Regions Using Multi-Temporal Sentinel-2-Derived Features
abstract: Crop classification in mountainous agricultural regions is challenged by fragmented fields, limited reference samples, class imbalance, and strong spatial heterogeneity. We evaluated the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) for reliability-aware small-sample crop classification using 2857 reference samples from Yuxi City, China, and 66 multi-temporal Sentinel-2-derived spectral, vegetation-index, and texture features, excluding longitude and latitude from model inputs. Under five fixed stratified 70/30 splits, TabPFN achieved an overall accuracy of 0.8944 ± 0.0127 and a Macro-F1 of 0.8798 ± 0.0173, outperforming five conventional baseline classifiers. Probability reliability analysis and selective classification further showed that confidence scores were informative of prediction risk and could support the prioritization of low-confidence samples for expert review. Calibration analysis also indicated agreement between confidence and empirical correctness. In matched five-fold validation, pooled Macro-F1 decreased from 0.8632 under stratified random folds to 0.6559 under projected-coordinate spatial folds, a 24.0% relative reduction, although TabPFN remained the highest-ranked classifier among eight tabular models. Excluding four EVI-derived predictors reduced Macro-F1 from 0.8806 to 0.8573, indicating a useful but non-exclusive dependence on these predictors. Overall, the results show that random validation can be optimistic under spatial dependence and that broader cross-region and cross-year generalization requires independent evaluation.

title: Prototype Matching Guided by Temporal–Phenological Quantitative Features for Crop Classification
abstract: Accurate crop classification requires effective representation of crop-growth dynamics and traceable classification decisions. This study proposes a prototype-matching framework guided by quantitative temporal and phenological features to establish explicit relationships between crop-growth representations and class-level references. Using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery from an oasis agricultural region in Manas County, Xinjiang, China, four major crops were investigated: cotton, maize, spring wheat, and winter wheat. The framework integrates explicit temporal statistics, quantitative phenological descriptors, and their corresponding deep representations into a unified feature space. Class prototypes are constructed from the resulting representations, and final crop labels are assigned through explicit sample–prototype similarity or distance comparisons. Prototype-space relationships are further analysed to quantify class separability and examine potential classification ambiguity. The results demonstrate that temporal representations provide stronger class separation than phenological representations, while their integration enables continuous temporal dynamics and structured phenological characteristics to be examined within a unified prototype space. Prototype-space analysis reveals clearer separation for cotton and maize, whereas spring wheat exhibits the smallest similarity and distance margins. In the primary field-level classification experiment, the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 96.03%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.9356, a Balanced Accuracy of 86.05%, and a Macro-F1 of 86.26%. In a separate experiment under common training conditions, prototype matching achieves a Balanced Accuracy of 91.36% and a Macro-F1 of 89.53%, exceeding Transformer and random forest by 7.36 and 12.78 percentage points in Balanced Accuracy, respectively. The improvements are particularly evident for spring wheat. These findings demonstrate that the framework connects quantitative crop-growth representation with explicit prototype-based classification while providing measurable evidence for interpreting class-specific discrimination and classification ambiguity.

title: Integration of Solar Energy, Second-Life Lithium-Ion Batteries, and Plasma-Activated Water for Reduced-Nitrogen Greenhouse Cultivation
abstract: The research demonstrates a national project combining solar photovoltaics with second-life automotive lithium batteries for local-scale agricultural irrigation and greenhouse climate control. The auto-opening greenhouse system can adapt to various climate conditions in resource-limited areas. Applying in-house battery management system (BMS) based on adaptive control algorithm, it allows real-time monitoring and prediction of critical parameters such as effective capacity and safety, ensuring safe operation and longer battery life. Results show that, with optimized management, the lifespan of second-life batteries can be extended by an additional 7.8–9.3 years, achieving a maximum discharge power of 3.3 kW while keeping thermal control deviations within 0.3%. Both grid-connected and stand-alone microgrid setups have been successfully tested in the field, improving local energy independence and reducing reliance on external power sources. In addition, to avoid the harm of chemical fertilizers to the environment, air nitrogen fixation technology is employed to extract nitrogen fertilizer from the air to irrigate crops such as tomatoes and cucumbers. The control system uses solar power to store electricity in batteries daily to provide nitrogen fixation and basic greenhouse needs, and can maintain greenhouse operations without relying on power grid. This work offers a practical, scalable model for low-carbon agricultural energy solutions, reducing carbon emissions by about 1.28 metric tons of CO2 per system each year. It provides a framework to guide policies, promote low-carbon transitions, and support global sustainable development goals in underserved areas.

title: Asteraceae Extracts Against Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae): A Comprehensive Review of Biological Activity, Phytochemical Profiles and Acute Oral Toxicity in Mammals
abstract: Spodoptera frugiperda is a polyphagous pest of global significance, causing substantial yield losses in maize and other staple crops, which has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives to synthetic insecticides. The Asteraceae family has emerged as a promising source of botanical insecticides, but a comprehensive synthesis of its true potential including biological efficacy, chemical basis and acute oral toxicity in mammalian models remains lacking. This review critically examines the biological activity of Asteraceae extracts against S. frugiperda from the 2021 to 2026 period and their phytochemical profiles and acute oral toxicity in mammals. Our analysis reveals three major findings. First, essential oils exhibit the highest insecticidal potency, but they also present the most concerning mammalian acute oral toxicity profiles. Second, although 57 major constituents—including terpenoids, phenolic acids, flavonoids, and fatty acid derivatives— have been identified, fewer than 13% have been individually evaluated against this pest, introducing substantial uncertainty in attributing activity to specific compounds. Third, most mammalian toxicity studies report only limited LD50 thresholds (e.g., >2000 mg kg−1 BW), preventing accurate GHS classification and regulatory positioning. Therefore, realising the potential of Asteraceae based insecticides requires not only the discovery of bioactive extracts but also rigorous, integrated toxicity and phytochemical characterisation.

title: Digital and AI-Supported Game-Based Interventions for Executive Function Development in Early Childhood: A Systematic Review
abstract: Executive function (EF)—working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility—underpins school readiness, academic achievement, and socio-emotional competence in early childhood (ages 3–8). Digital and AI-supported game-based interventions are a promising but underexamined modality for EF training. This review aimed to synthesize the reported effects of digital and AI-supported game-based interventions on executive function in children aged 3–8 years and the technological features linked to reported gains. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review synthesized 19 studies from six databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore) covering January 2012–March 2026, involving 1890 children aged 4–8 years across 11 countries. Narrative synthesis indicated predominantly positive findings across all three EF components; this was observed most consistently for working memory. Adaptive difficulty calibration, immediate corrective feedback, and motivational scaffolding were the features most often linked to gains; positive findings were somewhat more frequent in school-based settings and in longer interventions, though these descriptive patterns rest on small, unbalanced subgroups and cannot establish setting or duration as moderators. Critically, the corpus was overwhelmingly conventional and rule-based: only three studies (15.8%) contained machine-learning components, with none driving pedagogical personalization (confined to gesture recognition or post hoc analysis); none employed conversational agents or affect-sensing, and no eligible study sampled 3-year-olds. Findings should therefore be read as evidence about adaptive digital game-based interventions rather than AI-driven ones. This near-absence of machine-learning personalization for typically developing children aged 3–8 years is itself a principal finding, alongside gaps in long-term retention, cross-cultural generalizability, and ethical AI data governance.

title: Parameter Estimation of a Single-Phase Diode-Bridge Rectifier Under Steady-State, Load Variation, and Startup Transient Using Terminal Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a numerical framework for parameter estimation of a single-phase diode-bridge rectifier with capacitive filtering. The proposed approach integrates a state-space model of the rectifier, numerically solved using the second-order Backward Differentiation Formula (BDF2), with a derivative-free Nelder–Mead optimization algorithm. Parameter estimation is performed using only terminal voltage and current measurements, eliminating the need for explicit conduction-interval detection or direct measurement of internal circuit states. The framework is experimentally validated under three operating conditions: steady-state operation, dynamic load variation, and startup transient. Five estimation scenarios are analyzed to assess the influence of the excitation condition and the inclusion of the initial capacitor voltage UC0 as an additional unknown parameter on estimation accuracy. The results demonstrate that excitation conditions strongly influence parameter estimation accuracy. Steady-state excitation yields the largest estimation errors, particularly for the series resistance and DC-link capacitance, whereas dynamic load variation improves the estimation accuracy of several parameters. The startup transient provides the highest overall estimation accuracy, with all four estimated parameters exhibiting relative errors below 5.5%. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for parameter estimation of single-phase rectifiers using terminal measurements only and highlights the importance of the excitation condition for reliable parameter estimation. The method can support the identification and modeling of nonlinear electronic loads in power-system and power-quality studies.

title: Modeling Nutrient Concentrations in a Greenhouse Cascade Soilless System
abstract: A dynamic simulation model was developed and calibrated to predict nutrient concentrations in a three-level cascade hydroponic system (CasH). The performance of the model was evaluated across donor/primary (tomato) and receiver secondary (mint, peppermint), and tertiary (sea fennel, lemon balm) crops. An independent dataset was available for both calibration and evaluation of the primary tomato crop, whereas data for the secondary and tertiary stages were used exclusively for model calibration. Following model evaluation, three distinct operational scenarios were simulated, ranging from a baseline monoculture to a comprehensive three-stage cascade system. The simulations forecasted the progressive nutrient accumulation across stages, identifying the operational point at which critical sodium and salinity thresholds are approached. The proposed model shows potential as a foundational component for digital twins of hydroponic systems, complementing rather than replacing physical sensors by providing dynamic hourly simulations of nutrient dynamics. The model serves as an effective tool for optimizing resource efficiency and mitigating salinity risks in sustainable, closed-loop horticultural systems. These findings confirm the feasibility of nutrient-specific tracking in closed-loop horticulture, though independent evaluation was restricted to the primary stage, and the empirical coefficients remain specific to the evaluated three-stage CasH configuration.

title: Nitrogen Management for Mitigating Agricultural N2O Emissions in Semi-Arid Morocco: A Comparative Review
abstract: Morocco’s semi-arid farms are under growing pressure to lower nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions while maintaining crop yields and soil health. Agriculture is a major anthropogenic source of N2O emissions in Morocco; improved nitrogen management is therefore relevant to the country’s broader climate mitigation efforts. This review examines regulatory, technical, and economic measures that have reduced nitrogen losses or agricultural N2O emissions in other countries and assesses their potential relevance to Morocco’s smallholder-dominated farming systems. In 2018, Moroccan managed soils released 13,108 Gg of carbon dioxide equivalents (CO2-eq) according to the national inventory, highlighting the importance of improved nitrogen management for agricultural climate mitigation. The study compares peer-reviewed research, policy documents, and regulatory frameworks from four benchmark countries: Denmark, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and Brazil. It addresses three questions: which nitrogen management strategies have evidence of reducing agricultural N2O emissions in contexts relevant to Morocco; which institutional, regulatory, and socioeconomic barriers may constrain their adoption; and how these strategies could be incorporated into a phased national framework. For each intervention, the review synthesizes reported outcomes, the agronomic and climatic conditions under which they were obtained, and their potential transferability to Morocco’s semi-arid agricultural systems. Outcomes are differentiated as direct N2O measurements, nitrogen loss or fertilizer use indicators, agronomic feasibility evidence, or policy and enabling evidence. The review also identifies gaps in Morocco’s fertilizer governance under Law No. 53-18 and considers national enabling assets, including soil fertility mapping, emerging organic-fertilizer supply chains, conservation agriculture initiatives, and existing agricultural-support programmes. The review presents an author-proposed Integrated Nitrogen Management Framework (INMF) based on three complementary pillars: regulatory reform, field-level technical measures, and economic instruments. It presents three implementation periods—2027–2029, 2029–2032, and 2032–2035—for testing, validating, and progressively scaling these measures under Moroccan conditions. The INMF is a conceptual, phased implementation framework rather than a quantitative national mitigation model. It does not estimate an aggregate agricultural N2O emission reduction because the reviewed interventions differ in their production context, evidence type, and measured outcome. Morocco’s unconditional Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) provides the broader policy context, but its economy-wide target is not interpreted as a sector-specific target for agricultural N2O emissions. The review discusses implementation challenges, including data limitations, institutional capacity constraints, and smallholder adoption barriers. It identifies priorities for Morocco: field measurement of N2O emissions and emission factors, multi-site evaluation of mitigation practices, strengthened monitoring and advisory systems, and socioeconomic assessment of farmer adoption and policy feasibility.

title: Unraveling Spatial Associations of Surface Subsidence in Typical Oil Production Areas of Songyuan City by Integrating Time-Series InSAR and Deep Learning
abstract: Oilfield subsidence threatens infrastructure and sustainable development. Although facility detection, factor-association analysis, and deformation forecasting have each advanced considerably, their systematic integration remains insufficiently explored for oilfields in agricultural plains, where C-band SAR decorrelation over cropland and wetland yields sparse and uneven deformation observations. This constraint complicates facility extraction, quantitative analysis of associations among interacting factors, and robust temporal prediction. To address these challenges, this study develops and applies an integrated modular workflow for the monitoring, analysis and prediction of surface subsidence in a typical oil production area of Songyuan City, China. We first used PS-InSAR for high-precision deformation monitoring and validated the results with leveling survey data. Subsequently, the YOLOv12 model was utilized for automated oil well identification, and the Geodetector model was applied to quantify the spatial associations between subsidence and the examined natural and anthropogenic factors. Finally, a hybrid LSTM–Transformer model was developed for time-series prediction and applied to forecast deformation through November 2025, twelve months beyond the final SAR acquisition. Results indicate significant spatial differentiation in deformation, with a maximum subsidence rate of −26.0 mm/y. Analysis identifies oil well density and surface elevation as the leading spatial factors among those examined, and the buffer zone analysis indicates a distance-related association of approximately 700 m between oil wells and subsidence rates. The hybrid model demonstrated superior overall accuracy compared to standalone LSTM and Transformer models. The findings provide concrete scientific support for risk mitigation in oil cities.

title: A Transformer Network for Settlement Generalization Integrating Raster Maps and Remote Sensing Images
abstract: To address the challenges of reliance on manual expertise and insufficient automation and intelligence in settlement generalization during scale transformation, this paper proposes a multi-scale settlement generalization model (DSG-Trans) based on the fusion of dual-source data: raster maps and remote sensing images. Leveraging the cartographic correspondence between remote sensing image resolution and map scale, this model integrates source-scale maps with specific low-resolution remote sensing imagery to automatically generate target-scale raster maps that adhere to cartographic specifications. The model employs a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism and a Transformer architecture to facilitate the semantic integration of dual-source data, while a progressive upsampling strategy is utilized to reconstruct spatial details. Additionally, a composite loss function incorporating four constraints is designed to enhance the quality of settlement generalization. Experiments were conducted in New York City, USA, using a multi-source dataset constructed from 3D-GloBFP building footprint data and multi-source remote sensing imagery, focusing on two scale transformation scenarios: 1:5000 to 1:10,000 and 1:5000 to 1:25,000. The results indicate that the proposed method effectively learns and simulates expert generalization knowledge, significantly improving the automation level and scale adaptability of map generalization while preserving geometric morphology and spatial distribution patterns.

title: Trajectory-SAM: Object Trajectory-Guided Segmentation for Remote Sensing Videos
abstract: The rapid proliferation of high-resolution remote sensing video (RSV) has made object segmentation an increasingly critical yet challenging task. Existing methods face two fundamental limitations in this domain: (1) the intrinsic complexity of RSVs arising from diminutive object sizes, dense distributions, and drastic scale variations; (2) prohibitive computational overhead and latency caused by the massive spatial resolution of remote sensing imagery. To address these challenges, we propose Trajectory-SAM, a novel object trajectory-guided segmentation framework tailored for rapid and accurate object segmentation in RSVs. Specifically, we first employ a Graph Neural Network to extract representative keyframes, improving data utilization efficiency while suppressing attention drift and interpretation bias induced by redundant frames. We then introduce Temporal-LoRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy for the Segment Anything Model (SAM), substantially enhancing its spatiotemporal contextual understanding in remote sensing domains. Finally, we devise a sample-augmentation-based knowledge distillation strategy to accelerate inference without sacrificing segmentation quality. Extensive experiments on the SAT-MTB, iSAID, and VHR-10 datasets demonstrate that our proposed Trajectory-SAM achieves superior performance, establishing a compelling trade-off between accuracy and speed.

title: DCA-Net: Deep Context Aggregation Network for Remote Sensing Object Detection
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing scenarios faces multiple challenges, primarily manifested in multi-scale objects, class imbalance, densely packed small targets, and occlusion. To address these issues, we propose DCA-Net, an object detection method based on deep context aggregation. Built upon the YOLO architecture, the proposed method introduces parallel multi-branch pooling paths and an adaptive feature reweighting mechanism to construct a deep context aggregation backbone (DCA-Backbone). This enables efficient fusion and selective enhancement of multi-scale contextual semantic information. Furthermore, a detection head based on efficient channel interaction (ECI-Head) is designed to enhance the representational capability for multi-scale objects and complex morphological features. Experimental results demonstrate that DCA-Net achieves mAP50:95 of 50.5% on DIOR dataset and 61.5% on NWPU VHR-10 dataset, achieving competitive performance compared with other methods. Extensive visualization and ablation experiments further validate its detection accuracy and robustness in complex remote sensing scenarios.

title: PRIVER: Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-Scale Visual Evidence Reranking for High-Resolution Remote-Sensing Imagery
abstract: High-resolution remote-sensing images contain dense object layouts and fine spatial details, but their spatial extent makes direct vision–language interpretation difficult. Patch retrieval offers a practical alternative by returning local regions as candidate evidence for downstream interpretation. However, independent semantic scores can leave relevant patches at isolated ranks or return lists with substantial irrelevant content. We propose Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-scale Visual Evidence Reranking (PRIVER), a post-retrieval method for ranking patches within one image using controlled object-category queries. It aggregates four predefined prompt templates and combines semantic scores with geometric support, principally from a degree-normalized inter-scale graph. No encoder weights are updated, and retrieval and reranking do not access object annotations. Parameters are selected on annotated DOTA-v1.5 development data and held fixed. With relevance defined by annotated object coverage, Precision@10 on 458 DOTA-v1.5 internal-test images increases from 0.567 to 0.625 (absolute gain 0.058; 95% source-image cluster bootstrap interval [0.052, 0.065]). Normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank 10 (nDCG@10) increases from 0.647 to 0.730 and distinct-object coverage at rank 10 from 0.773 to 0.873. On a disjoint 526-image SODA-A subset, the corresponding metrics increase from 0.414 to 0.502, 0.445 to 0.550, and 0.467 to 0.681. Coverage-based gains persist with GeoRSCLIP and RemoteCLIP and under altered tiling policies on fixed image subsets. Inter-scale support is the principal source of improvement. These results support training-free, coverage-defined patch prioritization for within-image visual evidence retrieval.

title: The Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Agricultural and Rural Modernization: Spatial Spillover and Threshold Analysis
abstract: In developing countries, agriculture underpins sustainable rural transformation. Using a provincial panel for China covering 2014 to 2023, this study investigates the role of digital inclusive finance in advancing agricultural and rural modernization. The empirical results indicate that digital inclusive finance significantly promotes agricultural and rural modernization. This effect is more evident in major grain-producing areas and in provinces characterized by a relatively high degree of population aging. However, its spillover effects are asymmetric. While digital inclusive finance promotes local agricultural and rural modernization, it generates negative cross-regional spillover effects. Moreover, traditional financial coverage exhibits a nonlinear moderating effect, with the complementary role of digital and traditional finance becoming evident only after traditional financial coverage exceeds a single threshold. These findings highlight the importance of coordinating digital and traditional financial services and accounting for regional differences and spatial spillovers when promoting agricultural and rural modernization. They provide useful implications for developing countries seeking to strengthen inclusive financial systems and support sustainable rural transformation.

title: Jevolution: A Framework for Studying Communication and Collective Dynamics in AI Agents
abstract: Experiments with remote decision-making agents depend on more than the policy: the world may change during inference, the simulator determines which actions are available, and births and immigration alter who can act. We present Jevolution, an instrumented spatial predator-prey framework that makes these dependencies explicit. Its reference implementation separates the evolving world, asynchronous request scheduling, controller adapters, and experiment records. The model combines local observations, energy and resource constraints, predefined signals, and inherited scalar traits. We describe these mechanisms using the ODD protocol and distinguish implemented controls from research questions requiring additional interventions. Free synthetic fixtures exercise scheduling, signaling, and inheritance against the pinned implementation; they validate specified software behavior rather than model intelligence or ecological realism. A completed communication case study illustrates the end-to-end workflow using Jev to control both species. Across 6 complete habitat-seed pairs, the mean signals-on minus signals-off difference in normalized rabbit abundance was -0.0095 (nominal 95% pair-bootstrap interval [-0.0772, 0.0602]). This small study does not resolve the direction of the signal-system effect. The contribution is an inspectable experimental system and its evidence boundaries, not a new policy-learning algorithm or a demonstration of emergent language, adaptive selection, or biological predictive validity.

title: Quantum-Fisher-information-aware optimization yields a quantum reservoir advantage over tuned classical reservoirs
abstract: We show that a quantum reservoir computer optimized with its quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a quantum advantage over a classical reservoir of equal readout cost, provided by a quantum-information advantage: optimizing the quantum parameters with the QFI metric. On Mackey-Glass forecasting, a driven Jaynes-Cummings reservoir with one to three atoms beats a tuned echo-state network at every size from 4 to 30 trained weights, by 25-69% in held-out error, and is ahead of 99.5% of 10,000 random networks. After grid and Bayesian searches saturate, the QFI-aware stage lowers the error by 29-51% at 12-30 weights, beyond equal-budget black-box search or classical-parameter gradients alone, and at 30 weights turns a loss into a win. We then derive a fundamental QFI bound on the first-order rate of change of the retrained loss and factorize the gap to this bound into five link efficiencies that identify the physical mechanism limiting optimization.

title: Optimize Once, Execute Fast: Latency-Aware Multi-Agent Workflow Learning for Recurrent Queries
abstract: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-based MAS) have shown remarkable success in solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized agents through multi-step workflows. To overcome the high cost and specificity of manually designed workflows, recent research has shifted toward learning them automatically. However, a key limitation remains: while agent calls introduce significant latency due to model inference time and service congestion, most automated methods optimize solely for downstream performance, ignoring execution time (makespan). This issue is amplified when workflows are reused across recurring queries, making latency accumulate over time. This limits deployment in recurrent applications such as AI customer support and AI cloud troubleshooting, where users expect fast responses. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new problem, termed latency-aware workflow generation, where the objective is to minimize workflow makespan while aiming to retain downstream performance. We propose LAWA (Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion), a novel framework that reduces makespan via theoretically grounded graph edits targeting critical-path bottlenecks. By unifying a graph generator with this graph-editing procedure, LAWA supports both de novo workflow generation and refinement of existing ones. Empirical results across seven benchmarks demonstrate that LAWA significantly reduces makespan while achieving competitive task performance, supporting efficient reuse of multi-agent workflows for recurrent queries.

title: Names Are Not Objects: Object-Bound Confinement for Compromised AI Coding Agents
abstract: Coding agents read repositories and web pages that anyone can write, and then act with their user's authority. Prompt-injection defenses make it less likely that the model is steered but do not prevent it, so the system around the model must contain an agent that is already compromised. Many exploits against deployed coding agents share one cause: a check approves a name, such as a path, an argument vector, or a directory, and a later step maps that name to a different object: the file behind a symlink, the behavior an option selects, or a repository that git discovers on its own. We present Zero-Trust Agent Cells (ZTAC). A cell runs the agent in a kernel sandbox whose only route to files, programs, and the network is a socket to a broker. The broker resolves each request to the object it will act on, decides on that object, and checks at use that it is acting on the object it authorized. Programs that the broker starts run in a sandbox compiled from the same policy, and approvals are bound to the resolved object and can be used once. Our macOS prototype has 3.2k lines of trusted Rust code, excluding dependencies. We evaluate it against 74 attacks with ground-truth oracles, including replays of 10 publicly disclosed incidents. A tool allowlist loses 66 of them, and an allowlist combined with the kind of command sandbox that deployed agents use loses 56. ZTAC loses 2, both of which encode a secret into traffic to an allowed endpoint, and holds 14 for review. It completes 43 of 46 benign operations, with 8 approval prompts, and 4 of 7 workflows. A no-op brokered request has a median latency of 4.0 ms, and the spawned programs we measured take 8.5 ms to 18.4 ms longer than without ZTAC.

title: A Gated Catchment Hydrology Model (GCHM) for Physically-Interpretable Rainfall-Evapotranspiration-Runoff Simulation Across Diverse Hydroclimatic Regimes
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have improved rainfall-runoff prediction, yet most data-driven models remain difficult to interpret and do not explicitly enforce physical conservation laws. We present the Gated Catchment Hydrology Model (GCHM), a mass-conserving architecture based on the Mass-Conserving Perceptron (MCP). GCHM uses five storage states representing canopy interception, snow, soil moisture, groundwater, and streamflow generation. Constrained gates govern precipitation partitioning, evapotranspiration, infiltration, seepage, runoff, and baseflow while learning context-dependent process relationships. We evaluate GCHM across 50 CAMELS catchments spanning snowmelt-dominated, recent-rainfall, historical-rainfall, and arid regimes, using NOAA AORC meteorological forcing and remotely sensed vegetation and land-surface data. Performance is assessed using the Jawad-Kling-Gupta Efficiency (JKGE) metric, which accounts for stationary and non-stationary hydrologic behavior. We compare the full architecture with ablated variants and recurrent neural network benchmarks. GCHM reproduces streamflow dynamics across diverse hydroclimatic regimes, including arid catchments, while maintaining interpretable states and fluxes. Ablation experiments show that simplified architectures may perform adequately under wet conditions but struggle to represent flow persistence and recession during dry periods, when groundwater storage sustains low flows. Learned gates recover hydrologically plausible relationships governing snowmelt, runoff, seepage, and evapotranspiration. GCHM combines competitive predictive performance with mass conservation and interpretability, providing a foundation for hydrologic modeling and counterfactual analysis.

title: Consumption adjustment with mean-reverting risk premia: A singular stochastic control approach
abstract: We study a two-sided singular stochastic control problem in which changes in consumption carry utility costs and the risk premium follows the mean-reverting Kim-Omberg model. Optimal consumption is reflected between two moving barriers given by thresholds that depend on the current risk premium. These thresholds are the stopping boundaries of a Dynkin game for a two-dimensional diffusion driven by a single Brownian motion. A sharp occupation estimate shows that they are Lipschitz in logarithmic scale, uniformly in the cost of reducing consumption, and that smooth fit holds along the diffusion direction at every contact point. Outside a bounded interval of risk premia and at most two further points, the thresholds are infinitely differentiable. As the reduction cost grows, optimal consumption converges to the ratcheting policy.

title: DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments
abstract: Large-scale multimodal data are a key enabler for integrating large generative artificial intelligence models into wireless networks. However, existing wireless datasets offer limited support for heterogeneous environments, particularly in terms of reusable high-fidelity scenes, scalable differentiable ray tracing, and synchronized multimodal data. These limitations are more pronounced in mobile and aerial scenarios with time-varying environments and channels. To address these limitations, we propose DeepTelecom, a material-aware, high-fidelity multimodal channel dataset and reproducible generation framework for networks involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. DeepTelecom refines coarse indoor/outdoor reconstructions and uses a large language model to map segmented surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, yielding material-aware Level of Detail 3 digital twins. Then, a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across the sub-6 GHz/millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz bands, and specifically captures rotor-induced micro-Doppler signatures of stationary or moving UAVs at different pitch angles and translational velocities. The framework synchronously produces channel tensors, coverage maps, transmission videos, multi-view images, and weather-conditioned renderings, and supports differentiable material calibration from sparse channel anchors. The released dataset contains 10 material-aware indoor/outdoor scenes and 50,000 synchronized UAV samples; the framework supports scalable generation of additional data for user-defined scenes and system configurations. In 3D UAV localization, DeepTelecom reduces the 90th-percentile error from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with schemes considering only channel state information, demonstrating its significance for artificial-intelligence-enabled wireless systems.

title: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization
abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning has shown superior sample efficiency by leveraging the learned latent dynamics either in the form of derivative-free planning/imagined rollout training or dynamics gradient-based policy updates. While these approaches achieve comparatively fast learning, they all suffer, to varying degrees, from issues of recurrent compounding errors, high inference-time latency, and instability in backward propagation through time (BPTT). In this work, we propose a model-based RL approach that uses the chunk world model as a differentiable training-time evaluator to optimize the chunk actor without recurrent model invocation. Through the collaborative chunk-wise prediction of the world model and policy, we can generate H-step hypothetical rollouts in a single forward pass and directly optimize value expansion, avoiding the costly and unstable BPTT. We evaluate our method on 19 challenging high-dimensional humanoid tasks from HumanoidBench and deploy our method to the real-world for quadruped bipedal walking. Project Website: https://song-wx.github.io/cmpo.github.io/

title: Reward-Aligned Distillation
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but remains computationally expensive and sample inefficient. On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision from a stronger teacher, yet standard OPD distills every token regardless of whether the teacher's preference actually improves task reward. Existing token-selection methods rely on proxies such as uncertainty or teacher--student divergence, which need not identify reward-improving supervision. We introduce Reward-Aligned Distillation (RAD), a bilevel framework that weights distillation signals based on their predicted effect on the student's post-update reward. RAD differentiates through a temporary optimizer step to score each token's supervision, then updates the token weights by projected ascent from the initial token weights. The resulting weights can strengthen, suppress, or reverse individual distillation-gradient contributions. At a matched training-response budget, RAD improves mean accuracy on six competition-math benchmarks over the strongest baselines by 6.5 percentage points for Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and 2.5 points for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. RAD-Simple, a simplified variant, achieves comparable math accuracy at the same training-response budget. On LiveCodeBench-v6, RAD reaches 54.69\% and 58.67\% pass@1 with Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and OLMo3-7B-Instruct, respectively, exceeding the strongest baselines by 8.7 and 6.4 points. These results support reward-guided weighting of teacher supervision across model families and tasks.

title: Iterate on an LLM, Serve on an SLM
abstract: As frontier LLMs gain more capabilities, the cost to run them also goes up. At the same time, small language models (SLMs) also gain more capabilities but have largely been able to keep their cost stable, offering 5-40 times cheaper inference for the narrow, repetitive subtasks that agents decompose work into. However, the standing limiting factor is getting the correct behavior out of a small model in a fast, efficient, and economical way. Unfortunately, in most cases, zero-shot small models fail narrow production tasks. Furthermore, retraining one every time the behavior changes is too slow to iterate on. We propose doing both in sequence. First, develop the desired behavior in prompt space, on a frontier model, with immediate feedback from live traffic. Then, once the behavior converges, distill the recorded production behavior (not synthetic imitations of it) into an SLM through supervised fine-tuning (SFT). We show a proper use case of this method through a scheduling agent for home-care agencies that fans out a single yes/no safety decision per caregiver-shift pair on GPT-5.4-nano. A LoRA-tuned Qwen3-8B trained on 11.6k recorded production decisions reaches 0.913 agreement, while the teacher (GPT-5.4-nano), re-run on its own recorded prompts, agrees with itself only 72.7% of the time, pointing to the fact that the SLM may also be more consistent. Furthermore, when the two disagreed, a blinded professional scheduler sided with the student 48-29. Finally, we find that the SLM has approximately 2.5 times lower median latency and is a fraction of the cost. We believe this lifecycle of quick building, live feedback, and cheap inference is a blueprint for others building similar systems.

title: Tail Instability and Scale Control in Conditional Normalizing Flows for Treasury Yield-Curve Scenarios
abstract: A conditional normalizing flow can produce extreme scenarios even when its point forecasts appear reasonable. We compare two fitted models for daily Treasury yield changes at eleven maturities reconstructed from Federal Reserve curve parameters. Both use an LSTM, an auxiliary location head, and an affine residual flow. On a previously unused 60-date window, the frozen Student-t model generated an absolute standardized coordinate of 34.3 million. A Gaussian-base model with tighter coupling scale control reached 14.72. Each generated 600,000 vectors. The original model's scenario-mean MSE was 33,908.95, while its location-head MSE was 0.3376. The stabilized model's two estimates remained close. Across five development windows, the stabilized maximum was 17.33 among three million vectors. Stability did not imply better prediction: historical simulation had better distributional scores and coverage closer to nominal on the new window. The original flow also had a better log score despite its extreme samples. Frozen-model evaluation is reproducible, but the comparison does not isolate architectural effects or establish a general forecasting advantage.

title: EviScene: Beyond"Is It AI?"for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment
abstract: Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported. We formulate Image Factuality Assessment: given an image and a generic verification instruction, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with an evidence-grounded explanation. Without a supplied textual claim, the system must progressively refine factual questions during investigation and align external evidence with the specific situation depicted. We introduce EviLens, an expert-reviewed benchmark of 10,174 supported and refuted images from controlled construction and web collection, covering twelve factual error types and evaluating both verdict accuracy and evidence sufficiency. We develop EviScene, a multimodal ReAct agent that interleaves visual inspection, external retrieval, and evidence analysis, using new findings to refine its questions and revisit relevant image details. We train a compact policy with supervised fine-tuning on reviewed teacher trajectories, followed by privileged on-policy self-distillation applied to verified decisions from the policy's own investigations. On the 1,527-image test set, the trained Qwen3.5-9B agent achieves 79.05% balanced accuracy and a Strict Evidence Sufficiency Rate (SESR) of 52.26%, improving over the same-backbone base agent by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points, respectively. Its SESR is the highest among the evaluated agents.Code, models, and data will be released at https://github.com/wangzian828/EVISCENE and https://huggingface.co/ZiAnwang/EviScene.

title: From Rainfall to Road-Network Functionality: Transferable Graph Forecasting for Flood-Disrupted Transportation Networks
abstract: Extreme rainfall can rapidly degrade road-network functionality (RNF), disrupting emergency mobility, accessibility, evacuation, logistics, and infrastructure restoration. Existing flood-transportation impact models are often difficult to deploy across regions because they rely on local calibration, intensive simulation workflows or target-region retraining. This study proposes G-R2R, a transferable spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that reframes rainfall-induced road-network disruption as a region-conditioned, topology-flexible graph forecasting problem for unseen transportation networks. The framework integrates ego-centered subgraph sampling, terrain-conditioned graph representation, region-conditioned dual-level static encoding, and dynamic rainfall-network feature learning. Static geographic and infrastructure attributes are fused with rainfall forcing and recent RNF states to forecast node-level RNF across heterogeneous road networks. G-R2R is evaluated using simulation-derived RNF sequences from ten flood-prone regions in Wenzhou, China, under unseen-region testing protocols. It outperforms representative forecasting baselines, achieving a stabilized MAPE of 2.33% and $R^2$ of 0.855 under the fixed unseen-region benchmark. Leave-one-area-out evaluation yields stabilized MAPE values of 2.30%-3.54%. Ablation analysis supports the contributions of the terrain-conditioned graph representation and dual-level static encoding. A historical-event replay of Typhoon Fitow further shows that G-R2R reproduces principal temporal trajectories and node-level spatial patterns of the simulation-derived RNF reference under observed rainfall forcing without target-region retraining. These results support rapid and transferable node-level RNF forecasting across the regional road-network domains represented in this study.

title: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a route to AI systems that participate in their own continued development. Recent methods allow language agents to retain changes to their parameters, memory, skills, and code for subsequent execution and improvement. We examine how these methods can inform new research ideas through two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce a unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions organized into four groups: update targets, update organization, update schedule and scope, feedback and selection. This taxonomy places existing methods in a shared design space, where examining individual dimensions and their interactions can inspire new research ideas. Second, we examine how existing RSI methods draw on traditional deep learning, for example through optimization, regularization, data augmentation, continual learning, and adversarial learning. We develop further ideas by examining more specific learning mechanisms and drawing on evolutionary computation. We also review how existing benchmarks assess self-improvement under online, offline, and offline-to-online settings. Together, these perspectives help researchers develop new RSI research ideas from existing designs and learning mechanisms. RSI papers and resources are available at https://prism-shadow.github.io/awesome-rsi/.

title: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks. However, object hallucination remains a persistent challenge, undermining model reliability in applications such as visual question answering, embodied agents, and human-AI decision support systems. In this paper, inspired by cognitive science studies on perceptual bias, we investigate a new failure mode termed Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination (PVFH). Specifically, PVFH refers to a premise-induced reasoning error in which models become anchored to visually confusable evidence, accept a false textual premise, and subsequently generate responses about an absent yet visually plausible object. To systematically study this phenomenon, we introduce PVFH-Bench, a benchmark that automatically constructs visually confusable but absent targets and pairs the core hallucination setting with diagnostic subsets to trace how models move from object recognition to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Experimental results on 10 state-of-the-art LVLMs demonstrate that all evaluated models are highly vulnerable to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Moreover, we find that explicit chain-of-thought reasoning can further exacerbate this failure mode by encouraging models to overinterpret weak visual cues as supporting evidence for hallucinated objects.

title: Impact of Expertise and Trust on AI-assisted Work
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents promise to extend what users can accomplish beyond their existing expertise, but they also raise the risk of producing plausible-looking work that users may struggle to evaluate. We ask how task-relevant expertise and trust in AI shape agent-assisted work. To isolate these factors, we conduct a think-aloud study in which 20 professionals with varying data-science expertise use the same agentic tool to complete the same data-science hiring assessment, used at a major U.S. company. We find that surface productivity can come at the expense of understanding: participants who delegated more completed more of the task, but were also more likely to produce invalid solutions. Experts more often resisted this tradeoff, sacrificing completion to decompose the task and scrutinize agent outputs. Our findings call for evaluating agentic assistance not only by how much it accomplishes, but by whether users remain able to evaluate the work they produce.

title: Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based AI Scientists advance scientific discovery, yet they suffer from inefficiencies due to noisy observations. Existing principle-evolving agents act on every anomaly, leaving its source unresolved: a new mechanism or an evaluation artifact, so invalid revisions bias evolution. To address this, we formulate revision as evidence admission: anomalies steer search immediately, but only independently verified evidence may rewrite persistent principles, and contradicted principles are retracted. We realize this in TRIAGE-PIEVO , which pairs an anomaly-responsive search portfolio with a staged verification gate that alone controls what enters principle state. Across four scientific tasks with three backbones, TRIAGE-PIEVO (1) attains the highest average solution quality with +7.5%~11.8% over the strongest baseline per backbone, matching the strongest baseline's full-budget quality with one-third of the evaluation budget on Qwen3-235B; and additional stress tests and cross-harness deployment demonstrate that (2) in constructed stress tests, it admits none of the corrupted, hidden-source, or exploit evidence that ungated variants admit, while missing no planted mechanism, and (3) plugged unchanged into three external research harnesses, it cuts false evidence admissions by over 60% and raises verified scores by 31%~43%.

title: Understanding Hidden Spatial Preferences in Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Bayesian optimization uses posterior uncertainty to decide where to explore, but this uncertainty is not spatially neutral. On bounded domains, Gaussian-process posterior variance is typically larger near faces, edges, and corners, giving variance-based acquisition functions a systematic boundary bias. This spatial preference is usually inherited from the surrogate rather than chosen as part of the exploration strategy. We separate these roles by keeping the predictive model fixed and modifying the spatial preference of the exploration term. We control the preference with spatial weight fields and amortize their construction with neural surrogates. Controlled experiments show that the Gaussian process' default boundary bias changes which parts of the domain are explored and which optima are reached. We compare three alternative exploration principles and find, across standard benchmark functions and stochastic robot-pushing tasks, that they can often lower regret, particularly early in the optimization. The spatial structure of posterior uncertainty is therefore not a neutral default: it shapes the exploration strategy and can materially affect optimization performance.

title: Towards Merging-conditional Backdoor Unalignment against Large Language Models
abstract: Model merging has become widely adopted for enhancing the task-specific performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) without additional training. While the specialized model from third-party platforms may undergo safety audits (e.g., backdoor detection), we reveal a novel and critical threat: One-sided Merging-Conditional Backdoor (OMCB). OMCB remains dormant and undetectable within one standalone model but activates upon merging, triggering safety unalignment. We first theoretically analyze the existence and geometric location of OMCB, revealing that the parameter shift crossing safety decision boundaries is the main cause of backdoor activation. Building upon this insight, we propose SMOKE, a meta-learning-based attack framework. SMOKE implants OMCB via a bi-level optimization strategy: the inner loop synthesizes surrogate meta-vectors through random low-rank initialization and finite-step maximization, while the outer loop optimizes the target model by simulating the merging process. Furthermore, preliminary analysis shows that the injected OMCB has bounded generalization loss under unknown merging configurations. Extensive experiments across diverse model architectures and merging techniques validate the effectiveness of SMOKE and its resistance to existing backdoor detections, highlighting a significant yet previously overlooked vulnerability in the model merging paradigm.

title: Lingdan-V2: Large language models for clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine
abstract: Large language models have advanced medical reasoning, but clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains challenging because prescription decisions require integrating domain knowledge, syndrome differentiation, treatment principles, herbal prescription composition, and dosage determination. We develop a TCM language model family comprising models with 4 billion, 8 billion, and 14 billion parameters. The artificial intelligence contribution is a staged clinical alignment framework integrating large scale continued pretraining on TCM and clinical records, complementary reasoning supervision, and prescription-centered reinforcement learning (RL). We further formulate herbal prescription generation as a structured RL problem with prescription-level feedback, enabling direct optimization of clinical decision outputs beyond knowledge reproduction and generic instruction following. The engineering application is TCM clinical decision support, particularly herbal prescription recommendation. We evaluate the models on a public benchmark containing 25,620 expert-verified items across 13 TCM knowledge and clinical reasoning tasks and on a private retrospective dataset of 4,348 spleen and stomach disease prescription cases. The 14 billion parameter reinforcement aligned model achieves a prescription generation F1 of 37.0 on the public benchmark, compared with 32.3 for DeepSeek-R1 with 671 billion total parameters, and a herb-level F1 of 52.8 on the clinical dataset with improved dosage agreement. Reinforcement post-training consistently improves prescription recommendation across all scales, while physician-source analysis shows that expert heterogeneity affects reward stability. These findings demonstrate a scalable pathway from domain grounding and reasoning supervision to clinically oriented prescription decision support.

title: Amortised Global Sensitivity Analysis of Pharmacokinetic models for Simulated Clinical Trials
abstract: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models are used in simulated clinical trials to compare dosing protocols and patient groups before a trial is run. Distinct virtual patient cohorts, representing renal impairment, obesity and overdosage, can impose different input distributions on the same model. Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) identifies which uncertain inputs drive the cohort's predictions, but a direct analysis incurs its full computational cost for every cohort. An alternative accounting is proposed here: a single surrogate is trained on an input envelope wide enough to contain every cohort, each cohort is then analysed using that surrogate, and the reported quantity is the number of cohorts at which the surrogate route has cost fewer mechanistic evaluations than the direct route. The study tests three GSA methods: variance-based GSA, Morris screening and optimal transport. It covers four PK and PK/PD models with seven to twenty-three free inputs, 21 cohorts and five surrogates. Every estimate is scored against a converged mechanistic solution obtained with its own method, and all costs are expressed in mechanistic model evaluations. The parameter ranking is recovered at low cost: gradient-boosted trees reconstruct it on 20 of the 21 cohorts and cost fewer evaluations to train than one direct cohort analysis, on all four models, at break-even counts between 0.02 and 0.14 cohorts. Amortisation is fastest at the highest dimensions, where each direct variance-based sample of a $D$-input model requires $D+2$ evaluations while the training budget does not scale accordingly. Recovering absolute index values is harder, and fewer surrogates manage it as inputs grow: two of the five surrogates fail at fifteen inputs, where the gradient-boosted trees and the Gaussian process still succeed, and at twenty-three inputs no surrogate succeeds on a majority of cohorts.

title: No, Your Tools Are Not Enough: It's Time to Bring Agents to the Hunt
abstract: Modern software systems are large and complex, demanding scalable and autonomous techniques for vulnerability discovery. Existing approaches still depend on human expertise for domain knowledge, and on human intervention throughout the process of vulnerability discovery. AI agents offer us an opportunity to make vulnerability discovery more adaptive, scalable, and autonomous. Agents bring the ability to make continuous decisions and adapt, and general knowledge that can be augmented. In this paper, we present our experience using AI agents to find vulnerabilities across diverse programs such as Windows drivers, the Linux kernel, XNU, firmware, and web applications. We use an iterative agentic workflow and find that it generalizes across these targets.
