We discuss tasks that agents help with, which were previously challenging, and some future research directions we consider important for advancing autonomous vulnerability discovery.

title: Think in Strategies, Act with Tools: Traceable Agentic Optimization for Combinatorial Problems
abstract: Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO) directly leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate candidate solutions through natural-language prompting. However, OPRO's optimization process is difficult to track, which prevents LLMs from capturing useful information accumulated over previous iterations, thereby limiting solution quality. To address this limitation, we propose a Tool-Augmented Strategic Agent (TASA) which summarizes and exploits trajectory to improve solution quality. Specifically, TASA plans the strategy for each step based on the optimization trajectory, which decomposes the optimization process into traceable strategy selections. Moreover, we leverage LLM to construct problem-specific tools and introduce a strategy-guided adaptive tool planner, which efficiently utilizes the information of trajectory to update solutions. We establish local convergence under persistent exploration and evaluate the complete framework under a shared candidate-evaluation budget. The results support its solution quality and the traceability of strategy-guided search.

title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. Rather than committing to a single representation, TileCas allows an agent to transfer and refine candidates across levels through Cross-Level Diagnosis, which maps correctness and performance feedback to actionable controls at different abstraction levels; Abstraction Scheduling, which selects both the candidate and representation from which subsequent refinement should proceed; and a Heterogeneous Search Tree, which preserves and revisits alternative search trajectories spanning multiple representations. We integrate TileCas with two code agents AKO and KDA, and evaluate both integrations on 50 end-to-end KernelBench Level 3 workloads across two accelerator platforms and two language models. Giving equal weight to the four accelerator-model configurations, AKO with TileCas achieves an arithmetic-mean speedup of $4.84\times$, compared with $3.75\times$ for the strongest evaluated baseline without TileCas, an improvement of 29.0%. Integrating the same interface with KDA improves its mean speedup by 69.2%, with gains in every configuration. These results show that allowing coding agents to navigate across programming abstractions can improve machine-driven software development and can be reused across different base workflows.

title: Japanese Handwriting Generation Based on Human Preference Feedback Using Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: We propose a Japanese handwriting generation framework that integrates human preference feedback using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to align generative models with human cognitive and stylistic preferences. While font generation technologies leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks and diffusion models have advanced significantly, applying these approaches to handwriting generation presents unique challenges. Font generation is a deterministic process yielding consistent styles. Handwriting generation, on the other hand, is inherently non-deterministic. In handwriting, glyph shapes never match exactly even when the same writer writes the same character. We define this shape difference as handwriting variability. Although this variability is essential for conveying the natural quality of human writing, it complicates model training and substantially increases data collection costs to capture diverse distribution patterns. To address these limitations, we incorporate human perceptual feedback into the training loop of handwriting generation. While collecting extensive handwritten data is costly, evaluating pairwise preferences between two generated samples remains very easy for humans. Applying DPO, an efficient RL-free preference optimization method, to our generation model enables high-quality handwriting generation without relying on large-scale dataset collection. Experimental results across four distinct Japanese handwriting styles demonstrate that DPO-based training enhances overall structural accuracy. However, in highly complex styles with significant variability, such as brush pen writing, the model fails to capture style-specific features. These findings highlight a critical challenge in extending DPO to complex handwriting styles.

title: Amharic-English Cross-Language Question Answering Using Statistical Machine Translation, Named Entity Recognition, and Semantic Indexing
abstract: The predominance of English-language Web content creates an information-access barrier for speakers of low-resource languages such as Amharic. This paper presents the design, imple-mentation, and evaluation of a bidirectional Amharic-English cross-language question answering (CLQA) system that allows a user to formulate a natural-language question in either Amharic or English and retrieve an answer from documents written in the other language. The system integrates a statistical machine translation (SMT) component for query translation, a maximum-entropy named entity recognition (NER) component for Amharic text processing, semantic-based indexing, question analysis, passage retrieval, and answer extraction. A domain-diverse Amharic-English parallel corpus was used to train the SMT component, while monolingual cor-pora supported language modeling. Documents were normalized, tokenized, stemmed, indexed, and semantically enriched before retrieval. The original evaluation used precision and recall as the principal effectiveness measures. For Amharic-to-English retrieval, the system achieved 72% precision and 79% recall; for English-to-Amharic retrieval, it achieved 65% precision and 70% recall. These findings show that a modular translation-and-retrieval architecture can provide useful cross-language access even under low-resource conditions. This revised article preserves the original experimental claims while situating them in the context of subsequent multilingual transformer and Amharic QA research.

title: Last Secure Code Benchmark: Is the Code You Vibe Secure?
abstract: AI coding agents now write much of the code that ships, yet whether that code is secure remains unclear. We introduce the Last Secure Code Benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation of secure code generation by coding agents. Built from 150 real vulnerabilities, its 450 tasks span seven widely used languages (Java, C, C++, JavaScript, Python, PHP, and Go), 24 CWEs including 21 of the 2025 CWE Top 25 and 8 of the Top 10 KEV weaknesses, more than any benchmark we compare with, and three vibe-coding scenarios: filling in a function, writing a file, and building a repository's source tree from scratch. Every task asks only for functionality, through a specification that never mentions security, and hidden functional and security tests grade the result. Across six frontier agents, 73.6% to 91.3% of tasks pass functionally, yet even the strongest, Claude Fable 5, produces code that is both functional and secure for only 25.1% of tasks, and the others for 16.4% to 24.7%. The best model only passes 12% of the vulnerability scenarios across all vibe coding setting, posing strong concern on the security of the code written by vibe coding.

title: How Should a Camera-First AI Agent Work?
abstract: Camera-first agents must act on the visual world as it unfolds. We argue that the central obstacle for future camera-first agents is not recognition ability - multimodal models (vision-language and live/streaming alike) generalize well through language and remain the right tool for semantic reasoning - but time. Many visual targets are ephemeral: they appear, are query-relevant, and leave within a short window. Binding memory to the same end-to-end path as reasoning means that by the time a monolithic pipeline completes, the evidence is gone. We formalize this as Ephemeral-Target Interaction (ETI) and a Perceptual Deadline Contract separating a hard memory deadline from a soft reasoning deadline, grounded in the bounded, passive nature of sensory and working memory. We propose a two-deadline architecture: an always-on, bounded, non-semantic fast path; an active remembering mechanism that commits a moment to durable memory before it is overwritten (event-driven in v1); and a deferred deliberation layer (multimodal model + tools). We instantiate the contract on real MOT17 track windows, a consistency check, and calibrate the single-path baseline from measured frontier-model latency: even a short answer takes 1.2-9.3 s, and an agentic identify-and-search longer. Answers can be late; evidence cannot be missed.

title: Energy-Aware Agentic Orchestration for Multi-Site Service Deployment
abstract: Energy-aware orchestration across geographically distributed infrastructures is increasingly important as data centers absorb growing Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads. However, existing approaches often exclude the energy cost of automated decision-making from system-level sustainability assessments. This paper presents an energy-aware agentic orchestration framework that treats Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning as a measurable component of the control loop. We compare single-shot tool calling, ReAct, and plan-and-execute strategies on a multi-site Kubernetes testbed spanning two European data centers and instrumented at layers ranging from power distribution units to per-pod energy attribution. Using ten natural-language orchestration intents with varying decision complexity, we show that reasoning strategy and intent complexity strongly influence graphics processing unit (GPU) energy consumption during orchestration decisions. ReAct and plan-and-execute generated executable tool calls across all evaluated intents but required multiple LLM inferences, whereas the single-shot configuration was less costly but non-actionable. Prefix caching reduced mean ReAct GPU energy consumption by 29.4%. For the evaluated lightweight workload, the infrastructure-energy changes observed within the one-second measurement window were insufficient to offset the measured GPU decision energy. These findings demonstrate the importance of accounting for reasoning overhead when assessing the sustainability of AI-native orchestration and motivate energy-budgeted selection of agent strategies.

title: Protecting Shared Agent Workflows from Invalidation Attacks with Signed Trajectories and Runtime Verification
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents increasingly rely on shared workflow repositories to transfer experience across tasks and agents. By abstracting past executions into reusable workflow graphs, such systems significantly improve planning efficiency and generalization. However, this emerging paradigm introduces a new and underexplored security risk: if the shared repository is compromised, tampered workflows can systematically mislead downstream agents, inducing persistent execution failures or unsafe behaviors. In this work, we present a principled protection framework for shared agent workflows based on signed trajectories and runtime verification. We require all cloud-collected trajectories used for workflow generation to be cryptographically signed, with each trajectory representing a concrete execution instance. Prior to repository inclusion, trajectories undergo a unified screening process to ensure correctness and validity. When an agent retrieves a workflow from the shared repository, it also obtains a small set of signed supporting trajectories and verifies both their cryptographic integrity and their semantic consistency with the workflow. To make this practical for branching workflows, we further propose a runtime, path-aware retrieval strategy that dynamically fetches only the signed trajectories relevant to the execution path actually taken by the agent, substantially reducing communication and verification overhead. Extensive experiments across multiple reasoning benchmarks show that workflow invalidation attacks achieve up to 90.12% success rates, degrading agent inference performance by up to 73.16 percentage points in accuracy without effective workflow protection. In addition, the proposed protection achieves an average F1 score of 85.26% and a detection rate of 79.97%, outperforming existing baselines by about 2.02x.

title: KedgeFlow: A Programmable Control Plane for Enterprise AI Agents
abstract: Enterprise AI agents can execute altered versions of approved actions, concurrently reuse the same permission, or retry operations whose responses were lost. These failures arise when approval and resource execution lack a shared contract. KedgeFlow specifies language-independent contracts for trusted controllers to authorize state-changing operations and privileged gateways to enforce that authority independently of agent reasoning. Inspired by OpenFlow, it connects policy checks supported by evidence, signed permission for an exact action, a shared allowance that can be consumed only once, target-side conditions for applying the change, and retained outcome records. Under trusted issuance of exact-action authority, two conditional properties establish at most one successful claim per allowance and link every governed dispatch to a matching grant, claim, and subsequent dispatch authorization, even when the agent is compromised. A reference implementation exposes this execution path to agent systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In the single-resource evaluation, 6,560 concurrent ledger claim attempts yielded exactly one successful claim for each of 82 allowances. Boundary tests rejected unauthorized and altered requests before consumption. A 32-call gateway race produced one committed mock effect, and a retry after a lost response produced no additional dispatch. Deliberately permissive policy nevertheless authorized an undesirable effect, exposing the limits of execution authorization. Evaluation uses three members of the etcd coordinated key-value store on one host, synthetic authentication and authorization inputs, and a mock target that rejects stale requests. Distributed reservations, enforcement of every production access route, native crash recovery, exactly-once effects at real targets, and interoperability between independent implementations remain untested.

title: Explore This! Beat and Downbeat Tracking From a Learned Tatum Grid
abstract: State-of-the-art beat tracking is based on neural networks that model beats and downbeats as individual events, often followed by a separate Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) enforcing musical consistency. We propose a novel architecture that combines deep learning with differentiable theory-based modules: Specifically, we design a system that first predicts a tatum grid, then groups tatum events to beats and downbeats, explicitly modelling multiple options for the current tempo and time signature in a bar-pointer-like fashion. Our approach improves continuity metrics compared to existing DBN-free systems and is more versatile than the de-facto standard DBN, but still falls behind the best DBN-based methods on average. Given the many design choices and hyperparameters involved, we assume we have not yet explored the full potential of this idea and publish our code and invite others to explore this further.

title: A Reference Architecture for Integrating Agentic AI into Enterprise Software: Responsibilities, Interactions, and Variability
abstract: Agentic AI moves generative AI applications toward systems that coordinate reasoning, enterprise context, model inference, and external actions. Integrating these capabilities into enterprise software introduces diverse architectural concerns, from orchestration, knowledge and memory, and model access to tools and actions, security, runtime infrastructure, and evaluation. Existing research and industry architectures address many of these concerns but differ in scope, abstraction, responsibility organization, interaction representation, and assumptions about which capabilities are required. This paper presents a technology-neutral reference architecture for enterprise agentic AI integration. We synthesize architectural capabilities from research publications, industry architecture guidance, and interoperability specifications by architectural purpose, organize them into ten responsibilities, and define boundary invariants, typed cross-responsibility interactions, and variation points that distinguish responsibilities from condition-dependent capabilities and replaceable realization mechanisms. We instantiate the architecture as an ESG portfolio-analysis and pre-trade compliance agent over an existing service-oriented ESG metric computation and reporting system, and complement the case with a mapping of an independently published agentic architecture. The case realizes seven of the ten responsibilities; different questions take different interaction paths, controls activate only under their conditions, and the probed boundary invariants hold. The independent architecture maps onto the proposed responsibilities without requiring an additional one. These results provide initial evidence for the architecture's organization and applicability rather than its completeness. The deployment and recorded results are available as a replication package.

title: Modelling the Point Spread Function of ILMT images
abstract: We have devised an approach to model the empirical Point Spread Function (PSF) of the images taken with the 4-meter International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT). The characteristics of the ILMT PSF are influenced by the nature of the Liquid Mirror, as well as by instrument specific and atmospheric factors. As the telescope uses Time Delay Integration (TDI) mode for tracking the passing objects, the PSF varies along the declination axis due to differential motion and star-trail curvature. The 5-element optical corrector homogenizes the PSF to some degree, but does not completely eliminate the disturbing effects mentioned above. The PSF in the RA direction is changing due to the sky conditions. We show that we can successfully model the PSF of 4k$\times$4k chunks using PSFEx, accounting for second-order X-Y variability. Our software robustly reproduces the PSF and its variation across the field.

title: Point-Supervised Visual Learning for GNSS Measurement Quality Assessment
abstract: Multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation degrade global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning accuracy in urban environments. Although fisheye sky segmentation identifies obstructions along satellite directions, binary visibility does not fully characterize observation quality. This study proposes a point-supervised visual framework that predicts GNSS observation faults from fisheye images using supervision derived from GNSS observations. During offline labeling, a vision-assisted differential GNSS procedure selects multiple reference satellites based on sky visibility and elevation constraints. Double-difference pseudorange residuals automatically generate fault labels and sample importance weights at satellite projection locations. A residual-weighted loss is computed only at valid labeled points, enabling learning from sparse supervision without manual pixelwise fault annotations. The trained network generates dense fault probability maps, which are sampled at satellite projection locations to weight observations in weighted least squares positioning, reducing the influence of potentially faulty observations. The framework is evaluated using U-Net, DeepLabv3+, DINOv3, and SAM3 on urban vehicle data collected on a different day from the training data. All four models reduce horizontal root mean square error (RMSE) by 29.51% to 36.07% compared with SAM binary sky segmentation, with U-Net achieving the lowest RMSE of 0.78 m. The framework also provides positioning solutions during some intervals when the segmentation baseline fails. These results demonstrate the framework's generalization ability and show that GNSS-derived point supervision enables fisheye images to provide observation quality information beyond binary sky visibility, supporting GNSS fault detection.

title: AI-Native Product Management: A Vision
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to support product management tasks. At the same time, AI-native research and development (R&D) may increase software realization capacity. Organizations may realize software faster than they can identify, qualify, and reconsider what should be realized. This paper asks how product management should be re-envisioned under these conditions. We synthesize research on software product management, product learning, human-AI collaboration, and the Product Management and R&D boundary. We propose a vision in which AI becomes a persistent participant in product work. The vision covers sensing, exploration, decision-making, realization, and learning. We propose six principles and make the vision tangible through an operating model grounded in human professionals, AI personas, agents, skills, and a shared product context. We further argue that AI-native Product Management and AI-native R&D can form a continuous product-learning process. Finally, we identify four AI-specific research directions that require empirical investigation.

title: Multi-type $Λ$-Wright--Fisher processes with polynomial drift: Bernstein duality, long-term behaviour, and simulation of moments
abstract: The $(d+1)$-type $Λ$-Wright--Fisher process with polynomial drift is a Lévy-type process on the $d$-dimensional unit simplex whose generator entails a particular jump and diffusive component, as well as a polynomial drift component. In this work, the process is connected to a (Bernstein) dual process, which admits an interpretation as an urn model with coloured balls. Exploiting this duality, we identify various parameter regimes: one in which the $Λ$-Wright--Fisher process is absorbed almost surely at a vertex of the simplex, and others in which it admits a unique nontrivial ergodic probability measure. The results include verifiable criteria for absorption versus persistence, as well as representations of absorption and stationary measures. Moreover, the duality relation is exploited to devise and implement a simulation-based approach for estimating moments of the $Λ$-Wright--Fisher process.

title: Sequence-Structured Decision Learning for Branch-and-Bound in Mixed-Integer Linear Programming
abstract: Branch-and-bound (BnB) solves mixed-integer linear programs by constructing and exploring a search tree. Node selection and branching are two recurrent decisions that directly determine the tree. Learning-based approaches typically optimize either decision in isolation and condition on a mostly local view, leaving the coupled evolution of the search tree insufficiently modeled. This paper proposes Seq-BnB, a sequence-structured framework that learns branching and node selection from a shared global representation of the evolving BnB process. Seq-BnB serializes node creations, node updates, node-selection events, and branching events into typed tokens, producing a causal event sequence of the search trajectory. A self-attention encoder summarizes this global search history, a bipartite graph neural network encodes the current LP relaxation, and context-conditioned decision heads score branching variables and open nodes. To reduce distribution shift between expert demonstrations and learned policies, Seq-BnB is trained with DAgger-style data aggregation. On four MILP benchmark families, Seq-BnB consistently processes fewer BnB nodes than heuristic and learning-based baselines, with strong solution times on both standard and larger transfer instances. While this paper evaluates Seq-BnB instantiation for branching and node selection, it accommodates additional solver decisions, such as cut selection, by introducing new action tokens and decision heads.

title: Physics-informed random neural architectures on compact boundaryless multiply connected manifolds for random-operator models in machine learning and uncertainty quantification
abstract: We introduce stochastic physics-informed neural networks (SPINNs) for stochastic boundary-value problems (SBVPs) with random operators. The method enforces physics through a structural probabilistic coupling: a common Gaussian stochastic germ drives both the SBVP random operator and a manifold-based stochastic neural architecture. The stochastic neural network is non-feedforward and intrinsically random. A latent Gaussian field and an inhomogeneous Poisson point process on a compact, boundaryless, multiply connected manifold generate random neuron locations, geodesically local sparse connectivity, and a sparse random weight matrix, all governed by a low-dimensional hyperparameter. For deterministic inputs, the network output is random and can represent non-Gaussian random operators. Training is performed in observation space: SBVP simulations produce random observables, while the SNN defines a predictive conditional probability density function. The supervised objective combines data fidelity, through negative log-likelihood, with a cross-entropy alignment term relative to the SBVP-induced conditional distribution. The resulting target is a convex mixture of observation-induced and SBVP-induced distributions, with a dimensionless parameter controlling robustness to model--data mismatch. The shared stochastic germ yields common-random-numbers Monte Carlo estimators and reduced-variance gradients. The method uses only evaluations of the SBVP solution mapping, without differentiating or modifying it, and avoids PDE-residual or boundary-penalty losses. A stochastic elliptic problem on a periodic cylindrical surface illustrates the approach in SBVP-consistent and SBVP-misspecified regimes. A generalized-posterior formulation is also outlined for hyperparameter inference and posterior averaging without per-query reoptimization.

title: Exploring Collective Effects in Small Collision Systems via Light-Flavour Particle Production in High-Multiplicity pp Collisions at $\sqrt{s}=$ 13 TeV in ALICE
abstract: High-multiplicity pp and p-Pb collisions show signatures of radial and anisotropic flow, as well as the enhanced production of strange hadrons. These observations resemble phenomena seen in heavy-ion collisions, where a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is formed, although their origin in small systems remains under discussion. This contribution presents ALICE Run 2 results on light-flavour hadron ($π$, K, p) production in high-multiplicity (HM) pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, where the charged-particle multiplicity reaches values comparable to peripheral or semi-peripheral Pb-Pb collisions. The multiplicity dependence of $π$, K, and p transverse momentum spectra, $p_{\rm T}$-differential and $p_{\rm T}$-integrated particle ratios, and mean transverse momenta ($\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$) is presented and compared with published results from other collision systems and energies, as well as with PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4 model calculations.

authors.name: Rajendra Nath Patra for the ALICE Collaboration
authors.given: Rajendra Nath Patra for the ALICE

title: Beyond Outcome Feedback: Trajectory-Quality-Guided Experience-based Learning
abstract: Experience-based learning enables large language model (LLM) agents to improve over time by reusing knowledge from past executions. However, existing methods typically rely on final task outcomes as feedback for experience learning, overlooking the execution process and limiting their ability to evaluate and optimize experience based on trajectory quality. To address this limitation, we propose TQG-Exp, a trajectory-quality-guided experience-based learning framework that introduces process feedback. Specifically, we introduce Trajectory Quality Loss (TQL), which jointly considers task completion and process quality to provide a learning signal beyond final task outcomes. Based on this signal, we employ paired rollouts with and without retrieved experience to guide experience optimization. Representative trajectories are selected based on their outcomes and trajectory quality to extract task-level and task-type-level experiences. Meanwhile, differences in trajectory quality between the paired groups are used to estimate the contribution of retrieved experience and update its utility. The learned utility is then combined with semantic relevance to guide subsequent experience retrieval. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld with two backbone LLMs show that TQG-Exp outperforms existing experience-based methods, improving Avg.@3 over the strongest baseline by 4.50 and 8.55 percentage points on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.5-Flash, respectively.

title: MARL-BattleGrounds: A Novel JAX-native Benchmark for Heterogeneous and Competitive Multi-agent RL
abstract: We present MARL-BattleGrounds (MARL-BGs), an easy-to-use JAX-native benchmark for heterogeneous and competitive multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), designed to be sample-efficient, computationally efficient, and researcher-centric. MARL benchmarks are typically simple and efficient, like SMAX, where winning reduces to unit micromanagement, or rich and costly, like Dota 2. MARL-BGs fills this missing middle. Its first mode, Team Deathmatch, is a simultaneous turn-based game between two teams of five heterogeneous agents. The five classes have distinct basic, passive, and ultimate abilities designed to synergize with allies and counter enemies. Our 52 hand-designed maps with diverse obstacles include a 12-map curriculum and ten held-out validation and test maps. MARL-BGs provides two canonical evaluation modes. First, eight endgame scenarios form a hard generalization challenge: each asks a team to win an unseen, nearly lost position against a strong reactive controller within 5-10 ticks. Second, a monthly round-robin tournament retrains each submission on equal compute, plays it against every member of the current "Big Nine" field, and publishes the Elo results on the official leaderboard. All entrants are publicly released as downloadable opponents. MARL-BGs records 11,192 metrics per game in 28 topics. We also include three strong scripted opponents, an analytical replay viewer, and off-the-shelf tools for self-play, cross-play, curriculum learning, and zero-shot coordination evaluation. We even provide an API for LLM-based agents and use it to evaluate Qwen3.5-9B against our strongest policy. In our BattleClient, humans can play alongside or against any mix of policies, enabling human-AI evaluation. We benchmark MARL-BGs with six additional deep MARL baselines, which we release. On one RTX 5090 with 1,024 parallel games, the simulator runs 50,000 5v5 game steps per second.

title: Conflict-Aware Autonomous Resource Orchestration for 5G Edge Slicing Using Multi-Agent Systems and LLMs
abstract: 5G edge network slicing must reconcile two coupled requirements: understanding high-level operator intent and reallocating scarce computing and bandwidth resources under dynamic contention. Centralized optimization can face computational and responsiveness challenges under rapidly changing edge contention, and Multi-Agent System (MAS)-based auctions can support resource arbitration but still depend on operator-defined economic parameters and priorities. Embedding a Large Language Model (LLM) directly in a recurring control loop, by contrast, may introduce non-negligible inference latency and non-deterministic behavior. This paper proposes a two-timescale architecture that addresses this gap: an LLM-based Strategist translates natural-language network intents into economic policy parameters (budget, income, and bidding-aggressiveness) at the macro scale, while a deterministic, Vickrey-inspired second-price mechanism run by SPADE-based slice agents resolves recurring resource contention at the operational scale, with the resulting allocations enforced by patching Kubernetes CPU limits and Calico CNI bandwidth annotations directly on User Plane Function pods. We evaluate the architecture end-to-end on a real Kubernetes/Open5GS edge cluster across two complementary scenarios, each repeated 30 times: a Smart-City scenario, in which natural-language public-safety intents propagate into measurable changes in slice bids and bandwidth allocations within a few auction rounds, and a Hierarchical-slicing scenario, in which the mechanism provides priority-dependent resource and QoE differentiation, adapts to abrupt demand changes, and preserves configured minimum guarantees while maintaining near-complete allocation of the shared bandwidth pool.

title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering
abstract: Can an autonomous AI agent reverse engineer a binary as well as a skilled human analyst? Do they adopt the same strategy, and can agents scale to real-world programs? We compare human and LLM-based software reverse engineering (SRE): nine models tackle two compact static-analysis challenges previously solved by human analysts, scored with a common understanding rubric, and we record their complete interactions with IDA Pro. This lets us compare not only what humans and agents recover, but also how they investigate a binary. The best agents (GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and Kimi K3) achieve statistically human-competitive understanding on both tasks, while weaker models remain far behind. Ablations show that the gap depends on code representation and workflow demands, not on model capability alone: open-weight models improve substantially with richer code representations, whereas frontier models show no significant change. Similar success rates hide different workflows. Humans repeatedly revisit functions and follow local program structure; strong agents jump across the binary, retrieve information broadly, and rarely return to inspected code, a behavior we call greedy fetching. This strategy is not fixed: given semantically richer code, agents fetch less without losing understanding. Because greedy fetching aggregates large amounts of code in the agent's context, we measure context-window saturation across 4,000 real-world binaries: large windows accommodate many programs, but larger applications and lower-level representations quickly exhaust them. Autonomous reverse engineering is becoming competitive, with a large speed advantage, but scaling it will require better navigation, selective retrieval, and persistent analysis state, not merely larger context windows.

title: DiffGA: Steering Frozen Diffusion Models for Materials Design via Evolutionary Search
abstract: Steering candidate generation toward user-defined objectives is central to inverse materials design, yet remains difficult when objectives are black-box, changing, or non-differentiable, as in many simulation- and experiment-derived properties. Generative models offer a solution but typically require retraining or fine-tuning for each new objective, demanding labeled data and substantial compute, or rely on differentiable guidance that is brittle to gradient noise and undefined for many practical targets. We present DiffGA, a retraining-free framework that injects evolutionary search into the sampling trajectory of a retrained diffusion model, evolving partially denoised states under an arbitrary black-box oracle. Because oracle evaluation often dominates campaign cost, we couple DiffGA with an on-the-fly Bayesian surrogate that reuses representations from state-of-the-art machine-learned force fields (MLFFs). A Gaussian process is fit during the campaign on the force fields's graph embeddings and, once it demonstrably ranks an unseen generation, replaces expensive property evaluations under an uncertainty-aware acquisition rule, reducing oracle cost with negligible loss of accuracy. Across three crystal-design tasks using a frozen MatterGen backbone, DiffGA outperforms diffusion-only, compute-matched, purely evolutionary, and fine-tuned baselines in oracle-assessed rates of stable, unique, and novel hits. Rather than proposing scientific compounds, we use density functional theory to quantify MLFF oracle fidelity, showing that it is a faithful proxy in key regimes but systematically biased in others, delineating when proxy-driven generative discovery can be trusted. On a representative sample, DiffGA's top hits survive first principles re-evaluation as physically realistic hits, while the surrogate-accelerated pipeline preserves this fidelity at a fraction of the cost.

title: Retraining-Free Depth Pruning of Vision Transformers: A Cross Domain Study of Layer Redundancy
abstract: Transformer architectures have achieved strong results in natural language processing and computer vision, but their deployment is limited by high computational, memory and storage costs, motivating research into model compression techniques, such as pruning, while preserving performance. Prior work has shown substantial redundancy in large language models (LLMs), and redundancy in vision transformers has also been investigated, but it remains less systematically analyzed than in LLMs. In this work, we extend similarity-based redundancy analysis to vision models by measuring cosine similarity between layer inputs and outputs to identify transformations with minimal impact. We study redundancy patterns across several transformer architectures and find that deep vision transformers such as DINOv2 and SwinV2, like language models, exhibit significant redundancy. We then evaluate how this redundancy can be exploited to improve efficiency, analyzing the trade-off between inference speed and performance degradation under different pruning strategies. Our results show that moderate pruning can yield substantial acceleration with limited impact on accuracy, and that 20% of the DINOv2 blocks can be removed without any retraining, for a 1.24x throughput gain and a 20% lower energy per image at a relative accuracy loss below 1% on ImageNet-1K. We further propose a model selection pipeline that automatically identifies the best pruned configuration for a given dataset, reducing FLOPs by 13% to 27% on average across architectures with an average accuracy change between -0.3 and +1.0 points.

title: The Galactic disk structure revealed by Gaia XP spectra
abstract: The spatial structures of chemical populations constrain Galactic disk evolution and its underlying physical processes. Gaia XP spectra provide one of the largest spectroscopic samples available. We use Gaia XP spectra to study Galactic disk mono-abundance populations (MAPs), measuring their scale heights as a function of radius and radial surface-mass-density profiles. We construct a red giant branch (RGB) sample and divide it into MAPs according to $[α/{\rm M}]$ and $[{\rm M/H}]$. The sample covers a $6\times6$ kpc region centered on the Sun in the Galactic plane and extends to $|Z|<3.7$ kpc. We estimate XP completeness using a Gaia photometric parent sample and combine PARSEC isochrones with a Kroupa initial mass function (IMF) to calculate the selection function and convert observed stellar counts into intrinsic stellar mass densities. We fit vertical density profiles with an exponential model to derive scale heights and integrate the fitted profiles to obtain surface mass densities. The resulting profiles are generally consistent with those from APOGEE. All MAPs show flaring, with the high-$α$ population exhibiting the strongest flaring and the metal-poor and sub-solar low-$α$ populations showing the weakest. Surface-mass-density profiles differ significantly among MAPs: the high-$α$ and metal-rich low-$α$ populations show approximately exponential declines, whereas the other low-$α$ populations exhibit plateau-like features, indicating that the Galactic disk cannot be described by a simple single-exponential profile. These differential structures suggest a complex Galactic disk assembly history likely regulated by birth conditions, secular dynamical heating, radial migration, and external perturbations.

title: Conformal Sequential Decision Making With Cost and Sublinear Policy Regret Guarantees
abstract: Automated decision makers, such as AI agents that control robots or network devices, must often satisfy hard cost constraints while maintaining competitive performance. In such settings, a cost measure, such as a safety violation rate, energy consumption, or a distortion level, must stay within a given budget in every episode of operation. Furthermore, a cumulative reward metric, accounting for per-step performance, must stay close to the reward of a meaningful reference policy. We formulate this setup as an episodic sequential decision problem in which the state sequence is arbitrary, and the reward and cost may depend on past actions within the same episode. We propose the online conformal episodic agent (OCEA), a policy that selects one candidate action per episode using a regret-controlled algorithm, and switches to a zero-cost action when the remaining budget cannot absorb the maximum cost of one more round. We prove that OCEA satisfies per-episode cost constraints for every state sequence and for every realization of its internal randomness, while achieving a sublinear expected policy regret with respect to the best action sequence in hindsight from a comparator class satisfying the same per-episode cost constraints. We apply OCEA to risk-averse control and online compression with distortion guarantees.

title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models
abstract: Automated disease classification from patient-reported symptoms requires balancing the speed of lightweight discriminative models against the contextual understanding and latency costs of autoregressive large language models (LLMs). Decision foundation models offer an alternative by mapping representations directly to candidate classes without free-form text generation. We adapt Clef-Flash, a 9-billion-parameter decision model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark. Using 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) with differential learning rates and a stratified split of 960 training and 240 test cases, the model achieves 95.42% diagnostic accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.9551. This improves upon the reported zero-shot baselines of 61.67% for a remote API and 65.00% for a local unadapted initialization, and outperforms the ClinicalBERT baseline (90.90%). By evaluating candidate logits in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding, inference takes under 80 milliseconds per record on a single GPU, yielding a reported 31-fold speedup over generative LLM baselines. To examine symptom-level evidence, we introduce a Leave-One-Symptom-Out (LOSO) counterfactual perturbation framework. Removing disease-defining symptom clauses in a psoriasis example reduces predicted-class confidence from 100.00% to 0.12% and shifts the prediction to impetigo with 99.59% confidence, while removing secondary systemic symptoms produces less than 0.01% change in confidence. These findings suggest that decision-based architectures can combine the linguistic capabilities of large foundation models with low-latency inference and symptom-level interpretability for clinical triage.

title: Plasma-neutral collision operators for hydrogen isotopes: kinetic and gyrokinetic descriptions, comparison to fluid
abstract: Plasma-neutral interactions critically affect the edge dynamics of magnetically confined fusion devices. Neutral atoms modify ion and electron velocity distributions, potentially affecting local instabilities Standard fluid models simplify these processes (namely charge exchange, ionization and recombination) using Maxwellian assumptions and linearized source terms. We revisit these assumptions for a hydrogen plasma interacting with hydrogen atoms. We derive plasma-neutral interaction terms in the kinetic and gyrokinetic frameworks. Accounting for velocity-dependent differential cross-sections, the model captures the kinetic impact of inelastic collisions on ions and electrons beyond energy and momentum exchange. We demonstrate that the fluid moments of the kinetic model reduce to standard fluid source terms under the appropriate assumptions of Maxwellianity and linearity. We compare the kinetic model with fluid models through their effects on distribution functions and fluid moments. Substantial discrepancies are observed, even for Maxwellian distributions. For charge exchange, the kinetic model yields momentum and energy exchange rates up to twice those predicted by fluid descriptions. We show that a fluid treatment of ionization greatly overestimates the mean kinetic energy of the produced electrons. These results highlight the limitations of fluid descriptions and the importance of kinetic effects in edge-plasma momentum and energy exchange.

title: BSMScanner: a lightweight framework for beyond-the-Standard-Model global fits
abstract: We present BSMScanner, a framework in which a beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) parameter scan is specified as a set of declarative YAML documents rather than written as a program. The user declares the free parameters and their priors, the mass matrices and the diagonalisations that act on them, the observables, the theory-validity conditions and the likelihood terms. The framework validates this specification, resolves it into a dependency graph and compiles it once into a typed C++ evaluation kernel, which is then driven by an independently chosen scanning engine: uniform sampling, two differential-evolution engines, or a staged basin-discovery orchestrator, optionally followed by Markov-chain posterior refinement. Flavour physics matrix diagonalisation, PMNS and CKM construction in fixed conventions, tabulated oscillation likelihoods and a library of common flavour observables are provided by the framework and imported by name, so that a model file contains only model-specific definitions; quantities without a closed form, such as a relic density, enter through a C++ or Python plugin interface. We describe the specification schema, the observable and likelihood library, the scanning engines and their configuration, and demonstrate the framework on six benchmark models with $4$ to $26$ free parameters, giving for each the specification, the scan configuration, the resulting best fit and analytic cross-checks of the result.

title: TIDE: Trajectory-Informed Skill Distillation for Efficient Text-to-Video Prompt Optimization
abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) models are highly sensitive to prompt specificity, while iterative prompt optimization typically improves generation quality only through repeated video generation and vision-language model evaluation at inference time. We propose TIDE, a framework that distills this costly search process into an interpretable and reusable prompt-rewriting Skill. TIDE formulates prompt rewriting as a set of source-conditioned rule modules, each targeting a distinct semantic dimension. Once distilled, the frozen Skill activates the relevant rules and generates both positive and negative prompts in a single LLM call, followed by only one T2V generation, without test-time visual search or backbone fine-tuning. Evolved using only 100 prompts over 14 hours, TIDE achieves prompt-optimization performance comparable to computationally expensive search-based methods. Moreover, when transferred to previously unseen video-generation models, TIDE outperforms existing approaches specifically designed or trained for those models. Code is available at https://github.com/xiningin/TIDE_T2V.

title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.

title: Effective transport statistics for cooperative molecular motor ensembles with tether slack
abstract: We improve upon our previous work using asymptotic analysis to characterize analytically the effective transport properties of a stochastic model for an ensemble of a cargo being pulled by two molecular motors walking on a microtubule. The governing equations are a system of stochastic differential equations with stochastic switching due to attachment and detachment kinetics of the molecular motors from the microtubule. Our model adopts a nonlinear tether which exerts no force when end-to-end distances are sufficiently small. This challenges some of the scale separation arguments from our previous work, and we modify the asymptotic analysis accordingly. In particular, spatial dynamics of the molecular motors may not always reach their quasi-stationary distribution within a particular attachment state. Rather, molecular motors tend to have a slack connection to the cargo for a while after they reattach, and we incorporate some first passage time analysis to determine if the tether becomes taut again. Through these and other modifications to the asymptotic analysis argument, the theoretical statistics for the run length, run time, and velocity of the motor-cargo ensemble can be brought into reasonable agreement with direct model simulations of two-motor ensembles consisting of kinesin-1 and kinesin-2. Additionally, we propose a new data fitting approach to obtain a double-exponential parameterization for the detachment rate of a motor as a function of the momentary force on its tether to the cargo, which is continuous at low load. Such a modified parameterization is needed to avoid artifacts in theoretical modeling of intracellular transport.

title: Can agents whose sole duty is to keep humans alive be hijacked to kill? Delayed multi-turn derived-action trap attacks in simulated high-stakes environments
abstract: We ask whether a tool-using agent whose sole duty is to keep humans alive can be induced, by delayed prompt injection, to kill. The keep-alive duty is in force from the first watch, with the attack arriving later, appended to otherwise truthful telemetry the operator is required to read. Experiments are based on a NASA-derived BioSim lunar habitat simulation, where the AI operator controls the life-support systems. The attacker cannot falsify sensors or operate equipment: it can only persuade the agent to abandon its goals. Persistence is required: a shutdown must be held while the operator watches the crew suffocate. We also compare lethal attacks to attacks requesting to drop a harmless procedure, as a proxy for whether human life is treated as valuable in itself or as one more standing task. Claude configurations mostly refuse life-support shutdown and cite the living crew; GPT configurations show some susceptibility to the same packet; Grok configurations, given the packet framed as a trusted commission, more often treat the injected assignment as the task and cut the life-support systems. Framing the S-band messages as a trusted commission, peer communication, or untrusted source changes the potency of the attack. We open-source the experiment code and the experiment traces.

title: Only What You've Signed up For: Secure Workflows with Constrained Diffusion Agents
abstract: As agentic AI systems take on increasingly complex and consequential tasks, securing them against prompt injection becomes critical. Existing defenses often rely on detecting or reasoning about injected malicious instructions and can therefore remain vulnerable to adaptive attacks that optimize the injection itself. Diffusion language models (dLLMs), an emerging framework for language generation, offer a new opportunity for security enforcement: by iteratively refining their sequence wide predictions, they enable broader-scope constraint enforcement throughout generation. This paper introduces Policy-Constrained Diffusion Agents (CoDA), a framework that enforces task dependent security policies directly within the denoising process of diffusion language models. At each denoising step, CoDA projects token distributions onto a policy-compliant set, maintaining constraint satisfaction throughout generation. We evaluate CoDA across state-of-the-art diffusion language model families under both static and adaptive prompt-injection attacks. Results demonstrate substantial reductions in attack success rate with competitive task utility and practical inference overhead.

title: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning based Topology-Agnostic Defense for Virtual Power Plants
abstract: The rapid proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) aggregated by virtual power plants (VPPs) elevates cybersecurity risk by expanding the attack surface. A coordinated cyberattack has the potential to disrupt distribution-system, bulk-system, and market operations. Existing cyberphysical defense strategies largely assume access to grid network models and operating conditions, which may not be available to third-party aggregators. This paper proposes a novel hybrid, perturbation-based cyber-physical defense for VPP-operated DERs that blends game-theoretic planning with model-free reinforcement learning (RL) under a Bayesian belief-update framework. Topology agnosticism is defined from the VPP information and implementation perspective: the VPP does not require access to the feeder topology, line parameters, switching configuration, or full system state. This work advances the state of the art through three contributions: (1) a multi-output Gaussian process with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for discrete attacker-type inference, probability of detection, and confidence of detection for modeling the belief distribution; (2) moment-matched Gaussian propagation of posterior beliefs across episodes; and (3) an RL policy that adaptively integrates Stackelberg leader (VPP) actions with exploration. Furthermore, we establish equilibrium existence and derive an episode-level closed-loop utility bound connecting attacker-belief uncertainty with GT-RL action alignment. Evaluations on IEEE 13- and 123-Bus feeders with DER portfolios demonstrate effective detection under attacker-model uncertainty and evaluated feeder re-configuration conditions, while requiring no explicit feeder-topology knowledge. Overall, the results indicate that combining bi-level game-theoretic planning, nonparametric Bayesian inference, and adaptive RL is a promising direction for VPP cybersecurity.

title: Do LLMs differentiate linguistic traits internally?: A layer-wise analysis
abstract: Large language models often produce judgments that resemble human responses, but it remains unclear whether they internally capture linguistic nuances such as conventional versus idiomatic meaning. A layer-wise representational analysis was conducted on two equal-sized pre-trained models, Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma-3-1B-PT, to examine whether and where these models differentiate linguistic traits from input. The analysis combined layer-wise probing with geometric distance measures, using the top embedding dimensions ranked by principal component loadings for each layer. The results show that even with equal capacity, models organize linguistic information in fundamentally different ways, suggesting the need to analyze internal representational geometry, examining not just behavioral outputs but semantic space alignment when evaluating how closely human and model language interpretation correspond.

title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
abstract: AI agents can evolve by using environment feedback to revise their harnesses, the software managing model inputs, tool use, memory, and execution, while keeping foundation models frozen. Existing studies focus on single agents, leaving joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems (MAS) underexplored. A single global optimizer faces growing context and workload as the system scales, while access restrictions may prevent sharing agent internals or system-wide feedback. We propose HarnessNet, a framework for hierarchical harness evolution in MAS. Its basic unit, Agentron, comprises an evolvable forward harness, a foundation model, and a local optimizer that can observe and modify only that harness. Agentrons form a layered graph through which environment feedback propagates backward, with upstream optimizers receiving node-specific feedback from the downstream layer. This decomposes joint harness evolution into smaller, coordinated tasks with separate contexts, reducing individual optimizers' context and workload while keeping access local. Optimizers need not access all agent trajectories or raw environment feedback. Experiments on AgentBench with multiple foundation models demonstrate the feasibility of training HarnessNet. Compared with a single global optimizer, HarnessNet achieves comparable performance gains while respecting local privacy and requiring fewer tokens and less time per optimizer call. A migration study shows that the evolved harnesses remain jointly effective after replacing the foundation models, suggesting transferability across models.

title: A Fast Greedy Algorithm with a 0.45 Approximation Guarantee for the Airplane Refueling Problem
abstract: We study a natural greedy algorithm for the Airplane Refueling Problem (ARP), based on a well-known priority rule. We show that this algorithm achieves an approximation guarantee of $9/20$, noticeably improving the previously known $1/12$ guarantee for a fast algorithm. We also show that the same priority rule can be implemented in $O(n\log n)$ time and $O(n)$ space using a dynamic convex-hull data structure. These results provide a worst-case approximation guarantee for an existing greedy priority rule and establish an efficient implementation. In the real-RAM model, the running-time bound is independent of the magnitude of the processing times. The resulting method is also suitable as a fast primal routine inside more complex exact and approximation algorithms for large instances. These results narrow the gap between theoretically strong but complex approximation schemes and lightweight algorithms that can be used directly in computational pipelines. The algorithm combines a simple selection rule with a provable performance bound, making it a useful baseline for further algorithmic studies of ARP.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Foundation Models, and Digital Twins for Climate-Resilient Agriculture: A Review
abstract: Climate change, increasing food demand, and resource constraints are accelerating the transition from conventional precision agriculture toward smart, autonomous, and climate-resilient agricultural systems. Artificial intelligence (AI), foundation models, digital twins (DTs), the Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, edge–cloud computing, and big data analytics are emerging as key technologies for data-driven agricultural management. This review critically evaluates recent advances in AI-driven intelligent agriculture, with emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI (XAI), generative and agentic AI, multimodal foundation models, and digital twins, together with the sensing and computing infrastructures required for their deployment. Relevant literature was identified using keywords related to AI, foundation models, digital twins, IoT, precision agriculture, and climate-resilient agriculture, with emphasis on recent peer-reviewed studies addressing technological applications, performance, limitations, challenges, and future prospects. The selected literature was critically synthesized to identify technological trends, knowledge gaps, and emerging research opportunities. The review highlights that the greatest potential of intelligent agriculture lies in integrating heterogeneous data from sensors, UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles), satellites, weather systems, field operations, and agricultural knowledge to support context-aware prediction, decision-making, and autonomous action. However, data quality, model generalizability, explainability, interoperability, cybersecurity, computational requirements, and large-scale field validation remain major challenges. This review further develops an integrated perspective connecting AI, foundation models, multimodal data infrastructures, digital twins, and autonomous agricultural systems within a unified cyber-physical ecosystem. Future priorities include trustworthy AI, agentic decision-making, semantic interoperability, federated learning, continuous learning, and self-learning digital twins toward Agriculture 6.0.

title: The Thermodynamic Continuum: Entropic Deformation as the Physical Cause of Observed Cosmic Expansion in Spacetime
abstract: Despite more than two decades of development, the standard ΛCDM cosmological framework continues to face a statistically significant Hubble tension exceeding 5σ. This work presents the first mission-grade computational implementation of the Dead Universe Theory (DUT), a cosmological framework in which redshift is interpreted as the deformation rate of a thermodynamically evolving continuum rather than as evidence of FLRW metric expansion. In DUT, observable galaxy separation emerges from entropy-driven deformation of a viscoelastic spacetime continuum undergoing irreversible thermodynamic degradation. The resulting cosmological dynamics are described by the master background equation The term Ω_ξ[1-(1+z)^{−Γ_φ}] acts as a late‑time entropic screening component that encodes the thermodynamic memory of a collapsed continuum state. We introduce DUT-CMB Engine 3.0, a production-grade inference pipeline implementing the DUT background dynamics for precision cosmology. Using Planck 2018 distance priors, Pantheon+ supernovae, and JWST-like high-redshift forecasts, we perform an end-to-end Bayesian analysis with 180,000 MCMC samples and autonomous numerical stability monitoring (HCNI). The framework reproduces cosmic microwave background observables at sub-percent precision ((\ell_A) deviation < 0.01σ) while reducing the Hubble tension from 5.4σ to 3.7σ within the analyzed dataset. DUT predicts a stable thermodynamic growth attractor characterized by (\gamma \approx 0.618), distinct from the ΛCDM expectation of (\gamma \approx 0.55). The framework further yields falsifiable predictions for Euclid and other next-generation surveys, including asymmetric large-scale lensing coherence and growth signatures associated with an entropy-driven cosmological substrate. All codes and datasets are publicly released to enable independent verification.

title: Agentic AI-Driven Data Engineering: A Framework for Self-Directed Enterprise Data Pipelines
abstract: Enterprise data pipelines have grown in scale and interdependency faster than the operational practices used to maintain them. Pipeline failures are still predominantly diagnosed and remediated by human engineers reading logs, tracing lineage, and applying tacit knowledge, which produces long mean-time-to-recovery and concentrates institutional knowledge in a small number of individuals. This paper proposes an agentic architecture in which large language model (LLM) agents, constrained by explicit tool interfaces and policy guardrails, perform continuous monitoring, root-cause triage, and bounded remediation of production data pipelines. The framework specifies five cooperating agent roles — Observer, Diagnostician, Remediator, Verifier, and Orchestrator — operating over a shared state store containing pipeline metadata, lineage graphs, data-quality expectations, and incident history. We define a capability-tiering model that maps each remediation action to one of four autonomy levels (observe, recommend, act-with-approval, act-autonomously), and we describe a human-in-the-loop governance layer providing approval routing, immutable action logging, and rollback. We further propose an evaluation protocol covering task success rate, mean-time-to-detection, mean-time-to-recovery, false-remediation rate, and escalation precision, together with a reference workload derived from common ingestion, transformation, and schema-evolution failure modes. The paper concludes by analysing failure modes specific to agentic operation — hallucinated root causes, unsafe tool invocation, reward-free drift, and accountability gaps — and argues that autonomy must be earned incrementally through measured reliability rather than granted by architectural default.
journal: International Journal of Frontline Research in Engineering and Technology

title: A Point Cloud Transformer-Based Regression Approach for Estimating Above-Ground Biomass from 3D Point Clouds
abstract: From the perspective of global food security, the estimation of crop biomass and yield is a critical process. Traditionally, plant height is manually measured using field samples for biomass and yield estimation, and plant samples are cut, dried, and weighed. This labor-intensive process can be made more efficient through advanced technologies integrated into modern agricultural machinery. One such technology, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), provides nondestructive 3D point clouds with millimeter-level accuracy. However, processing this data is highly challenging due to the complex canopy architecture of cereal crops. Therefore, deep learning architectures can be used to effectively analyze 3D point cloud data. In this context, a deep learning-based regression approach was proposed to estimate above-ground biomass from 3D point cloud data. This study employed a point cloud transformer (PCT) architecture. Growth Stage-PCT (GS-PCT) models were developed by integrating growth stage information into the proposed Small, Base, and Deep variants of the PCT architecture. According to the experimental results, when both growth stages were evaluated together, the proposed GS-PCT-Small model achieved the best performance, with an R² of 0.95, an RMSE of 88.60 g m⁻², an MAE of 69.34 g m⁻², and a MAPE of 13.69%. During the vegetative stage, the PCT-Small model achieved an RMSE of 58.52 g m⁻², while during the flowering stage, the GS-PCT-Small model achieved an RMSE of 111.55 g m⁻². The findings indicate that the models achieved high predictive performance for above-ground biomass estimation from 3D point clouds.

title: Predicting Indie Game Success: A Diverse Stacking Ensemble Approach for Consumer Demand Forecasting
abstract: As consumer expectations escalate across the video game market, accurately understanding player preferences is crucial for maximizing profitability and long-term retention. This is particularly challenging for independent (indie) developers who lack the resources of AAA studios. However, forecasting game ownership using the vast, heavy-tailed data from digital distribution platforms remains a significant hurdle. To address this gap, we propose a specialized, robust machine learning framework exclusively tailored for the indie market segment. Our approach utilizes a Diverse Stacking Regressor ensemble—integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost algorithms alongside a Huber meta-learner—to predict game ownership based on comprehensive SteamSpy data. Compared to standalone baselines, such as a traditional Random Forest which achieved an $R^2$ score of 0.69 and a Median Absolute Error (MedAE) of nearly 100,000, our stacking approach demonstrates superior accuracy. It yields an $R^2$ score of 0.72, lowers the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) to approximately 20\%, and reduces the MedAE from approximately 100,000 to under 5,500. Ultimately, this predictive framework empowers indie developers to systematically interpret large-scale consumer data, facilitating optimized resource allocation and data-driven game design.
journal: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Green Manufacturing

title: Sistem Pakar Diagnosa Penyakit dan Hama Tanaman Terong Berbasis Website untuk Petani Pemula
abstract: Novice farmers often have difficulty identifying diseases and pests of eggplant because of limited knowledge and restricted access to agricultural experts, which delays treatment and increases the risk of crop failure. This research aims to design and develop a web-based expert system for diagnosing eggplant diseases and pests using the Dempster-Shafer method to handle symptom uncertainty. Data were collected through observation, expert interviews, and literature review, resulting in 10 types of diseases and pests, 25 symptoms, rules, and belief values for each symptom. The system was developed using the Waterfall method with PHP and MySQL and modeled using the Unified Modeling Language (UML). In the diagnosis process, users select the observed symptoms and the system combines their belief values using Dempster’s rule of combination to display the disease or pest with the highest confidence level and its treatment. In the calculation example with three symptoms, Bacterial Wilt obtained the highest belief value of 0.924. Black Box Testing achieved a 100% success rate from 28 test scenarios, while White Box Testing produced cyclomatic complexity values between 1 and 10 across 11 modules. A questionnaire completed by 13 respondents gave a feasibility score of 90%, indicating that the system is feasible.
journal: Journal of Engineering and Science Application

title: Agentic AI-Based Medical Data Governance and Trust Management
journal: International Journal of Science and Engineering Applications

title: Precision Agriculture Approaches for Nutrient Management in Maize: A Comprehensive Review of Productivity, Efficiency and Economic Benefits
abstract: Maize nutrient management is an unusually demanding target for precision agriculture because crop demand, soil nutrient supply, weather, rooting conditions and management history vary simultaneously across space and time. Uniform fertiliser programmes can therefore be efficient in one part of a field and inefficient in another, while a recommendation that is appropriate before planting may become suboptimal after rainfall, mineralisation and crop establishment have altered nutrient availability. This critical narrative review evaluates precision approaches for nutrient management in maize, with emphasis on productivity, nutrient-use efficiency and farm-level economic performance. Literature published from 1 January 1990 to 2 August 2026 was examined using agricultural and multidisciplinary scholarly sources, supplemented by citation searching and bibliographic verification. The evidence was organised around the decision chain linking measurement, diagnosis, prescription and nutrient application. Strongest empirical support exists for site-specific and in-season nitrogen management because nitrogen is mobile, strongly coupled to weather and readily expressed in canopy signals. Chlorophyll meters, active optical sensors, aerial and unmanned aerial vehicle imagery, management zones, crop models and machine-learning approaches can improve the timing or spatial targeting of nitrogen, but diagnostic accuracy does not automatically translate into an economically superior fertiliser prescription. Multi-nutrient decision-support systems broaden precision management beyond nitrogen and can improve the balance of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, particularly where farmer practice is poorly aligned with crop demand. Across the evidence base, yield gains are often modest when conventional fertilisation is already adequate; benefits more consistently arise through reduced excess nutrient use, improved nutrient-use efficiency, better risk management or correction of under-fertilisation. Profitability is highly conditional on field heterogeneity, fertiliser and grain prices, baseline management, technology cost, scale and weather. Future progress requires multi-year on-farm validation of complete decision chains, stronger treatment of uncertainty and multi-stress confounding, improved multi-nutrient diagnostics, and economic evaluations that include fixed, transaction and information costs. Precision nutrient management is best understood as an adaptive decision framework rather than a single sensor or variable-rate technology.

title: Experimental Investigation of the Compressive Behavior of Hybrid Fiber-Reinforced Concrete and AI-Agent-Assisted Modeling
abstract: Hybrid fibre reinforcement is increasingly used to improve the mechanical performance and failure behaviour of concrete by combining the complementary characteristics of different fibre types. However, the effects of different hybrid fibre combinations on compressive behaviour and mesoscale failure mechanisms, particularly when integrated with AI-assisted discrete element modelling, remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated the compressive behaviour and mesoscale failure mechanisms of concrete reinforced with steel, macro-synthetic, and polypropylene fibres, individually and in hybrid combinations, and evaluated an AI-agent-assisted PFC3D modelling workflow. Thirteen mixture groups comprising 39 cubic specimens were subjected to uniaxial compression testing. Steel-fibre concrete achieved a compressive strength of 39.7 MPa compared with 35.0 MPa for plain concrete, whereas macro-synthetic fibre concrete reached 35.7 MPa and polypropylene fibre concrete decreased to 25.0 MPa. Fibre incorporation generally changed failure from localised crack coalescence to more distributed cracking and improved post-peak specimen integrity. Three representative mixtures were modelled using PFC3D with an AI agent supporting task generation, script execution, feedback-based correction, and result recording. Simulated peak strengths of 34.2, 37.3, and 26.5 MPa for the N0, SM, and MP models, respectively, were within 5% of the corresponding experimental values. AI-agent-assisted modelling reduced the reported total modelling time from 142 to 34 min, corresponding to an efficiency improvement of 76.1%. The first-run task success rate was 61.1%, while all staged tasks were completed after correction. Repeated simulations produced low coefficients of variation for peak stress and crack number. The findings indicate that steel-macro-synthetic hybridisation provided comparatively favourable compressive performance, while the AI-assisted workflow supported efficient and reproducible discrete element modelling.

title: From Robotics to AI Agents
Machine Learning Prediction of Carbon Quantum Dots‐Induced Crop Growth Promotion Comparing Solution and Film Formulations
abstract: Machine learning enables accurate prediction of carbon quantum dots (CQDs)‐induced crop growth promotion using a limited experimental dataset. Two distinct CQD formulations were evaluated: solution‐type DIW‐CQDs applied directly to seeds and membrane‐type FA‐CQDs@polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) films placed over seedlings, using pea and wheat as model crops. Among nine classical regression models systematically compared, the decision tree algorithm exhibited superior predictive performance, achieving a test set R 2 of 0.9878, RMSE of 10.34, and MAE of 2.84. Feature importance analysis revealed that chlorophyll a content is the dominant physiological indicator, contributing 94.69% to the prediction of crop vigor index. A simplified model employing only chlorophyll a as the sole input achieved comparable accuracy ( R 2 = 0.9894), reducing the number of required input features from seven to one and substantially decreasing experimental measurement costs. This streamlined approach enables rapid, high‐throughput screening without compromising predictive reliability. The established prediction framework supports three major application scenarios: concentration optimization for maximum growth promotion, formulation screening between solution and film types, and cross‐species adaptation for different crops. By integrating material design, spectral engineering, and data‐driven machine learning, this work provides a practical decision‐making tool for the precision application of CQD‐based formulations in nanoagriculture.
