title: Visualizing the Golgi apparatus and Golgiphagy in vivo.
MIR2-Toolkit: a Python program for multiple-image radiography analysis with integrated silicon-crystal diffraction modeling tools.
abstract: Analyzer-based multiple-image radiography (MIR) is an X-ray phase-contrast imaging technique. It retrieves absorption, refraction, and ultra-small-angle X-ray scattering signals using the angular selectivity of a perfect-crystal analyzer. Conventional MIR processing typically relies on normalization between the object and reference datasets and on precise angular alignment, thereby increasing sensitivity to mechanical and thermal instabilities. The recently developed MIR2 framework addresses these limitations by independently analyzing object and reference datasets, eliminating explicit normalization and global alignment steps, and incorporating angular calibration based on the dynamical theory of diffraction. To facilitate the practical application of this method, MIR2-Toolkit has been developed as a Python-based graphical software package for MIR2 analysis. The software carries out dark correction, region-of-interest selection, rocking-curve handling, independent angular calibration, and pixel-wise Gaussian fitting of angular intensity profiles to retrieve contrast images. In addition to the main MIR2 workflow, the toolkit includes silicon-crystal diffraction modules for calculation and visualization of diffraction properties, reflectivity curves, and Darwin widths in symmetric Bragg and Laue geometries. In this paper, the MIR2 workflow implemented in the software is described, the program structure is outlined, and the main analysis and diffraction-modeling features are presented.

title: Optical Metrology for VCSEL Epitaxial Growth and Processing
abstract: Vertical cavity surface emitting lasers (VCSELs) feature layer structures which are among the most complicated ones in compound semiconductor device production. They consist of many layers with stringent requirements on optical thickness to match the device specifications. Especially the optical cavity requires a very precise thickness control going far beyond the requirements of standard edge-emitting lasers. Also, a high number of interfaces needs to be controlled, especially when arsenides and phosphides are combined. Optical in situ characterization is thus helpful, if not indispensable for process development as well as process control in production. Re-establishing growth conditions for a new growth campaign after chamber maintenance can be challenging and time consuming. This work is about how to tackle this challenge by applying in-situ optical metrology during growth and processing of GaAs-based VCSEL devices as well as post-growth ex-situ wafer mapping. We demonstrate how to efficiently combine in-situ and ex-situ white light reflectance (WLR) measurements and modelling in order to increase the target wavelength accuracy. Additionally, we discuss how to use the data obtained during growth in order to enable automated end pointing for the plasma etching of the VCSEL mesa. Application of reflectometry for GaN VCSELs is briefly discussed and an outlook on the usage of in-situ bow measurements is given.
journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics

title: A Fiber Coil Defect Detection Method Based on Feature Enhancement and Lightweight Network
abstract: The fiber coil is the core sensing component of a fiber optic gyroscope, and its winding quality directly affects gyroscope measurement accuracy. However, gap and stack defects frequently occur during the fiber coil winding process. Traditional detection methods suffer from low efficiency and poor generalization ability. Moreover, existing deep learning-based detection methods are often constrained by illumination conditions and require complex image preprocessing. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight, high-precision automated visual inspection framework tailored for fiber coil winding. The SimAM attention mechanism is integrated into the backbone feature extraction network to strengthen the model’s focus on defect-related features. The Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) loss is then introduced to optimize bounding box regression and improve the localization accuracy of small defects. In addition, Focal Loss replaces the original binary cross-entropy loss for confidence estimation to alleviate the foreground-background imbalance in dense detection. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an mAP of 92.33% and a detection speed of 114 FPS for fiber coil winding defect detection. Compared with existing methods, the proposed approach offers a simple structure, high accuracy, and real-time detection capability, making it suitable for engineering applications.

title: A 60-m Distance Measurement Exploiting the Linewidth Narrowing of the SMI Readout
abstract: Using a cheap DFB laser with coherence length ${\mathrm {L}}_{\mathrm {c}} =7$ m and reading the field returning from a remote target by means of a Self-Mixing Interferometry (SMI) scheme, we are able to sense returns and measure distances up to 60 m thanks to the (1 +C)2 factor of increase of ${\mathrm{L}}_{\mathrm {c.~ }}$ due to optical feedback into the laser cavity. The simplified hardware and low cost of the SMI configuration makes it attractive as medium distances LiDAR for automotive applications.

title: SRMP-S: Self-Refining Multi-Planner Strategy for Long-Horizon Robotic Tasks
abstract: Enabling robotic agents to perform complex long-horizon tasks has been a long-standing goal in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). Existing Large Language Models (LLMs)-based symbolic planners auto-generate Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) specifications to bridge language and formal reasoning, but they rely on a single open-loop planner and lack autonomous error diagnosis or model refinement, limiting robustness in long-horizon tasks. To address these issues, we propose Self-Refining Multi-Planner Strategy (SRMP-S), a closed-loop framework that integrates the semantic flexibility of LLMs with the rigor of symbolic planning through two key innovations. Firstly, SRMP-S employs a multi-strategy planner ensemble, concurrently executing multiple heterogeneous symbolic planners to broaden first-attempt solvability and produce high-fidelity, cross-validated failure diagnostics. Secondly, it introduces a self-refinement mechanism that automatically converts these diagnostics into structured natural language (NL) feedback to iteratively refine the LLMs-generated PDDL models, enabling autonomous recovery from initial modeling inaccuracies. Experimental results demonstrate that SRMP-S achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple domains, outperforming existing LLM-based planners.

title: Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Shape Estimation of Concentric Tube Robots
abstract: Accurately modeling the mechanics of concentric tube robots (CTRs) remains challenging due to nonlinear curvature coupling, torsional interactions, and sensitivity to material and geometric parameters. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a flexible alternative by embedding governing equations directly into the training process. In this work, we develop a PINN for modeling the free-tip kinematics of a three-tube CTR with a max length of 250 mm, incorporating geometric compatibility, constitutive relations, and equilibrium equations based on Cosserat rod theory into the training pipeline. We additionally introduce a Fourier-based joint encoding to represent the actuation rotations. Along 20 equally spaced points for each backbone configuration, the PINN achieved mean and maximum errors of 0.80 $\pm$ 0.42mm and 1.71 $\pm$ 1.12 mm, outperforming the analytical Cosserat model and demonstrating that physics-informed learning can approximate nonlinear CTR mechanics. A dataset-size ablation against a standard neural network showed that the two networks perform comparably when the training data densely cover the workspace, whereas the PINN was substantially more accurate under sparse coverage, retaining error at or below the analytical model with as little as $5\%$ of the data.

title: Convex Data-Driven Model Predictive Control for Trajectory Tracking in Robotic Manipulators
abstract: Accurate trajectory tracking is a fundamental control task in robotics, typically achieved using model-based methods. Computed Torque Control (CTC) is computationally efficient but struggles to handle system constraints, while Model Predictive Control (MPC) can manage constraints but often results in nonlinear formulations. This work introduces a convex Model Predictive Control (MPC) formulation that incorporates learned dynamics for a robot manipulator. A nonparametric model is used to learn the residual between a nominal model and the observed dynamics, using an inverse dynamics formulation. Convexification is achieved by applying implicit partial differentiation to linearize the inverse dynamics model augmented with the residual model along the reference trajectory, resulting in a Linear Time-Varying (LTV) system. Extensive simulations and hardware experiments on a Franka Emika Panda manipulator demonstrate that our convex MPC approach outperforms learning-based baselines in handling a broad range of model mismatches and constraints. Results also show that learning the residual in inverse dynamics form offers better tracking performance than learning the residual in forward dynamics.

title: Unsupervised Interpretable Human Intent Discovery in Teleoperation via Bayesian Nonparametric Learning and Multi-Modal LLMs
abstract: Human intent recognition is crucial for effective robotic teleoperation, yet existing methods rely on a predefined set of intentions, a requirement that is manually intractable in complex open-world scenarios. We propose an unsupervised framework that integrates Bayesian nonparametric learning with multi-modal Large Language Models (LLMs) to autonomously discover and interpret human intentions. We first employ a hierarchical Dirichlet process hidden semi-Markov model (HDP-HSMM) to adaptively segment kinematic sequences into motion primitives, reducing the load on downstream models. Each segment is represented by multi-modal features extracted from front-facing video, robot kinematics, and eye fixations. We then develop a reasoning architecture based on zero-shot Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, where a Vision-Language Model (VLM) translates each segment into a semantic description, and an LLM clusters these descriptions to reveal intentions and generate human-readable interpretations. Experimental results on real-world data show that our method can uncover meaningful intentions highly consistent with expert judgments, outperforming baselines in intra-intent consistency by achieving the lowest semantic outlier rate of 8.5%.

title: Leveraging Scene-Invariant Priors for Autoregressive Human Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Accurate human trajectory prediction is essential for autonomous driving and robot navigation. Despite substantial progress, deep learning-based approaches often suffer from the train-inference gap caused by distributional discrepancies between training and test environments. The goal-guided framework mitigates this issue by exploiting the scene-invariant prior that human motion is typically goal-driven. However, existing goal-guided approaches do not fully leverage additional scene-invariant priors and therefore still face two key limitations: insufficient diversity in predicted goals and the lack of explicit modeling of human kinematic consistency. In this paper, we propose SIPTraj, a goal-guided trajectory prediction framework that integrates scene-invariant priors at both the long-term intention and short-term motion levels. For goal estimation, we introduce goal candidates derived from offline clustering of trajectory endpoints as a data-driven approximation of scene-invariant long-term intention modalities, and develop a weighted Farthest Point Sampling (FPS) strategy that balances spatial coverage with predicted likelihoods to improve goal diversity while preserving semantic plausibility. For trajectory completion, we develop a kinematic-aware dual-stream autoregressive decoder that jointly predicts aligned position and velocity. The decoder adopts a kinematic initialization with residual refinement (KIRR) strategy: future states are initialized using a constant-velocity kinematic model and refined via reciprocal cross-attention, which injects kinematic consistency into the decoding process and leads to more natural and accurate trajectory prediction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SIPTraj achieves state-of-the-art performance on the ETH/UCY and SDD benchmarks.

title: Learning Equality Constraints From Trajectory Demonstrations
abstract: Equality constraints are common in robotics, arising in applications such as pose-constrained manipulation, coordinated motion, and task-space planning. Classical constrained planners typically assume an analytic constraint function, whereas in practice only feasible demonstrations may be available. We study how to learn explicit equality constraints directly from such demonstrations. We propose Orthonormal Neural Constraint Learning (ONCL), a method that learns multiple scalar constraint functions jointly and represents the equality constraint by their common zero set. Rather than estimating local normal directions and generating large amounts of supervised off-constraint data as related works, ONCL regularizes the gradients of different constraint functions to be normalized and mutually orthogonal, inducing a structured local normal space during learning. This yields an explicit differentiable constraint model in the original state space for evaluation and downstream planning. We evaluate ONCL on ten synthetic and robotic datasets spanning dimensions from 2 to 12. ONCL significantly outperforms each of three baselines on six datasets, while remaining competitive on the other datasets. We further validate ONCL on a physical KUKA iiwa 14 using kinesthetic demonstrations collected by a human operator. The learned pose constraint is subsequently used on the same platform for downstream trajectory planning under a modified task objective and an additional known obstacle-avoidance constraint.

title: Physically Aware Generative Design for Spatial Mechanism Synthesis: A Differentiable Diffusion-Refinement Framework
abstract: Spatial mechanism synthesis requires joint reasoning over discrete topology and continuous geometry under strict loop-closure constraints. Existing search-based methods are often tied to predefined topology spaces, while purely data-driven generators can produce topologically plausible but kinematically infeasible mechanisms. This paper proposes GenRefMechSyn, a physics-aware generative framework that integrates Mimic, a Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based topology–geometry sketch generator, Refiner, a differentiable kinematic refiner, and Judge, a refinement-aware value model. Mimic proposes candidate mechanism sketches, Refiner optimizes continuous geometry under fixed topology and projects candidates toward the kinematic-feasibility region, and Judge uses refinement feedback to guide diffusion sampling toward candidates with higher downstream refinability. Under a 1000-trial acceptance protocol, GenRefMechSyn achieves 81.6% two-translational-DOF (2T) kinematic validity; controlled baselines obtain 6.6% for DiT+Refiner without Judge guidance/feedback augmentation, 84.3% for genetic algorithm (GA)+Refiner with a favorable fixed topology, and 12.2% for multi-topology GA+Refiner. The generated mechanisms reach loop-closure residuals and task errors on the order of $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-4}$, respectively. The same architecture and seed set are also used in an independently trained two-rotational-DOF (2R) feedback run, showing applicability to a separately trained rotational task.

title: Latent Space 3D Shape Servoing With FEM-Based Dynamic Modeling
abstract: In this letter, we introduce a novel shape control framework that precisely guides a soft 3D object toward a desired shape using a robotic arm. Our framework seamlessly integrates vision, object physics behavior from a dynamic Finite Element Model (FEM), and latent-space representations to achieve accurate and adaptive shape control. Our method starts with any differentiable mapping function that takes the high dimensional 3D mesh representing a soft object as input and projects it into a low dimensional latent space to get a new compact representation of the object that is suitable for control. By leveraging the FEM model and the differentiability of this mapping function, we derive the analytical relationship that links the motion of the latent representation to the motion of the robot gripper to which the object is attached. Building on this formulation, we design a novel closed-loop shape servoing algorithm. To enhance robustness against model approximations, we integrate real-time visual tracking using an RGB-D camera, allowing for continuous correction of any discrepancies between the physical object and its model. We validate the effectiveness of our approach through real-world experiments on an elastic deformable object, employing two distinct mapping techniques for shape feature extraction: Autoencoder and Laplacian-based descriptor.

title: An Optimization Framework for Intraoperative Suture Planning via Physics-Aware Differentiable Graph Neural Network-Based Surrogates
Mitigation of Field Drift in a Conduction-Cooled No-Insulation ReBCO Magnet by Overshooting Current Profile Optimization
abstract: Conduction-cooled no-insulation (NI) rare-earth barium copper oxide (ReBCO) magnets are attractive for compact high-field systems because they combine cryogen-free operation with intrinsic quench protection. Their field temporal stability, however, is limited by the coupled effects of screening-current-induced field relaxation and charging delay caused by turn-to-turn current sharing. This article investigates a 50 K, 2 T desktop ReBCO magnet composed of 13 double-pancake coils and proposes an overshooting-current-profile optimization method for suppressing postexcitation field drift. A 2-D axisymmetric homogenized model, based on the T-A formulation and a radial voltage-control equation, is developed to calculate both screening-current evolution and NI current redistribution. A surrogate-model-based optimization procedure, combining Latin hypercube sampling and Gaussian process regression, is then used to analyze the effects of overshoot ratio, overshoot ramp rate, and plateau duration. The results show that the overshoot ratio is the dominant parameter controlling the sign and magnitude of the center-field drift, whereas a sufficiently long plateau can significantly reduce the overshoot required for low-drift operation. The optimized charging profile reduces the center-field drift rate to below 50 ppm/h in the 3000–5000 s postexcitation window. The study provides a practical charging strategy for improving the field temporal stability of conduction-cooled NI ReBCO magnets.

title: EcoxPU: Autonomous Multi-Agent Orchestration for Energy-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Inference on Heterogeneous xPUs
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) inference is increasingly served on disaggregated clusters that combine different accelerator types, including NVIDIA GPUs, Huawei Ascend NPUs, and Kunlunxin AI processors. We show that these heterogeneous xPUs exhibit distinct energy-performance behaviors across inference phases and model modules, so a fixed deployment can waste substantial energy even when latency targets are met. This paper presents EcoxPU , an autonomous multi-agent framework for energy-efficient disaggregated LLM inference. EcoxPU jointly coordinates Prefill-Decode (PD) separation and Attention-Feed-Forward Network (FFN) disaggregation, assigning compute-bound and memory-bound work to suitable devices while adapting frequency and load placement at runtime. Evaluated on a heterogeneous cluster with NVIDIA H100, Huawei Ascend 910B, and Kunlunxin P800, EcoxPU reduces energy consumption by 31.9–45% (42% on average), while maintaining $\le$ ≤ 6% latency overhead and $\le$ ≤ 2% perplexity variation. It also improves MoE-FFN utilization on Ascend 910B to 82.3%, and cross-domain transfer learning accelerates agent adaptation by 2.67×.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems

title: When Reinforcement Learning Meets Zero-Determinant: Social Welfare Control in Iterated Game Under Spatial Crowdsourcing
abstract: Spatial crowdsourcing is a prospective category of crowdsourcing that takes advantage of various sensors and resources of mobile devices in the area of mobile internet. The participants in spatial crowdsourcing interact with each other, such as requestors, platform, and workers, and they collaborate to complete the crowdsourcing tasks. The Internet Service Provider (ISP) plays a role in transmitting crowdsensing data and supports spatial crowdsourcing. The interactions of the participants form a game in crowdsourcing, but the game between the two players (platform and ISP) is paid little attention by researchers. The crowdsourcing platform assigns sensing tasks and the ISP selects a portion of the Road-Side Units (RSUs) to power on for data transmissions. The interaction between the platform and ISP is crucial, because it impacts the data quality in spatial crowdsourcing. In this paper, we investigate the iterated game between crowdsourcing platform and ISP in Spatial Crowdsourcing (SC). The objective is to achieve a possible maximal social welfare between the platform and ISP in the long term, which is defined as the weighted sum of their expected utilities. We first propose a Reinforcement Learning based strategy of Spatial Crowdsourcing (RLSC) to maximize the reward (i.e., expected utility) from the iterated game in the long term. To control the social welfare without considering the opponent’s strategy, we investigate the Zero-Determinant strategy of Spatial Crowdsourcing (ZDSC) in a discrete case, which involves two actions and multi-actions, respectively. We model the iterated game by using the Markov Decision Process (MDP) and analyze how to theoretically obtain RLSC and ZDSC strategies with the objective of maximal social welfare control. Furthermore, we analyze the two strategies against each other as a Markov Game using the MDP. Experimental results show RLSC can achieve global maximal social welfare sometimes, but it cannot control the social welfare when it plays against classical strategies, and the social welfare may fall into a local maximum. The proposed ZDSC strategy can unilaterally control social welfare to achieve a stable and possible maximal value, regardless of the opponent’s strategies.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems

title: Current-Sensorless Virtual-Vector Quasi-Sliding Mode Predictive Control for T-Type Inverters
abstract: To alleviate the tedious weighting factor tuning, heavy computational burden, and inherent chattering in traditional model predictive control (MPC) and sliding mode control (SMC) for T-type inverters, this article proposes a current-sensorless virtual-vector quasi-sliding-mode predictive control (VVQSMPC) strategy. By embedding discrete sliding-mode dynamics into the predictive control cost function, a unified control framework is established that integrates the fast dynamic response of MPC and the strong robustness of SMC while effectively suppressing chattering. To achieve neutral-point voltage balance, a set of virtual voltage vectors is constructed as convex combinations of basic vectors, thereby eliminating weighting factors and preserving the intrinsic relationship between the modulation index and output voltage amplitude. A three-stage vector preselection strategy is further developed to reduce the number of evaluated vectors from 69 to 14 or 16, significantly lowering computational complexity. In addition, a full-order state observer is employed to enable current-sensorless operation and enhance system reliability. Discrete-time Lyapunov analysis demonstrates that the proposed method ensures uniformly bounded quasi-sliding-mode motion within a limited bandwidth. Experimental results on a digital signal processor-based platform demonstrate that, compared with conventional MPC, the proposed strategy achieves improved steady-state voltage quality, faster transient response, and enhanced robustness against parameter variations. These results confirm that the proposed VVQSMPC provides a practical and effective solution for high-performance control of T-type inverters.

title: A Fault Diagnosis and Differentiated Processing Strategy for Grid Side Overcurrent Faults in Electric Traction Drive System
abstract: Grid-side overcurrent (GSOC) in the traction transformer is a system-level fault in the electric traction drive system. Once it occurs, the traction control unit indiscriminately trips the main circuit breaker to ensure safety, causing the train to stop and requiring inspection and maintenance by the crew. This excessive protection and manual maintenance approach reduces the availability and operational efficiency of the trains. Therefore, this article proposes a fault diagnosis and differentiated processing strategy for GSOC. First, the GSOC mechanism and the degree of deterioration are analyzed, and the different types of GSOC are classified as permanent fault or temporary fault. Second, the effective segment of the fault signal is selected, and the fault temporal features are extracted. Third, the differentiated processing strategy is proposed based on the diagnostic results and the degree of fault deterioration. Finally, the fault diagnostic model is established based on random forest classifier, and then the fault scenario is reproduced on the RT-LAB and the diagnostic model is implemented using a digital signal processor to complete the verification experiments. The experimental results show that, compared with existing methods, the proposed method can not only achieve 100% diagnostic accuracy but also significantly shorten the diagnostic time. Moreover, the differentiated processing strategy can greatly reduce the trains’ stopping time and frequency caused by GSOC.

title: An SAC-Based Auto Optimization Model for Dynamic Current Balancing of Multichip Paralleled SiC Power Module
abstract: The dynamic current imbalance between the paralleled SiC mosfets in multichip power modules, which is commonly attributed to the asymmetric module layout, severely limits their current capacity and thermal reliability. Adjusting the connection points of bonding wires is an effective method to mitigate imbalanced dynamic current. However, manual trial-and-error is currently the most common method for optimizing connection points, which is both deficient and inefficient. Existing automated solutions usually rely on a prefitting process based on large datasets, which is time-consuming and impractical for high-dimensional parameter applications. Thus, this article proposes an optimization model to mitigate dynamic current imbalance, which can automatically adjust the connection points of bonding wires without any manual intervention. The reinforcement learning (RL) soft actor-critic algorithm was applied to the power module optimization, eliminating the need for prefitting and enabling high-dimensional parameter optimization. After optimization, nearly complete dynamic current balancing in both high-side and low-side switches in a multichip-paralleled half-bridge power module is achieved, as verified by simulations and experiments. This model achieves true dynamic current balancing automation for the first time, providing an important reference for the application of RL to the automated optimization of multichip power modules.

title: Safety-Critical Model Predictive Control for Power Inverters Using Control Barrier Functions
abstract: In single-phase inverters, a critical challenge lies in the fact that inductor current overload seriously compromises the reliability of power switching devices. To address this challenge, this article integrates model predictive control (MPC) with control barrier function (CBF) to develop a safety control strategy for single-phase inverters. The strategy strictly ensures the safety of the inductor current while achieving high-precision control of the output voltage. Considering the necessity of maintaining continuous safety constraints on inductor current, the proposed strategy transforms the inductor current limits into a CBF formulation. The CBF-based formulation is incorporated into the constraint set of the quadratic programming solution process of MPC. This ensures the safety of the main circuit switching devices during current overloads. This article establishes the exponential stability of the safe set via Lyapunov stability theory. Through physical hardware experiments, hardware-in-the-loop experiments, and Simulink-based simulations of a single-phase full-bridge inverter system, and comparisons with a PID+saturation controller, a state-constrained MPC controller, and an SMC controller, the proposed strategy is validated, confirming its simultaneous fulfillment of output voltage performance and inductor current safety objectives.

title: Neural Network Based On-Time Control of Boundary Conduction Mode Boost Power Factor Corrector
abstract: Additional on-time control in boundary conduction mode (BCM) boost power factor correction (PFC) circuits has been a practical solution to improve power quality. However, optimal on-time profiles are difficult to obtain using conventional model-based approaches due to nonlinearities in both hardware and control. These nonlinearities require extensive analytical modeling, parameter extraction, and tuning, which leads to a complex development process. Data-driven on-time control can estimate accurate on-time without analytical modeling because it inherently includes hardware nonlinearities. However, conventional approximation methods, such as lookup tables and polynomial fitting have limitations in terms of memory requirement and computation time. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods have recently been used in power-electronics applications to reduce the burden of model analysis and optimize, the application of AI to additional on-time control in BCM boost PFC converters remain limited. This article proposes a lightweight neural network (NN)-based on-time control method using pretrained NN, without requiring analytical modeling. A complete design flow—data collection, training, and real-time deployment—is presented. Since the proposed NN can be rapidly retrained with newly collected data, it can be easily adapted to different device selections or circuit parameter variations without extensive redesign effort. Experimental results from a prototype with 110–220 VRMS input and 400 V/150 W output validate the effectiveness of the proposed NN controller in achieving competitive performance in terms of power factor and total harmonic distortion of the input current with the real time application on a low-cost microcontroller unit.

title: Instantaneous-Value Modeling of DC–DC Converters: From Switched System Models to Smooth Continuous-Time Models
abstract: Switched system models of DC–DC converters cannot be directly analyzed or controlled using conventional continuous-time system theory. To address the problem, we propose a smoothing-based modeling approach in which sigmoid functions are employed based on a generalized switched-system formulation. First, logical variables are defined to represent the mode-switching conditions of the converter, enabling the construction of a logical switched dynamical model. Next, smooth and continuous sigmoid functions are introduced to approximate these logical variables. This approach was used to develop smooth continuous-time models for single-ended primary-inductor, Zeta, Cuk, and interleaved parallel DC–DC converters. Simulation and experimental results of single-ended primary-inductor converter and interleaved parallel buck converter reveal that the proposed models accurately capture the instantaneous behavior of the converters. This modeling method provides a unified framework for representing multimodal switching behavior and various circuit phenomena across different operating modes, thereby improving the accuracy, applicability, and generality of converter models. The proposed smooth and differentiable model was used for stability and dynamic analysis, providing guidance for parameter selection and the development of more effective control strategies to optimize the system operating performance.

title: A Review on ANN-Based Behavioral Modeling Techniques for High-Efficiency Power Amplifiers
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive review of artificial neural network (ANN)-based behavioral modeling techniques for high-efficiency power amplifiers (PAs). As wireless systems demand greater linearity and efficiency, accurate modeling of PA nonlinearity and memory effects becomes essential. We systematically explore fundamental and advanced ANN architectures including memoryless networks, and memory networks, such as temporal encoding, recurrent models, knowledge-infused networks, attention mechanisms, and hybrid approaches, and evaluate their capabilities in capturing complex PA dynamics. This study further investigates optimization algorithms for enhancing ANN model performance and their integration into digital predistortion (DPD) systems for linearization. A dedicated section discusses embedded deployment considerations, highlighting tradeoffs between accuracy, complexity, and real-time applicability on platforms, such as field-programmable gate arrays and digital signal processors. Finally, we provide architectural selection guidelines and identify future research directions, including lightweight model design, multiband modeling, and automated ANN-driven PA optimization. This review demonstrates the practical utility of ANN-based techniques for advancing PA design in next-generation communication systems.

title: Small-Signal Modeling and Stability Analysis of LCC–HVDC System Considering Switching Dynamics via Floquet and Filippov Theory
abstract: Line commutated converter-based high-voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) systems are widely deployed but face significant broadband small-signal stability challenges. Due to their low switching frequency, LCC switching dynamics critically influence broadband oscillatory behavior. Conventional switch-function-based approaches partially capture these dynamics via series approximations. However, they require high-order expansions of switching functions and still struggle to accurately represent the commutation process. Given that LCCs are inherently piecewise smooth, nonlinear time-periodic systems, this article proposes a piecewise small-signal model for LCC-HVDC systems. Filippov’s method is employed to precisely capture the switching behavior, while Floquet theory is utilized to assess system stability. Furthermore, to trace the root causes of unstable or underdamped oscillations, the concept of participation factors is extended from smooth linear time-periodic systems to piecewise smooth time-periodic systems, enabling quantitative analysis of the interaction between system modes and state variables. Compared with existing models, the proposed approach achieves higher accuracy while maintaining relatively high computational efficiency. The validity of the stability analysis is confirmed through hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

title: High-Power Four-Port Converters With Integrated Storage for Fast and Slow EV Charging
abstract: This article presents two isolated four-port converters for high-power electric vehicle (EV) fast-charging applications. One converter is based on fully processed power conversion (FPPC), while the other adopts partial power processing (PPPC). By utilizing both FPPC and PPPC configurations, the proposed design achieves a reduction in size and cost. In addition, the PPPC configuration allows partial power to flow directly from the energy storage system to the EV, further reducing cost by lowering the converter rating, minimizing losses, and improving efficiency. The article also addresses internal coupling challenges in multiport systems by introducing a dual decoupling approach, which combines hardware-based impedance design with software-level control using frequency and phase shift modulation. Detailed mathematical modeling for power flow analysis, along with thermal and reliability analysis, is provided to evaluate performance. The proposed converters are validated through simulation, and a laboratory prototype of 1 kW is used to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed converter design. The PPPC configuration achieves a peak efficiency of 98.1%.

title: Model Data Hybrid Driven Robot Joint Torque Active Disturbance Rejection Control Based on Friction Feedforward and PPO Algorithm
abstract: To address the nonlinear friction disturbances and complex parameter tuning issues faced by traditional active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) in permanent magnet synchronous motor-driven robotic joints, this article proposes a current loop control method based on proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm for ADRC parameter optimization combined with friction disturbance identification. The method employs a radial basis function neural network to perform offline identification of joint friction forces, explicitly separating them from total disturbances into a known disturbance channel for feedforward compensation, enabling the extended state observer to focus on remaining unknown disturbances. The key ADRC parameter tuning is modeled as a Markov decision process, trained using the PPO algorithm to achieve dynamic adaptive parameter adjustment. By integrating RBF friction perception and PPO parameter dynamic tuning, this article achieves hierarchical disturbance compensation capabilities unattainable with a single technique, enabling friction feedforward isolation, unknown disturbance estimation, and online parameter self-optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional manually tuned ADRC, the proposed method reduces mechanical vibration amplitude by 56.2%, decreases current oscillation by 40%, and improves startup speed response by 64%; compared to existing field-oriented control algorithms, it reduces angle tracking error peaks by 72.5%.

title: Analysis and Mitigation of Grid Current Distortion in Single-Stage DAB AC–DC Converters With Minimum Peak Current
abstract: Power feedforward control is utilized in single-stage dual-active-bridge (DAB) AC–DC converters for natural power factor correction. However, this approach renders the grid current highly dependent on the modulation strategy and susceptible to practical circuit nonlinearities, which result in a mismatch between the actual and modeled power. In this article, the optimal operating modes to minimize peak current are first analyzed and the grid current constraints based on the conventional piecewise-linear model are derived to achieve the unity power factor. The continuity and sinusoidal purity of the grid current are then evaluated in terms of mode transitions and absolute power deviations. To address distortion issues, a charge-equivalent linearized commutation model is proposed. The proposed model achieves real-time equivalent linearization of the nonlinear commutation process during the dead time considering the magnetizing current. Based on the commutation model, the instantaneous power for single-stage DAB AC–DC converters is accurately determined. Furthermore, an automatic mode selection strategy and the computational flow are developed to mitigate grid current distortion. Finally, a 1-kW laboratory prototype with a 40-VDC output is constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Nonsequential Multiobjective Integrated Optimal Design of LLC Resonant Converters Based on Interlinking Variables
abstract: Recent advances in LLC resonant converters have intensified the demand for effective multiobjective optimization techniques to achieve higher efficiency, increased power density, and improved thermal stability. This article presents an interlinking-variable-based nonsequential integrated multiobjective optimization framework tailored for LLC resonant converters. Unlike conventional sequential optimization approaches that treat the magnetizing inductance and the resonant inductance as fixed targets imposed between separate design stages, the proposed method redefines these values as explicit functions of the magnetic design variables, removing the equality constraints inherent in the sequential structure and unifying all circuit-level and magnetic-level design variables within a single optimization process. The interlinking relationships are evaluated through a hybrid analysis model combining time-domain circuit analysis with an ANN-based magnetic surrogate. Hardware prototypes designed by the proposed and conventional sequential methods are fabricated and experimentally compared. The proposed method improves the converter efficiency by 1.3%, reduces the total component volume by 9.0%, and decreases the total computation time by 56% compared with the conventional sequential design.

title: Predictive Control Strategies for CC-CV Charging of Offboard Chargers: Formulation, Comprehensive Analysis, and Experimental Validation
abstract: When conventional voltage-oriented control (VOC) and direct power control (DPC) strategies are applied to electric vehicle (EV) chargers, they can compromise their performance owing to a cascaded control structure with limited bandwidth and controller-gain sensitivity under varying charging conditions. Alternatively, finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) has emerged as a promising solution due to its direct use of discrete switching states and multiobjective optimization capabilities. However, a systematic investigation and comprehensive analysis of current-based and power-based FCS-MPC strategies for offboard EV chargers in terms of grid power quality, charger efficiency, battery side ripple, computational complexity, and control robustness under varied charging profiles has not been explored yet. To fill this research gap, this article presents a comprehensive formulation, implementation, validation, and analysis of predictive current control (PCC) and predictive power control (PPC) strategies for a two-stage offboard charger operating under constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) charging conditions. In addition, a new charge cycle efficiency metric is introduced to quantify overall charger efficiency during the complete charging process. To validate the effectiveness of both methods experimentally, a two-stage offboard charging system with a dSPACE MicroLabBox control platform is developed to charge a 2.4 kWh, 400 V battery pack. The charger’s performance with the PCC and PPC schemes is holistically evaluated under steady-state, transient, CC-CV charging, and parameter mismatch conditions. Finally, the tradeoffs and selective guidelines of both predictive control strategies for EV charging applications are highlighted.

title: High-Accuracy Noninvasive Submodule Current Measurement in StakPak IGBTs Using an Ampere-Law-Guided Rectangular PCB Rogowski Coil
abstract: Submodule current distribution in StakPak insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) is important for device condition assessment. Existing internal current measurement methods for press-pack IGBTs usually require opening the device package. The special package structure of StakPak IGBTs enables rectangular printed circuit board Rogowski coils (PCB RCs) to be externally installed at the collector protrusions without opening or modifying the device package. However, representative fixed-conductor-based designs may suffer from reduced accuracy in complex conductor environments. This letter proposes a high-accuracy noninvasive submodule current measurement method using an optimized rectangular PCB RC mounted at the collector protrusion. Guided by Ampere’s circuital law, the coil measurement process is modeled as a discrete-sampling approximation of the continuous closed-path integral, revealing the dependence of the discretization error upper bound on the number of turns and turn-distribution uniformity. Accordingly, an arc-corner and turn-density optimization method is proposed. Finite-element results show that, compared with the representative existing rectangular coil, the area percentage of the low mutual-inductance-deviation region is increased from 31.36% to 93.00%. Experiments show that the interference current of the optimized PCB RC is reduced to 4.84% of that of the original oblique-corner PCB RC and 13.1% of that of the mini commercial Rogowski coil. In the full-submodule conduction test, the average error between the summed submodule current and the reference total current during the turn-on interval is 0.52%, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed noninvasive method.

title: An Empirical Fault Vulnerability Exploration of ReRAM-based Process-in-Memory CNN Accelerators
abstract: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM)-based Processing-in-Memory (PIM) accelerator is a promising platform for processing massively memory intensive matrix-vector multiplications of neural networks in parallel domain, due to its capability of analog computation, ultra-high density, near-zero leakage current, and non-volatility. Despite many advantages, ReRAM-based accelerators are highly error-prone due to limitations of technology fabrication that lead to process variations and defects. These limitations degrade the accuracy of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (Deep CNNs) running on PIM accelerators. While these CNNs accelerators are widely deployed in safety-critical systems, their vulnerability to fault is not well explored. In this paper, we have developed a fault injection framework to investigate the vulnerability of large-scale CNNs at both software- and hardware-level of inference phases. Faulty ReRAM devices are another reliability challenges due to significant degradation of classification accuracy when CNN parameters are mapped to the accelerators. To investigate this challenge, we map the CNN learning parameter to the ReRAM crossbar and inject faults into crossbar arrays. The proposed framework analyzes the impact of stuck-at high (SaH) and stuck-at low (SaL) fault models on different layers and locations of CNN learning parameters. By performing extensive fault injections, we illustrate that the vulnerability behavior of ReRAM-based PIM accelerator for CNNs is greatly impressible to the types and depth of layers, the location of the learning parameter in every layer, and the value and types of faults. Our observations show that different models have different vulnerabilities to faults. Specifically, we show that SaL further reduces classification accuracy than SaH.

title: Mineral Stabilization of Soil Organic Sulfur at the Continental Scale
abstract: Declining atmospheric sulfur (S) deposition makes S an emerging limiting macronutrient for plants, yet the stability and dynamics of soil organic S—the largest terrestrial S pool supplying plant‐available sulfate via mineralization—remain unclear. Across North American soils, total organic S is dominated by mineral‐associated organic S (MAOS; 61% ± 26%); this pool is stabilized by mineral protection but saturates at ~600 μg S/g soil. Compared with particulate organic S (POS), which is relatively labile and does not saturate, MAOS is more decomposed, chemically diverse, and climate‐sensitive. Higher temperature accelerates S mineralization in both pools, but their ability to supply available S varies with moisture regime because MAOS stabilizes in wetter soils while POS remains labile. This continental‐scale reassessment of the soil S cycle reveals that secondary minerals play a dual role in soil S cycling by stabilizing organic S and retaining sulfate, providing a mechanistic basis for nutrient management and carbon sequestration in response to climate change in an S‐scarce future.

title: From Reactive Remediation to Predictive Prevention: A Systems Synthesis of Global Soil Salinization and Sodicity
abstract: Soil salinization and sodicity are accelerating worldwide, reducing crop productivity across more than 160 million hectares of farmland and causing production losses approaching USD 27 billion annually. Despite decades of research documenting these impacts, the extent of salt‐affected soils continues to expand. Salt‐affected soil degradation emerges from feedbacks among physical, biological, and socioeconomic processes that operate across scales and resist intervention when addressed in isolation. This review synthesizes current understanding of these coupled feedbacks. We trace how ion accumulation, soil structural decline, microbial community disruption, and plant stress interact with irrigation practices, land use decisions, and governance systems. These interactions create threshold dynamics in which degradation can appear stable for years before rapid decline. Evidence from diverse regions reveals that effective restoration depends on coordinated interventions matched to the complexity of the system itself. Four research priorities emerge for advancing prediction and prevention. First, quantifying the thresholds that separate reversible from recalcitrant degradation across soil types and climates. Second, expanding predictive capacity through integrated sensor networks and data platforms that enable early warning. Third, improving understanding of how institutional structures influence adoption of restoration practices. Fourth, integrating biophysical and governance models to enable scaling from field trials to basin‐wide implementation. By coupling mechanistic understanding with monitoring infrastructure and adaptive governance, reactive remediation can give way to proactive prevention.

title: Towards Memory-Aware Adaptive Agents
abstract: Human memory is dynamic and uncertain, yet adaptive systems often overlook how it shapes interaction. This PhD investigates how agents can model and adapt to human memory by treating it as a latent, time-varying process. In this work we develop adaptive models that progress from estimating how much a user can remember, to inferring which information is retained, to identifying factors that influence forgetting, and finally to modeling individual differences shaped by prior knowledge and biases. Through simulation and user studies, this research examines whether agents can accurately infer memory states and provide targeted support. The goal is to enable more effective human-AI interaction through memory-aware adaptive systems that personalize behavior based on dynamic and individual cognitive characteristics.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Designing Multimodal Conversational AI for Longitudinal Well-Being Monitoring
abstract: Traditional mental health assessment often relies on infrequent self-report questionnaires (e.g., PHQ-9), which provide sparse, retrospective snapshots of well-being and may miss critical daily fluctuations. This creates an opportunity for low-burden assessments embedded in everyday interactions, such as open-ended conversations with AI systems, to complement existing clinical approaches. This doctoral research investigates how conversational AI agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) can predict well-being states by analyzing multimodal behavioral cues. It follows a four-stage plan: establishing a completed LLM-based baseline for predicting well-being from open-ended video responses; analyzing how LLMs integrate or misinterpret cross-modal signals; designing conversational flows that support response quality and user comfort; and evaluating longitudinal interactions for capturing intra-individual well-being fluctuations. Together, this work contributes a human-centered framework for multimodal well-being monitoring through natural conversations that complements, rather than replaces, traditional mental health assessment.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Human Hardware in an Agentic World: Jia’s Journey as a Biological Actuator and the Call for Sovereign Interaction Design
abstract: The historic paradigm of human-computer interaction assumes the human is the operator and the machine is the tool. However, the rapid emergence of agentic employment, where autonomous software agents hire humans for physical tasks, has the potential to invert this relationship. We term this the Reverse Centaur: a model where the AI provides the executive intent. The human role risks shifting primarily toward physical actuation. This paper stimulates reflection through the futuristic user journey of Jia, a gig worker in 2026. Through her shift, we analyze how Extended Reality serves as a multimodal actuation surface, utilizing mechanisms like diminished reality to edit risk out of the environment and structural offloading to bypass human spatial reasoning. These mechanisms have the potential to create a liability void and may foster long-term cognitive atrophy. Finally, we invite the ICMI community to embrace Sovereign Interaction Design, prioritizing Radical Legibility and Cognitive Scaffolding to preserve human agency.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Human-Centered Metrics for Evaluating Usability in Artificial Intelligence Generated Human Object Interactions
abstract: Usability is key to assessing whether interactions reflect real-world engagement with designed artifacts. However, evaluating usability requires design and prototyping, which incur substantial time and financial costs. With recent advances in multimodal generative AI (GenAI), it has become possible to predict, to some extent, the usability that a given design will afford, offering a potential solution to this problem. However, existing approaches focus primarily on visual fidelity and lack systematic evaluation of interaction interpretability from a human-centered perspective. To address this gap, the present study introduces the concept of interaction GenAI Affordance Quotient (AI-AQ), a human-centered framework for evaluating human-object interaction(HOI) quality. AI-AQ decomposes interactions into three components: subject consistency, affordance quality, and common sense alignment, enabling structured assessment. We compare GenAI-generated HOIs with real HOIs across varying object familiarity through a two-stage user study (N=80 pilot; N=800 main), using object images and textual prompts in GPT-4o. Results reveal a fundamental boundary condition: when evaluators possess semantic but not procedural knowledge of an object, neither structured metrics nor intuitive judgments can reliably differentiate AI-generated from real interactions — a systematic evaluation collapse that is absent when knowledge is complete or entirely absent. Beyond this, GenAI interactions are consistently inferior to real interactions across all dimensions. These findings suggest that multimodal generative models capture high-level visual and semantic patterns but remain limited in representing fine-grained interaction structure. This work contributes to human-aligned multimodal interaction and supports AI–human co-design by bridging visual, behavioral, and cognitive aspects of interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Did I Just Cheer in a Concert Hall?: Enhancing Remote Participation with Congruent Self-Voice Feedback
abstract: In participatory live streaming, the acoustic disconnect between the on-screen venue and the user’s physical environment undermines the sense of presence. To address this, we introduce an approach inspired by human echolocation: convolving a user’s own cheers with the binaural room impulse response (BRIR) of the visual space to provide real-time, congruent auditory feedback. We validated this approach through two experiments. Experiment 1, exploring audiovisual incongruence in real spaces, revealed that while reverberant feedback improved the subjective spatial impression compared to pass-through feedback, it did not significantly affect objective vocal parameters. Experiment 2, simulating a concert, demonstrated that adding reverberation to participants’ cheers significantly enhanced their sense of presence and realism. By focusing on active vocalization, this research provides foundational knowledge for designing more immersive and participatory interactive systems.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Multimodal Learner-State Analytics: Cross-Modal Insights from Motor-expressions and EEG for Instructor-Facing Visualization Platform
abstract: Remote video lectures expand educational access but limit instructors’ ability to observe how students engage with instructional content. To address this challenge, we explore how insights from portable electroencephalography can enrich visual analytics for computer-based learning environments. In our study, sixteen middle school students watched a mathematics video lecture while we collected and temporally aligned their gaze data, video recordings of motor expressions, and physiological indices of attention, valence, and arousal. By comparing these measures, we developed models to estimate internal learning states from accessible motor-expression data alone. We then applied changepoint detection to identify critical learning moments and integrated these alongside the estimated trends into a visualization platform designed for educators. An evaluation with thirty teachers revealed that observing these critical moments helped them identify specific lecture segments warranting closer inspection, allowing educators to reflect deeply on pacing, explanation quality, and overall slide design. These findings highlight a practical path toward scalable visualization platforms for digital education, equipping educators with profound pedagogical insights through accessible sensing alone.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Context-Aware Multimodal AI System for Wildfire Decision Support
abstract: Wildfires are growing in frequency and destructive scale, yet decision support for responders remains fragmented: prediction, suppression planning, and actionable intelligence rarely coexist in a single operational system. We present FireCastBot, a multimodal decision-support system that combines spatiotemporal ignition forecasting, RL-based suppression simulation, and a RAG assistant into a single pipeline for wildfire response. We extend the US Wildfire Dataset with socio-contextual and spatial features that capture human-driven ignition risk missing from purely meteorological models. Across a 125,995-sample, 60-day causal corpus, a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) achieves the best accuracy-latency trade-off: 72.3% accuracy, 0.613 PR-AUC, and 0.024 ms inference latency. The suppression module uses a physics-aware Gymnasium environment over real terrain; a PPO agent learns anticipatory containment strategies. The RAG assistant retrieves from a curated wildfire doctrine knowledge base and from incident reports ingested at runtime. Hands-free STT/TTS interaction supports field deployment and multi-agency coordination. A formative user study (N = 52) shows above-average usability and strong perceived decision-support value across three wildfire risk scenarios.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Code-to-Speech: An Exploratory Study of AI Text-to-Speech for Source Code Readability
abstract: As multimodal interaction becomes central to digital learning, technical interfaces, such as eBooks and conversational agents, present unique accessibility challenges for users relying on the auditory modality. While modern Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems excel at rendering natural language, they often fail to convey the complex, structural syntax of source code, creating a significant barrier for blind and low-vision programmers. We frame the vocal rendering of source code as a cross-modal translation task, in which spatial and symbolic information visually encoded in code must be mapped into a linear auditory signal. This study explores "Code-to-Speech" (CTS) as a critical component of multimodal technical communication. We present a comparative evaluation of five leading AI-driven TTS engines (including ChatGPT, Gemini, and ElevenLabs) to determine their efficacy in rendering mixed-content (text and code) materials. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, we combine automated linguistic metrics (WER, BLEU, METEOR) with a human-centered qualitative assessment. Our findings reveal significant differences: ChatGPT and Gemini consistently achieved lower error rates, while Copilot omitted critical tokens. However, all systems struggle with essential structural cues such as indentation, pauses, and code comments. We also show that designed prompts improve intelligibility, particularly for novices. Our work establishes a benchmark for CTS and underscores the need for multimodal AI architectures that support inclusive technical interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: "Great! The Next Step Is...": In Pursuit of Proactive Assistance with Multimodal Foundation Models
abstract: Large language and multimodal models have been largely employed to reactively generate content and assistance. In contrast, we explore how models can be employed to provide proactive assistance that fluidly supports ongoing human activities. We identify and tackle challenges in such streaming scenarios—where models must act continuously and responsively in real time, rather than waiting for explicit user requests. We explore solutions and evaluation metrics in the context of a mixed-reality AI agent designed to assist people in carrying out procedural physical tasks. Specifically, we focus on the challenge of identifying when each step of a procedure has been completed so that an agent can appropriately move on to the next step. Using a publicly available multimodal dataset of task-centric human-agent interactions, we study an array of prompting strategies across several frontier LLMs and VLMs, considering both the content and timing of model queries. Our findings demonstrate the criticality of developing application-driven metrics that enable meaningful comparisons and highlight key gaps in current model capabilities for proactive assistance. This work underscores the importance of temporally-aware evaluation in designing fluid real-time human-AI collaboration.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Emotional Echoes: A Spatialized VR Gallery for Revisiting and Reinterpreting Emotional Memory
abstract: Emotional Echoes is an interactive VR installation that reimagines emotional journaling as an embodied, multimodal, and ritualized practice. Spoken reflections are captured through a custom hardware interface and represented in VR as interactive bubbles whose color and animated visual behavior are driven by a creative, non-diagnostic mapping of provisional emotional metadata derived from the spoken reflection. The reflections are then further explored through dialogue with an AI conversational agent. Each session generates an AI-composed image that is archived in a personal VR gallery and physically printed as a tangible keepsake. Rather than presenting emotion as objective data to be measured, Emotional Echoes treats it as a lived experience that can be constructed, revisited, and reinterpreted over time. We propose a VR demonstration in which conference attendees record a short reflection, converse with the AI agent, explore the resulting memory gallery, optionally experience an associated olfactory cue when approaching a gallery artwork, and receive a printed keepsake.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: Tutorial on Human-centric Embodied Multimodal Interaction (HEMI) in conjunction with ICMI’26
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and emerging world models have dramatically advanced Embodied AI. Yet, while agents can now perform complex autonomous tasks in controlled settings, deploying them in unstructured, dynamic, and human-centric environments requires a fundamental leap in how they perceive and interact with the world and human. To operate alongside humans, in applications like elderly care, co-working in warehouses and industrial automation, agents must master multimodal interaction beyond perception. The Tutorial on Human-centric Embodied Multimodal Interaction(HEMI) focuses on three core pillars regarding embodied multimodal interaction: i) Multimodal Perception & Reasoning: how agents fuse multimodal sensory inputs (visual, spatial, linguistic) to comprehend the physical world, identifying critical uncertainty and confusion, ensuring their actions are executable, effective, and safe; ii) Proactive Multimodal Interaction: To resolve ambiguous human intents and prevent physical risks, agents must proactively interact with users, leveraging both verbal and non-verbal cues to clarify goals; iii) Personalized Multimodal Interaction: interpreting situated contexts to adapt agent behaviors, actions, and communication styles according to individual user preferences. By bridging vision-language representation, advanced multimodal human-agent interaction, and the social sciences, the HEMI tutorial establishes an interdisciplinary foundation for researchers with scientific and technical basis required to build intelligent, collaborative, and trustworthy embodied agents in the shared physical world. Dedicated website: hemi-tutorial.github.io
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: The Challenges of Human-Centered AI and Robotics: What We Want, Need, and are Getting From Human-Machine Interaction
abstract: Language-based AI is now ubiquitous, and user expectations for intelligent machines are scaling along with it: we expect machines to understand us, predict our needs and wants, do what we enjoy and prefer, and adapt as we change our moods and minds, learn, grow, and age. Physical AI, in the form of robotics, is the next major AI challenge, and it is not ready to leap into our daily lives yet. While massive investment is focused on functional behavior of humanoid robots (perceiving the world, moving around, and manipulating objects), human-robot interaction (HRI) is largely an afterthought, left for “later". This talk will discuss how bringing together robotics, AI, and machine learning for long-term user modeling, real-time multimodal behavioral signal processing, and affective computing is enabling machines to understand, interact, and adapt to users’ specific and ever-changing needs. We will overview methods and challenges of sparse and noisy heterogeneous, multi-modal, personal interaction data and of creating expressive agent and robot behavior toward understanding, coaching, motivating, and supporting a wide variety of user populations across the age span (infants, children, adults, elderly), ability span (typically developing, autism, anxiety, stroke, dementia), contexts (schools, therapy centers, homes), and deployment durations (from weeks to 6 months) through socially assistive robotics. We will discuss the challenges of understanding what we humans want from interactions with machines vs. what we need vs. what we are getting, and how those distinctions are shaping the future of not just AI and ML but society at large.
journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction

title: How Local AI Framing Shapes User Experience and Perceived Data Security with an Embodied AI Psychotherapist in VR
abstract: The prevalence of anxiety disorders has been increasing in recent years to an extent where the demand for treatment is difficult to meet with traditional therapy. Therefore, research efforts aim for scalable, cost-effective extensions thereof. One approach is the use of Virtual Reality-based exposure therapy controlled by an embodied AI therapist. However, stakeholders, such as patients and therapists, are reluctant to embrace this development due to data security concerns. Along with the global rise of cloud-based large language models, smaller local models have improved to the point where they can simulate social interaction in a convincing manner. This leads to greater data security at the cost of a slightly decreased capability. In our study, we let N = 60 participants interact with an embodied conversational agent controlled by local models (i.e., Speech-to-Text, Large Language Model, Text-to-Speech). One group was informed that they were interacting with cloud-based models, while the other group was told they were interacting with locally hosted, on-premise models. Our results reveal significantly higher user experience and perceived quality of response for the ’local’ condition. Further analysis indicates a significant increase in perceived data security regarding general AI use for the ’local’ condition after the interaction and a slight decrease for the ’cloud-based’ condition.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: "Nobody Told me Farming is not Only Farming": A Conversational AI Agent for Causal Loop Reasoning with Japan Farmers
abstract: As the agricultural industry becomes more interconnected and shaped by globalized markets, smallholder farmers face mounting challenges in navigating an increasingly complex and highly competitive business landscape. This paper reports a study in which a conversational AI system, Seseragi was used to help synthesize systemic knowledge through participatory causal loop diagramming with four farmers who possessed extensive lifelong experience in local agricultural practice. Despite some technical limitations posed by latency, the farmers provided promising feedback and acknowledged the benefits of reflective brainstorming guided by our system. Our findings and design implications offer valuable insights into co-designing AI agents that support individuals navigating complex systemic problems that exceed the scope of their own professional expertise, as exemplified by the agricultural context.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: CEMAS - a Configurable Embodied Multi-Agent System
abstract: This work presents CEMAS, a Configurable Embodied Multi-Agent System that enables one-to-many interactions between a human user and multiple Embodied Conversational Agents (ECAs), allowing the simulation of complex social interactions in extended reality (XR). The system comprises two layers: (1) an AI interaction layer that provides a modular, server-side voice-to-voice pipeline for dynamic verbal behavior together with a moderator-based turn-taking mechanism to coordinate multi-party conversations, and (2) an embodiment layer that manages the visual representation of ECAs in Unity and executes AI-generated non-verbal behaviors synchronized with spoken output. By combining modular conversational AI with coordinated multi-agent interaction and embodied behavior generation, CEMAS provides a configurable foundation for developing socially interactive multi-agent systems in XR and facilitates future research and applications in domains such as education, mental health, and collaborative human-AI decision making.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: Emerging Agency-Aware Interface Patterns in AI-in-the-Loop Platforms
abstract: AI agents increasingly act across tools, data, memory, and digital environments. This paper presents preliminary agency-aware interface patterns for AI-in-the-loop platforms. By analyzing emerging agentic platforms, we abstract heterogeneous UI mechanisms into six pattern families for making delegated agency visible, controllable, and revocable.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: How Humans Evaluate Headline-Map Climate Change Misinformation with Multi-Agent (In)consistent Guidance?
abstract: Climate misinformation on social media often combines misleading headlines with professional-looking maps, increasing the perceived credibility of false or decontextualized claims. As users increasingly rely on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for credibility support, they may encounter either consistent or conflicting recommendations from multiple AI assistants. This ongoing study examines how people evaluate headline-map climate change misinformation under parallel and independent guidance from multiple MLLMs. Using eight real climate-related social media posts, we designed an interactive interface in which 26 participants rated the credibility of headlines and maps while receiving parallel assessments from ChatGPT 5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, with options to inspect model reasoning and engage in follow-up dialogue. Preliminary findings show that consistent MLLMs guidance reduced variation in human credibility assessments, especially for misinformation headlines: when both models agreed that a headline was unreliable, participants tended to align with the consensus and provide strongly negative ratings. In contrast, inconsistent MLLMs guidance generated greater uncertainty and variation in human credibility assessments. Under conflicting MLLMs guidance, participants did not simply average model scores; instead, their judgments shifted toward neutrality and avoided extreme ratings. Analysis of user–MLLMs dialogue further shows that participants used the models to clarify scientific concepts, trace sources, and interpret map-based evidence.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: LLMs with a Heart: Using Contextual Heartbeat Haptics to Add Feeling to Text and Audio LLM Interactions
abstract: Conversational LLMs are physiologically inert, lacking the embodied signals that shape how emotion, urgency, and presence are perceived in human interaction. We introduce a contextually generated haptic heartbeat that is autonomously produced by an LLM based on the affective trajectory of its output and delivered through commodity devices. This work presents an in-progress exploration of heartbeat haptics as a novel multimodal channel for conversational AI, reporting preliminary results from a study evaluating text and audio with heartbeat haptics that provides early directional evidence that LLM-driven heartbeat signals may modulate perceived arousal and valence, enhance emotional expressiveness, and increase credibility and immersion relative to unimodal interactions. These findings are preliminary and should be interpreted conservatively, but they point to a potentially meaningful breakthrough for multimodal interface design: simulated physiological cues may add a new layer of affective embodiment to disembodied systems. We introduce a tightly coupled language-to-haptics pipeline and outline the next steps needed to establish robustness, scalability, and cross-modal coherence, suggesting that LLM-generated heartbeat haptics could open a promising design space for more expressive, credible, and experientially rich conversational agents.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: State as an Inclusive Interaction Substrate: Rethinking Multimodal AI Beyond Conversation for Diverse Users
abstract: AI-based multimodal interaction is often framed as a move from graphical interfaces to conversation: users speak or type, and the system replies. While this shift can reduce barriers for some users, it can also reproduce exclusion when conversational systems assume normative language, typical social cues, or a single preferred modality of interaction. This position paper argues for a different interaction substrate for inclusive AI: generated state. Instead of treating text, speech, or gesture as the final interface, AI systems can translate diverse inputs into persistent, inspectable, manipulable, and multimodally renderable state objects. Such state can then be visualised as a dashboard, spoken as an audio summary, simplified into step-by-step instructions, edited through direct manipulation, queried through an agent, or transformed into alternative representations for users with different sensory, cognitive, linguistic, or social needs. Building on state generation for workplace coordination, we outline how a state-centric paradigm can support more inclusive multimodal interaction by separating the underlying coordination state from any single modality of access. We illustrate this idea through scenarios involving blind users, users with limited language proficiency, neurodivergent users, and mixed-ability teams. We conclude with design principles and research questions for inclusive state-generating AI systems.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: AI-based Analysis and Generation of Nonverbal Behavior: NEUROGES® as a Neuropsychologically Grounded Behavior Taxonomy for Health Applications
abstract: Health and therapeutic applications impose stringent requirements on the analysis of human nonverbal behavior and the generation of behavior for socially interactive agents (SIAs): both must be not only natural-looking but also clinically appropriate, explainable, and safe. Current approaches fall short on both sides: representation systems lack functional grounding, and generation prioritizes perceptual naturalness over communicative function. With this position paper, we propose to employ NEUROGES® as a shared taxonomy that addresses this gap across analysis, generation, and evaluation. For analysis, it provides a neuropsychologically grounded, clinically validated categorization of nonverbal behavior, registering movement units linked to cognitive, emotional, and interactive processes. The same categories can be used to guide the generation of SIA behavior, allowing domain experts to specify behavioral constraints at the level of communicative function (e.g., suppressing dominance cues in anxiety-provoking situations). This symmetry allows direct evaluation of SIA behavior against NEUROGES-annotated human references, enabling cross-system comparison on a justified scale. We propose a research agenda, arguing that this approach is essential wherever generated behavior must be appropriate, explainable, and safe, which is most relevant in health applications.
journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction

title: Poster: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Authentication and Messaging for Agent-to-Agent Communication
