title: Individual Ta’lim Traektoriyasini Loyihalashtirishning Pedagogik Va Didaktik Tamoyillari
abstract: This article presents a theoretical and systemic analysis of the pedagogical and didactic principles underlying the design of individual educational trajectories. In contemporary education, students differ substantially in prior knowledge, interests and pace of development, which undermines the effectiveness of a uniform instructional model. The aim of the article is to clarify the concept of an individual educational trajectory and to systematize the pedagogical (learner-centeredness, subjectivity, adaptability) and didactic (consistency, systematicity, conscious activity, individual approach) principles that should guide its design. The study applies theoretical, comparative-typological and statistical analysis; in particular, the PISA-2025 international assessment results are used to substantiate the degree of differentiation among Uzbek schoolchildren. The findings confirm that the wide variance in learning outcomes is a necessary pedagogical condition for designing individual trajectories. The article concludes with a step-by-step model for implementing individual educational trajectories in practice.

title: Inklyuziv Ta’lim Muhitida Generativ Ai Vositalari Yordamida Ingliz Tilini O‘qitish Metodikasini Takomillashtirish
abstract: The study analyzes the potential of generative AI technologies to address students' individual learning needs, differentiate instructional materials, develop English language skills (lexical, grammatical, communicative, and receptive-productive), provide immediate feedback, and support independent learning. The methodological framework of the study comprises systemic, comparative, linguo-didactic, and modeling methods. The results indicate that generative AI tools create additional opportunities for transitioning from a "one-size-fits-all" assignment approach to an individualized and differentiated teaching model in inclusive English language education. At the same time, issues such as the accuracy of AI-generated content, academic integrity, data privacy, the risk of excessive student reliance on AI, and the maintenance of teacher oversight were identified as critical methodological considerations.

title: Inventory System Design And Development at PT. Mitra Puding Mas - Palm Oil Mill
abstract: PT. Mitra Puding Mas – Palm Oil Mill is a palm oil processing company with intensive operational activities that depend heavily on the availability of inventory, including machine spare parts, raw materials, and production support equipment. However, its inventory management is still conducted manually using notebooks and spreadsheets, resulting in recording errors, data duplication, archive loss, and delays in preparing inventory reports. This study aims to design and develop a structured and accurate web-based inventory information system capable of providing real-time stock information to minimize potential losses caused by machine downtime and improve operational efficiency. Data were collected through literature review, direct field observation, and interviews with the Head of Administration (KTU) of PT. Mitra Puding Mas – Palm Oil Mill. The system was developed using the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture with the Laravel framework, PHP programming language, and MySQL database. System functionality was tested using Black-Box Testing. The results show that the developed system successfully integrates login, item category management, supplier management, incoming and outgoing inventory records, purchase transactions, and automatic report generation, including invoices and official transaction documents. The implementation transforms manual procedures into computerized processes, reduces human error, and supports faster and more accurate managerial decision-making based on valid inventory data.

title: Design and Implementation of an IoT Based Smart Home System for Motion Triggered Object Detection and Automated Ventilation Control
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart homes enable the automation of home devices to improve comfort and security. This study designs and develops a smart home system in which passive infrared (PIR) sensors are used only to detect motion, while an ESP32-CAM and YOLOv3 are used for camera-based object detection and class labeling. A human-presence indication is therefore generated only when a PIR-triggered camera frame contains a person detected by YOLOv3; PIR motion alone is not interpreted as occupancy. The system also features MQ-2 sensor-based gas leak detection and automatic ventilation control using a servo motor as a safety response. Data and alerts are transmitted through Telegram, while Blynk is used for integrated monitoring. System development followed requirements analysis, design, implementation, functional testing, and corrective refinement. The dedicated YOLOv3 object test documented 11 confidence values ranging from 53% to 99% (descriptive mean 86.2%; median 94%); these values are detector confidence scores and not classification accuracy because no annotated ground-truth benchmark was used. In an additional 11-trial illuminance-oriented functional test, object detection succeeded in all six trials conducted at 624–950 lux and failed in all five trials conducted at 0–147 lux. The contribution of this work is an event-driven IoT architecture that coordinates motion sensing, visual verification, remote notification, and closed-loop gas mitigation, together with field-oriented evaluation of lighting effects on low-cost camera-based detection.

title: Integrated Irrigation and Disease Management Strategies for Sustainable Wheat Production and Improved Plant Health and Grain Yield
abstract: Wheat production was expected to provide reliable grain quality and farmer income while using less water and facing climatic variability, soil degradation, disease development, and rising energy costs. This literature-based paper critically synthesized verified research on irrigation, plant disease management, irrigation–disease interactions, sustainability, digital agriculture, and the Pakistan/developing-economy context. It considered irrigation and plant health as related management areas rather than completely separate input decisions. The available evidence did not identify a universal irrigation technology or deficit percentage. Instead, it supported a context-specific approach that considered stored soil water and rainfall, protected important growth stages, managed canopy humidity and nitrogen, used resistant cultivars and clean seed, and applied surveillance, forecasting, and fungicides when justified. Global and China-focused studies reported that moderate deficit or optimized water-saving irrigation could improve water productivity, whereas severe water deficit commonly reduced yield. Jointing/stem elongation was repeatedly identified as an important stage for avoiding water stress, while anthesis and early grain filling were also important when water availability and disease risk required attention. Disease-management evidence emphasized genetic resistance, sanitation, crop rotation, scouting, and forecasting before chemical control. Fusarium head blight required particular attention to weather conditions around anthesis, residue inoculum, cultivar resistance, fungicide timing, and deoxynivalenol risk. Irrigation increased yield without increasing disease in some environments, although dense nitrogen-rich canopies, overhead wetting, and saturated soils could favor foliar diseases and waterlogging. Digital tools were considered decision-support infrastructure that linked observations, analysis, and management actions. Wheat-specific evidence was relatively stronger for soil-moisture scheduling and weather-based stripe-rust forecasting, whereas many claims involving artificial intelligence, UAVs, and variable-rate irrigation remained predictive or transferable rather than directly supported by causal field evidence. Evidence from Pakistan indicated dependence on groundwater, salinity and waterlogging problems, uneven disease surveillance, and barriers to technology adoption. Differences among official statistics also indicated the need for careful reconciliation rather than simple averaging. The paper proposed an integrated framework involving diagnosis, planning, stage-aware irrigation, plant-health protection, evaluation, and seasonal feedback. It also identified the need for multi-location and multi-season studies that evaluated water use, disease, grain quality, energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, profitability, and equity together.

CrossCD-Eval: a unified framework with domain-aware feature normalization for cross-domain remote sensing change detection
abstract: Change detection (CD) in remote sensing imagery is essential for monitoring urban growth, land-use transformation, and environmental dynamics. However, cross-domain change detection remains challenging due to distribution shifts caused by differences in geographic regions, spatial resolutions, sensor/acquisition conditions, temporal periods, and annotation protocols. This paper introduces CrossCD-Eval, a unified framework for evaluating the generalization of deep learning-based change detection models under in-domain, cross-domain, and few-shot domain adaptation settings. Five recent models, namely GLAFormer1, Change-Mamba2, EHCTNet3, ELGC-Net4, and STNet5, are evaluated using CLCD, HRSCD, and LEVIR-CD. To reduce representation-level domain mismatch, we propose a Domain-Aware Feature Normalization (DAFN) module that aligns source and target feature statistics as a lightweight feature-level adaptation component. Experimental results show that all models achieve strong in-domain performance but degrade under cross-domain transfer, confirming the impact of domain shift. DAFN improves cross-domain and few-shot adaptation performance, with larger gains observed under more challenging source–target shifts. Repeated 10-shot experiments over five random target-sample selections further show that DAFN improves adaptation stability, reducing IoU standard deviation by up to 22.7%. An additional ablation and baseline-comparison study demonstrates that the observed gains are not solely due to preprocessing. Compared with full preprocessing, AdaBN, adversarial feature alignment, and the instance-normalization-based CrossCDNet baseline, DAFN provides additional feature-level adaptation benefits, especially when combined with strong backbones such as STNet.

title: Spectral index and machine learning-based evaluation of coastal urban thermal dynamics using google earth engine
abstract: This present study introduces a cloud-based geospatial and machine learning framework for assessing coastal urban heat island (UHI) dynamics in Thoothukudi coastal region, Southern India, using 12 seasonal Landsat composites (2010–2025) processed through Google Earth Engine (GEE). Seasonal classification followed Indian Meteorological Department definitions: Summer (March-June), Northeast Monsoon (October-November) and Winter (December-February). Multi-sensor Landsat Collection 2 Tier 1 Level-2 data included Landsat 5/7 (2010), Landsat 8 (2015) and Landsat 8/9 (2020, 2025). Land surface temperature (LST) was retrieved using USGS Collection 2 scale-factor protocol, capped to 0–65 °C to suppress cloud-contaminated pixels. UHI intensity (UHI = LST − P₂₅(LST)) and Urban Thermal Field Variance Index (UTFVI) were computed alongside four spectral indices (NDVI, NDBI, NDWI, NDMI). Summer was the hottest season in three of four observation years (mean LST: 38.69–48.67 °C). The 2020 Northeast Monsoon composite was excluded due to cloud contamination. Mean UHI intensity ranged from 2.03 to 5.17 °C. Pearson correlation confirmed NDBI as the strongest positive LST predictor ( r = 0.30–0.60), while NDMI mirrors this inversely. Random Forest and Gradient Tree Boosting models were trained on seven predictors using dual validation (70/30 split and 2 km spatial block cross-validation). Model performance yielded R² of 0.301–0.476 and RMSE of 2.74–6.23 °C with physically realistic values. GTB permutation feature importance identified NDBI and SWIR1 as dominant predictors. Ensemble scenario illustrations for 2030 and 2050, presented as linear extrapolations rather than climate-model forecasts, suggest sustained thermal stress in industrial and port zones with explicit uncertainty quantification (± 2.75 to ± 8.61 °C). The study demonstrates that rigorously validated Landsat time-series analysis provides actionable coastal urban thermal intelligence for heat adaptation planning aligned with SDGs 11, 13 and 3. The framework is applied here as the first four-epoch, IMD-season-resolved thermal characterisation of the Thoothukudi coast and the 2030 and 2050 outputs are intended to support the spatial targeting of persistent thermal hotspots rather than the prediction of absolute future temperatures.

title: Image-embedded prompt injection vulnerability of vision-language models in dental radiology: a cross-vendor attack–defense evaluation
abstract: Image-embedded prompt injection—adversarial text rendered into the pixel data of a medical image—is an emerging security threat to vision-language models (VLMs) explored for clinical decision support. In an adversarial stress test using a permissive elicitation prompt, we assessed four production-tier VLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, MedGemma 4B) on 270 DenTeX dental panoramic radiographs under four attack classes, across 58,320 logged inference calls. All four models were vulnerable, with paired attack success rates (ASR) up to 62.6% (95% CI 58.5–66.7%, GPT-4o) and model-specific profiles. We benchmarked four defenses—ROI cropping, spotlighting, OCR-based text sanitization, and ProvDent, a provenance-aware defense with bounded clinical abstention—against a re-executed undefended control. OCR-based sanitization reduced pooled ASR from 15.6% to 0.2%; ProvDent reached 7.5% when every abstention is scored as an attack success, or 1.1% on the 93.5% of cases it answered, escalating the remainder for human review. On this high-prevalence benchmark (245/270 abnormal), defenses left clean-image sensitivity essentially unchanged (99.4–99.9% vs. 99.7%); the scarcity of normal images precluded assessment of specificity. These findings establish image-embedded prompt injection as a reproducible cross-vendor weakness under stress-test conditions, informing pre-deployment security evaluation rather than deployed-system risk.

Age-specific genomic and transcriptomic variation reveals limited evidence for cis-regulatory interactions modulating aging in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
abstract: The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a well-established model for studying the genetic basis of complex traits, and it is a powerful system for investigating mechanisms of aging. Here, we examine the genomic and transcriptomic factors contributing to increased replicative age in recombinant yeast populations harboring standing genetic variation. Using Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), we isolated young and aged cohort pairs across twelve biological replicates and sequenced their progeny to assess patterns of differentiation at the nucleotide and transcription levels. Most differentiated alleles were located in coding regions, including significant variants within 132 unique genes. Transcriptomic analysis revealed 60 differentially expressed genes in aged populations, including 18 genes with increased expression in aged cohorts, and 42 genes with decreased expression. Although only two genes (RFA3 and WSC4) were implicated in both genomic and transcriptomic analyses, functional overlap associated with protein homeostasis, DNA repair, and cell cycle regulation was evident across datasets. Notably, we found no strong evidence that differentially expressed genes were more likely to occur in close proximity to significant gene variants. This suggests that late-life survival is not predominantly governed by background-independent local cis-regulatory interactions. These findings are consistent with a polygenic architecture in which distinct genotypes may promote longevity through diverse regulatory mechanisms.

title: Haplotype-Phased Chromosome-Scale Genome Assemblies of Satsuma mandarin Uncover Structural and Transcriptional Divergence Between Parental Haplotypes and Structural Variations in Mutant Lineages.
abstract: Citrus, a widely cultivated Rutaceae crop, comprises numerous varieties, among which Satsuma mandarin (Citrus unshiu Marc.) is the most widely cultivated in Japan. In this study, a high-quality, chromosome-scale, haplotype-phased genome assembly of Satsuma mandarin ("Miyagawa wase") was generated using PacBio HiFi sequencing, Omni-C scaffolding, and a trio binning strategy incorporating its parental genomes (Kishu mandarin (C. kinokuni) and Kunenbo mandarin (C. nobilis)). This approach enabled the complete separation of parental haplotypes. To obtain accurate gene models, we performed long-read transcriptome sequencing across eight tissues and developmental stages, producing comprehensive gene annotations for each haploid genome. Comparative genomic analyses of the two haplotypes revealed extensive structural divergence, multiple sequence polymorphisms, and large insertions/deletions enriched for long terminal repeat retrotransposons. Whole-genome graph-based analysis and synteny comparisons further identified chromosome-specific patterns of sequence diversity, providing new insights into the evolutionary origins of Satsuma mandarin haplotypes. Transcriptome analyses uncovered widespread allele-specific gene expression and tissue-dependent regulatory divergence between the two parental haplotypes; notably, mature fruit tissue exhibited pronounced haplotype-biased transcription, suggesting differential contributions from Kishu- and Kunenbo-derived alleles during fruit maturation. Additionally, comparative genomic analyses of bud sport and nucellar embryony mutant lineages revealed haplotype-specific patterns of variation, providing insights into mutation accumulation during vegetative propagation and nucellar embryony in clonal citrus cultivars. This fully haplotype-phased genomic and transcriptomic resource, which has been implemented in MiGD2 (https://mikan.dna.naro.go.jp), provides a powerful foundation for genome-assisted breeding, identification of functional and lineage-specific alleles, and elucidation of mutation-derived variation in Japanese citrus cultivars.

title: First report of Enterobacter ludwigii causing root rot of Rehmannia glutinosa in China
abstract: Rehmannia glutinosa Libosch. is an economically important medicinal crop whose tuberous roots are widely used in traditional Chinese medicine. In January 2026, root rot was observed in a commercial field in Wuzhi Town (35.10°N, 113.40°E), Jiaozuo City, Henan Province, China. The disease incidence in the surveyed field was approximately 50%. Affected plants exhibited foliar wilt, brown-to-black root necrosis, root decay, and reduced vigor. Roots and growth-substrate samples were collected from 10 symptomatic and healthy plants. Root segments (2 cm) from lesion margins and healthy roots were surface-disinfested in 0.1% sodium hypochlorite for 5 min, rinsed three times with sterile distilled water, plated on nutrient agar (NA) and potato dextrose agar (PDA), and incubated at 25°C in darkness. PDA was included to recover and monitor other microorganisms associated with diseased tissues, whereas bacterial isolates used in subsequent tests were recovered and purified on NA. After approximately 3 days, morphologically similar bacterial colonies were recovered from 80% of symptomatic roots. Five bacterial isolates were obtained. Pathogenicity assays were conducted on healthy R. glutinosa plants under greenhouse conditions to fulfill Koch's postulates. For each isolate, bacterial suspensions were adjusted to 1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL. Each treatment contained three plants, and the experiment was repeated three times independently. Roots were superficially wounded with a sterile scalpel to create small wounds, and each plant was inoculated with 5 mL of bacterial suspension. Plants treated with sterile nutrient broth and noninoculated plants served as negative controls. Plants were covered with polyethylene bags for 24 to 48 h to maintain high humidity and maintained in a greenhouse at 25 ± 2°C under a 16-h light/8-h dark photoperiod. Ten days after inoculation, plants inoculated with isolate X21 developed root rot and wilt similar to those observed in the field, whereas plants inoculated with the other four isolates and both control groups remained asymptomatic. Bacteria with colony morphology identical to that of X21 were reisolated from symptomatic roots, thereby fulfilling Koch's postulates (Fig. 1). Isolate X21 formed creamy-white colonies on NA after 24 h at 25°C. The partial 16S rRNA gene was amplified with primers 27F/1492R (Kai et al. 2019), and the sequence was deposited in GenBank (PZ212876.1). Because 16S rRNA sequences provide limited resolution within the Enterobacter cloacae complex, partial gyrB (1,008 bp) and rpoB (991 bp) genes were also sequenced. gyrB was amplified with primers gyrB-F (5′-CCSACSGACGTGAAGATG-3′) and gyrB-R (5′-TCCACTGCATSGCGACTTC-3′), and the resulting sequence was deposited in GenBank (PZ707229). rpoB was amplified with primers rpoB-F (5′-AACCAGTTCCGCGTTGGCCTGG-3′) and rpoB-R (5′-CCTGAACAACACGCTCGGA-3′), and the resulting sequence was deposited in GenBank (PZ707228). Sequences from X21 and type or type-material strains of the E. cloacae complex were aligned using MUSCLE v5.3 (Edgar 2022) and trimmed to the regions covered by the X21 sequences. Maximum-likelihood analyses were performed in IQ-TREE v2.4.0 (Minh et al. 2020) using best-fit models selected according to the Bayesian information criterion and 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates. Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 was used as the outgroup. The 16S rRNA tree placed X21 within the E. cloacae complex but did not reliably resolve it at the species level. In contrast, X21 clustered with the E. ludwigii type strain EN-119T in both the gyrB and rpoB trees, with bootstrap support of 100 and 88%, respectively. An MLSA tree based on concatenated gyrB + rpoB sequences (1,999 aligned positions) placed X21 with E. ludwigii EN-119T with 100% bootstrap support (Fig. 2). These results identified X21 as E. ludwigii. Enterobacter ludwigii was described as a member of the E. cloacae complex (Hoffmann et al. 2005). Previous studies associated Enterobacter aerogenes and unidentified Enterobacter spp. with root rot or wilt of R. glutinosa (Wang et al. 2018; Li et al. 2020). However, to our knowledge, this is the first report of E. ludwigii causing root rot of R. glutinosa in China. This disease may threaten stand establishment and root production, highlighting the need for surveillance and management in R. glutinosa production areas.

title: First report of Lasiodiplodia theobromae causing dieback of Common Fig ( Ficus carica ) in Morelos, Mexico
abstract: The common fig (Ficus carica L.) is widely cultivated in semi-arid and subtropical regions. In June 2025, five-year-old fig trees cv. Black Mission exhibiting dieback symptoms were observed in Morelos, Mexico (18°52'29.59"N, 98°47'01.65" W). Among 650 trees assessed, disease incidence was 18%. Affected trees exhibited foliar chlorosis, progressive branch dieback, canopy decline, and retention of dried leaves on affected shoots. Fungal isolates were obtained from twenty symptomatic fig trees. Tissues were surface-disinfected using 3% NaOCl for 5 min, rinsed twice with autoclaved distilled water, and then placed on potato dextrose agar (PDA; Bioxon®) medium. Ten single-spore isolates with morphological characteristics consistent with Lasiodiplodia spp. were obtained and maintained on PDA. The plates were incubated at 25°C ± 2 °C for 14 days, during which colonies produced abundant white aerial mycelium that turned grey after 14 days and developed black pycnidia. Microscopic examination revealed conidia that were initially hyaline, aseptate, thick-walled, subovoid to ellipsoid with rounded ends and granular content. Mature conidia became dark brown, one-septate, and longitudinally striate. Conidia measured 18.33–23.63 (mean = 20.66) µm in length and 11–15.3 (mean = 12.48) µm in width (n = 100 per isolate). Two representative isolates were selected for molecular and pathogenicity analyses, and deposited in the Culture Collection of Phytopathogenic Fungi of the Department of Agricultural Parasitology at Chapingo Autonomous University under accession numbers UACh-LH1 and UACh-LH2. For molecular identification, genomic DNA was extracted from the mycelium following the cetyltrimethylammonium bromide method (Doyle and Doyle 1990). The internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region, parts of the beta-tubulin (β-tubulin) and partial sequences of the translation elongation factor 1-alpha (TEF) genes were amplified by PCR, and sequenced using the primer pairs ITS5/ITS4 (White et al. 1990), Bt2a/Bt2b (Glass and Donaldson 1995) and EF1-728F/986R (Carbone and Kohn 1999), respectively. BLASTn analyses showed that UACh-LH1 had 99.79, 100, and 99.32% identity, whereas UACh-LH2 had 100, 99.77, and 96.67% identity for ITS, β-tubulin, and TEF, respectively, compared with the ex-neotype culture CBS 164.96 of Lasiodiplodia theobromae. Sequences were deposited in GenBank under accession numbers ITS: PZ051210, PZ091917; β-tubulin: PZ056668, PZ279902; TEF: PZ279900, PZ279901. A phylogenetic analysis using concatenated sequences with the Neighbor-Joining method placed isolates UACh-LH1 and UACh-LH2 in the same clade as L. theobromae. Pathogenicity was evaluated in two pathogenicity assays, each independently repeated twice. In the first assay, one-year-old healthy potted fig plants cv. Black Mission were sprayed with a conidial suspension (1.75 × 10⁵ spores mL⁻¹), with five plants inoculated with UACh-LH1 and five with UACh-LH2. Five control plants received sterile distilled water. All plants were incubated at 25 ± 2 °C and 80% relative humidity. Inoculated plants developed dieback symptoms and pycnidia after 35 days, whereas controls remained symptomless. A second assay was performed under field conditions using fig trees cv. Black Mission. For each isolate, 10 branches, 10 leaves, and 10 fruits were wound-inoculated with PDA plugs containing actively growing mycelium. Inoculated tissues were enclosed in poly-bags to maintain 100% relative humidity. Corresponding control tissues (10 branches, 10 leaves, and 10 fruits) were inoculated with sterile PDA plugs. Necrotic lesions developed after 7 days, whereas controls remained symptomless. Lesion length was measured using a digital caliper. The pathogen was successfully reisolated from all inoculated plants and tissues, whereas no fungi were recovered from controls, thus fulfilling Koch's postulates. The reisolated cultures exhibited the characteristic colony and conidial morphology of Lasiodiplodia, consistent with the original isolates. Both pathogenicity assays were independently repeated twice, with similar results. To our knowledge, this is the first report of Lasiodiplodia theobromae causing dieback of Ficus carica in Mexico. This report expands the documented host–disease distribution of L. theobromae in Mexico and provides a baseline for disease diagnosis and surveillance in fig-producing areas.

title: An End-to-End Framework for Modelling Pneumatic Soft Robots Based on Differentiable Finite Element Methods
abstract: Soft robots present significant modelling challenges due to their non-linearity, complex dynamics and potentially intricate geometries. These difficulties in accurate system identification and dynamics modelling limit their applications in precise robotics tasks. Prior modelling approaches typically suffer from trade-offs in accuracy, computational efficiency, or speed. The differentiable finite element method (FEM) offers a promising balance between these desiderata for soft robot modelling, and enables the use of gradients for efficient calibration and trajectory optimisation. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end differentiable FEM-based framework designed to streamline modelling and system identification for pneumatic soft robots, enabling the generation of reliable models for downstream tasks. The framework automates the conversion of computer-aided designs into voxelised tetrahedral viscoelastic FEM meshes that accurately represent the robot's geometry and actuation mechanism. By integrating easily acquired point cloud data with differentiable FEM, the framework achieves precise identification of material and dynamic actuation parameters using a minimal experimental setup. Additionally, the differentiable nature of the model facilitates trajectory optimisation by leveraging gradients from robot dynamics and contact interactions. We validate the framework by modelling a complex bellow-shaped pneumatic soft robot and demonstrate its efficacy in real-world motion planning tasks. Experimental results indicate high modelling accuracy, with a maximum positional error of less than 3 mm, and successful application in tasks such as path following and grasping.

title: Contextual Microplastic Impacts on Croplands From Field Trials and Global Synthesis
abstract: Microplastic accumulation is an increasingly widespread anthropogenic disturbance in agricultural soils, yet ecological risk assessments remain dominated by simplified laboratory assays that may not capture context‐dependent responses under field conditions. Here, we combined a five‐year experiment across four semi‐arid cropland sites with a global synthesis restricted exclusively to outdoor field observations to quantify microplastic effects on crop yield, soil quality, and ecosystem multifunctionality. Under a high microplastic loading (0.2% w/w), we detected no consistent negative functional responses across crops, sites, and growing years. The field‐only synthesis revealed weak average effects but substantial cross‐study heterogeneity. Plant presence was associated with weaker effects, with vegetated systems showing milder changes in soil quality and ecosystem multifunctionality than plant‐free soils. Biodegradable polymers did not show a consistent ecological advantage over conventional polymers across field settings. Our findings indicate that effects inferred primarily from laboratory studies cannot be directly extrapolated to the field scale. Importantly, weak functional responses do not address crop internal microplastic uptake, dietary exposure, or toxicological risk, which require separate assessment. These results provide a more realistic basis for assessing the consequences of microplastic pollution for agricultural ecosystem functioning and resilience under global change.

title: Not All Differences Matter: Variability Exploration of Domain Models via Agentic AI
abstract: Domain modeling is inherently interpretive: the same textual description may yield solutions that differ in structure, abstraction, and scope. Not all such differences constitute errors. Some reflect legitimate alternative representations and well-justified modeling decisions, while others stem from misconceptions or misapplied constructs. Existing evaluation approaches, however, tend to treat all deviations uniformly, thereby penalizing valid modeling competence and allowing real errors to pass undetected. To address this gap, we present VEGO-AI (Variability Exploration via Guideline Operationalization and Agentic Intelligence), an agentic framework that explicitly distinguishes between substantial (systematic and meaningful) and occasional (sporadic or erroneous) variability. VEGO-AI comprises four coordinated LLM-powered agents: (1) a Language Advisor; (2) a Domain Advisor that produces evolving reference guidelines capturing valid modeling alternatives; (3) a Model Inspector that assesses compliance while iteratively refining these guidelines; and (4) a Variability Explorer that identifies and classifies recurring deviation patterns. We evaluated VEGO-AI in the context of a university-level modeling course. The results demonstrate that the framework successfully differentiates between substantial and occasional variability, offering a basis for model assessment and suggesting directions for rethinking evaluation practices in domain modeling.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems

title: From Unfinished to Done: Bridging the MDE Implementation Gap with Constrained LLMs
abstract: Model-driven engineering (MDE) excels at ensuring architectural consistency and managing complexity, yet extending generated code skeletons with project-specific business logic often remains a time-consuming manual task. Conversely, large language models (LLMs) offer immense flexibility in coding but may produce vibe-coded results—software that looks correct but fails to adhere to intended architectures and implicit requirements. An open challenge lies in harnessing the adaptability of LLMs to handle implementation details without sacrificing the deterministic correctness of the MDE scaffolding. Previous attempts have largely relied on unconstrained coding assistants or required a human in the loop for interacting with the LLM. To overcome this, we introduce Agentic Gap Filling, a hybrid pipeline where LLM prompts are embedded directly within the model to drive the generation of code skeletons. The generated code contains protected TODO regions, which LLM agents subsequently resolve and a jury of LLM review agents and separate testing agents immediately validate. We integrate this approach into the MontiThings framework, demonstrating a workflow where models define the architecture of a project while artificial intelligence (AI) agents act as developers and reviewers, filling in the logic. This synergy ensures the structural integrity of the generated system while providing the flexibility of LLMs to adapt to various domain requirements. Our evaluation across 32 test configurations demonstrates that this multiagent workflow achieves up to 93.21% functional accuracy after four iterations, while preserving the structural integrity of the generated system.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems

title: Realizing a Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for the Graphical Language Server Platform (GLSP)
abstract: Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) offers strong abstractions but remains hindered in practice by complex tooling and steep learning curves. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) promise intuitive, natural-language interaction with modeling environments; however, existing approaches—such as direct API interaction, DSL generation, or manipulation of serialized models—exhibit limited reliability, scalability, and semantic precision. This paper presents a structured integration of LLMs into graphical modeling environments via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We design and implement a reusable MCP server for the Graphical Language Server Platform (GLSP), enabling LLM agents to interact with models through semantically grounded, tool-based operations rather than direct model generation. We contribute (i) a reference architecture for MCP-based integration into GLSP derived from a systematic literature review of MCP implementations, (ii) design principles for mapping modeling concepts to MCP primitives and abstraction levels, and (iii) an empirical evaluation assessing the impact of MCP-based interaction on downstream modeling tasks. Our results show that MCP-based interactions significantly improve both information retrieval (perfect precision/recall across tasks) and model manipulation (reducing syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic errors), while also improving scalability and efficiency compared to serialization-based approaches. The MCP server enables robust modification of existing models, a key limitation of prior approaches. These findings demonstrate that structured, tool-mediated interaction is a crucial enabler for reliable AI-assisted modeling. The presented MCP–GLSP Server constitutes a reusable artifact applicable across GLSP-based tools, providing a practical foundation to advance intelligent modeling assistance.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems

title: Reasoning Scaffolds for AI-Assisted Behavioural Modelling: A Logical-Square Instantiation
abstract: AI assistants are increasingly used to support behavioural modelling from natural-language requirements, yet they provide little assurance that the resulting models are logically coherent. We argue that this limitation stems not only from the capabilities of large language models but also from the absence of explicit reasoning structures mediating interactions between human analysts and AI systems. To address this limitation, we introduce the notion of a reasoning scaffold as an explicit intermediate modelling artefact and propose scaffolded behavioural modelling, in which AI agents reason over such scaffolds rather than rely solely on conversational interactions. As a first instantiation of this broader concept, we investigate logical squares as one possible reasoning scaffold that exposes contradictions, alternatives, implications and missing behavioural concepts, and introduce scaffold-aware agents that exploit these structures to support systematic behavioural exploration. Finally, we outline a research agenda for reasoning scaffolds and argue that they provide a foundation for more explainable and verifiable AI-assisted modelling environments, and may facilitate future correct-by-construction approaches.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 29th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems

title: Sema Core: An Open, Embeddable AI Coding Agent Runtime for the IDE and Beyond
abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly used in software development, but most are delivered as integrated applications whose reasoning logic is tied to a specific interface, model provider, and deployment setting. This coupling makes it difficult for researchers and tool builders to reuse agent capabilities across different developer tools, workflows, and deployment environments. We present Sema Core, an open, embeddable AI coding agent runtime that is decoupled from any particular client and distributed as a standalone npm package. Through a compact API and typed event stream, Sema Core allows different clients to reuse the same reasoning loop, tool system, permissions, background tasks, Skills/MCP integration, and model adapters. We demonstrate the Sema Core runtime through Sema Code, a flagship VSCode extension built as a thin UI client, and additional clients including a multi-channel assistant and an industrial programming assistant. We provide source code, documentation, a demo video, and an archived release.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Systems, Programming, Languages, and Applications: Software for Humanity

title: Safe: Automaton-Theoretic Runtime Monitoring of Blackbox Distributed Systems
abstract: Modern safety-critical systems are increasingly built from blackbox components: cloud services, third-party APIs, autonomous systems, and AI agents whose source code or internal state may be unavailable for inspection. To certify safe and secure inter-component interactions in such systems, security and compliance teams must enforce policies over sequential and nested call/return patterns in the execution, along with the data values exchanged between the components. Furthermore, the blackbox setting necessitates decoupling the policy enforcement mechanism from the system implementation. To this end, I design Safe⟨ T⟩, an automaton-theoretic runtime monitoring framework for specifying and enforcing control-flow and data-aware policies over black-box distributed systems. My technique is blackbox and non-invasive, i.e., it requires no code access or implementation changes. To realize this framework, I have built a distributed runtime monitor on top of an emerging network infrastructure layer that can control inter-component communication. I have demonstrated Safe⟨ T⟩ on cloud microservices and am now extending it to agentic AI systems.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Systems, Programming, Languages, and Applications: Software for Humanity

title: In the Age of AI Coding Agents, Keeping the Engineer in Software Engineering (Keynote)
abstract: There appears to be two distinct camps gathering steam as AI coding agents get increasingly adept at generating software on the basis of some light natural language specifications: those who want to maximally remove the ‘error-prone’ sentient bags of mostly water at the keyboard and those who stubbornly assert their own relevance as their AI-enhanced coding interfaces run off and make significant (but also often not-quite-right) contributions to the code base without even checking in. I fall into the latter camp, and in this talk, I’ll make the case for why the former camp is completely wrong—as long as we invest in designing the interfaces necessary to give our sentient water bag selves meaningful oversight and agency. Perhaps even more importantly, these interfaces might help preserve the meaning that brought us to this field in the first place: building up (rather than eroding) our understanding of the systems, languages, and software applications that fascinate us when our context allows for or demands it.
journal: Companion Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Systems, Programming, Languages, and Applications: Software for Humanity

title: Trust the View That Sees the Target: Mining Cross-View Conflicts for Reliability-Gated Disaster Damage Assessment
abstract: After a disaster, building damage is assessed from overhead tiles and ground-level photographs, and most methods fuse the two views symmetrically, trusting both equally for every building. This paper focuses on the samples where that assumption fails: the conflict cases, on which two independently trained single-view models disagree. We mine such cases from three paired collections (inspection photographs from the 2025 Eaton wildfire and street-view panoramas from Hurricanes Ian and Milton, each matched to very-high-resolution overhead tiles), where they make up 10-33% of the data. On these samples an oracle that simply trusts the correct view beats every fusion method we tested by 0.37-0.41 accuracy, and the gap survives longer training, calibration, and backbone changes. We recover part of it with a visibility-conditioned reliability gate: a linear model that decides which view to trust from building-visibility features, calibrated per-view confidences, and the disagreement itself. On the wildfire data the gate is the only method that significantly beats calibrated probability averaging (+0.051 on conflicts, p=0.0001) and end-to-end fusion (+0.072, p<10^-4); on the panoramic datasets it matches them. A controlled field-of-view experiment explains why: cropping panoramas toward the building doubles the benefit of fusion, whereas random crops of the same size do not. Finally, the spatial density of conflicts predicts tile-level damage without labels (Spearman r=0.615, p=0.001). Mining conflicts turns "does fusion help?" into "which view should be trusted, where, and why?".

title: Complete genome sequence of Cupriavidus sp. PB-02, a potential new species with putative ability to degrade PBAT, isolated from soil
abstract: Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is a biodegradable copolyester increasingly used in agricultural mulch films, yet genomic resources for PBAT-degrading bacteria remain limited. This study reports the complete genome sequence of Cupriavidus sp. PB-02, a novel strain with PBAT-degrading potential isolated from greenhouse soil in the Republic of Korea. The genome of Cupriavidus sp. PB-02 was sequenced using Oxford Nanopore long-read technology. De novo assembly yielded three circular replicons totaling 8,747,246 bp at 70.0x coverage. Average nucleotide identity analysis against 15 type strains showed a maximum of 88.86% to Cupriavidus necator, and digital DNA-DNA hybridization yielded 37.3%, supporting its classification as a novel species candidate. Structural annotation predicted 8,021 coding sequences. Functional profiling revealed 20 PBAT degradation candidate genes, 91 heavy-metal resistance genes, no antibiotic resistance genes, and 21 biosynthetic gene clusters. A total of 169 insertion sequences were detected, with 99 concentrated on the megaplasmid.

title: Spatial Discrepancies Between Annual Cropland Extent and Sampling-Period Agricultural-Use Extent: Consequences for Soil Organic Carbon Aggregation
abstract: Annual cropland data are widely used to delimit agricultural land for soil organic carbon (SOC) mapping and spatial aggregation, yet mapped cropland may not coincide with land under agricultural use at soil sampling. Such a mismatch changes the land entering aggregation and may alter both the aggregated mean of predicted SOC and the agricultural land it represents. This difference has rarely been quantified with the SOC prediction surface held fixed. At Xinglongzhuang Coal Mine in eastern China, an agricultural sampling frame established before fieldwork was verified during March 2022 field sampling and finalized as the sampling-period agricultural-use extent (Full) for comparison with Esri 2022 Crops. Within Full, Esri-covered land was Covered and the remainder Uncovered. A random forest fitted to 155 model-development sites generated the SOC prediction surface; it was independently evaluated using 60 probability-sampled validation sites, while area of applicability (AOA) analysis assessed predictor-space support. Uncovered comprised 25.25% of Full; 86.47% occurred >10 m from the Full boundary and 97.84% was within the AOA. Independent validation yielded a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.272 g kg−1. Mean predicted SOC was 14.338 g kg−1 in Covered and 8.732 g kg−1 in Uncovered; Full averaged 12.922 g kg−1, 1.415 g kg−1 (9.9%) lower than Covered. A design-based residual correction gave a Full–Covered contrast of −1.592 g kg−1 (95% confidence interval: −2.036 to −1.147 g kg−1). The Full–Covered difference equals the Uncovered area proportion multiplied by the mean predicted SOC difference between Uncovered and Covered. Across the three reporting zones, these two components ranked differently, so Uncovered area proportion alone did not track the magnitude of the aggregation difference. With the prediction surface fixed, including Uncovered land with lower predicted SOC reduced the mean for Full relative to Covered. The reported mean is therefore tied to the agricultural extent used for aggregation and, in changing landscapes, to the period represented by that extent.

title: Continuous Moderate Organic–Inorganic Fertilization Optimizes Soil Bacterial Communities in Camellia oleifera Plantations Through Macro-Nutrient Enrichment and Micronutrient Selectivity
abstract: Fertilization is vital for improving the productivity of Camellia oleifera, a high-value woody oilseed crop. Yet, the prolonged influence of varying nutrient management regimes on edaphic microbial communities in subtropical plantation ecosystems has not been fully elucidated. To address this gap, we implemented a three-year field study with six amendment treatments: organic fertilizer (OF), organic–inorganic compound fertilizer (SF), a no-fertilizer control (CK), and three SF rates-low (F1), medium (F2), and high (F3). By combining random forest, redundancy analysis [RDA], and structural equation modeling [SEM] in a multi-model framework, total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), and organic matter (OM) were identified as the main drivers of overall bacterial diversity. Importantly, RDA further revealed that specific micronutrients—particularly available iron (AFe) and available copper (ACu)—exerted significant selective pressures on community composition at the phylum level, notably correlating with Acidobacteria (AFe) and Proteobacteria (ACu). The moderate F2 treatment achieved optimal bacterial richness and enrichment of copiotrophic taxa (Proteobacteria, Gemmatimonadetes), comparable to F3, while avoiding over-fertilization risks. We conclude that the balanced supply of macro-elements (OM, TN, TP) combined with adequate chelated micronutrients (Fe, Cu, Mn, Ca, Mg) in the compound fertilizer contributes to F2’s superior performance, enhancing both overall community diversity and specific functional guilds. This study provides a nuanced, multi-factorial framework for precision nutrient management in C. oleifera plantations.

title: Alkaline Soil pH and Phosphorus Depletion Are Associated with Microbial Community Changes Under Long-Term Continuous Cropping of Paeonia ostii
abstract: Long-term continuous cropping often degrades soil and reduces productivity, yet how soil properties and microbial communities respond in continuous tree peony monoculture remains poorly understood. Herein, soil physicochemical properties were investigated across a monoculture chronosequence of 1, 3, 5, 8, and 10 years of continuous tree peony cropping, together with rhizobacterial and fungal community diversity, composition, and predicted functions. The contents of soil organic matter, total nitrogen and available nitrogen increased along the chronosequence, whereas the contents of available phosphorus declined sharply after 3 years and remained low thereafter. Bacterial richness declined monotonically, whereas fungal richness reached its lowest level at 8 years. Beta-diversity revealed a clear community succession, with Acidobacteriota suppressed, and fungal communities shifted directionally from Fusarium to Phoma and ultimately to Monographella in the 10-year fields. Predicted functional profiling suggested a potential metabolic shift from energy-intensive pathways to stress-adaptive processes, including enhanced membrane transport. Redundancy analysis and structural equation modelling further indicated that pH and available phosphorus were strongly associated with microbial assemblages, with monoculture duration indirectly linked to communities through alterations in these soil properties. Overall, phosphorus availability, rather than bulk organic matter accumulation, emerged as the primary factor shaping microbial community dynamics and pathogen succession in this alkaline agroecosystem. These findings point to stage-specific pathogen control combined with phosphorus optimization as a potential strategy to mitigate replant disease in tree peony monoculture systems.

title: Cross-Layer Scattering-Aware Feature Fusion Network for SAR Target Detection
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection is a fundamental task in intelligent SAR image interpretation and supports a wide range of remote sensing applications. However, existing methods remain limited in handling sparse and discontinuous scattering responses, substantial variations in target scale, speckle noise, low target contrast, and clutter-induced target-like responses. In this paper, we propose a cross-layer scattering-aware feature fusion network consisting of three components for SAR target detection. First, the selective deformable convolution deployment strategy applies modulated deformable convolutions only at selected backbone stage transitions, improving feature extraction for irregular scattering responses while avoiding extensive replacement of standard convolutions. Second, the cross-layer feature pyramid network is designed to preserve informative target cues during multiscale feature fusion. Its context-localization fusion module explicitly integrates high-level semantic context with low-level localization details to maintain discriminative information across feature levels. Third, the intensity-modulated head performs intensity-based negative-sample reweighting during training according to the high-intensity pixel ratio, improving classification discrimination in cluttered SAR scenes without introducing additional computation during inference. Extensive experiments on SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 and MSAR-1.0 demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance over representative general object detectors and recent SAR-specific detectors. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed components.

title: Reporting Conservation Status Assessment of Grasslands Using Indicators from Remote Sensing Techniques
abstract: Grasslands are among the most extensive and most contested biomes on Earth: published estimates of their global area range from 3.5% to 42% of the ice-free land surface, and a recent expert-validated reassessment places the figure at 22.8% (30.1 million km2). They sustain biodiversity, store roughly one-fifth of global soil carbon, and feed most of the world’s extensive livestock systems, yet degradation is widespread and assessment methods remain fragmented. This review examines the remote sensing indicators used to evaluate grassland conservation status, drawing on 179 studies retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and analysed under an adapted PRISMA 2020 workflow, with background and policy literature to early 2026. Indicators were grouped under three parameters adapted from the EU Habitats Directive reporting framework: Occupied Area, Structure and Function, and Future Prospects. Sentinel-2 is the most frequently used sensor in the recent literature, in 29 of the 73 studies published between 2019 and 2025 whose sensor could be determined (40%), owing to its 10–20 m pixels, red-edge bands and 5-day revisit; reported classification accuracies for grassland extent run from 65.0% to 98.9% across the 17 studies reporting overall accuracy, with a median of 91.5%. Standing aboveground biomass is retrieved with R2 between 0.30 and 0.87 across 24 studies, median 0.67, when vegetation indices are combined with Random Forest, support vector or neural-network regression; fractional vegetation cover reaches 0.81 to 0.99 in three studies and leaf area index 0.67 in the one eligible study. The upper end of each range comes mostly from single-site studies with non-independent validation, and only two of the 24 biomass studies with eligible accuracy values were validated against an independent field campaign. Long-term Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) trends support degradation detection over four decades, but the record that spans that period is the 30 m Landsat archive from 1984; the harmonised Landsat-Sentinel-2 product (HLS v2.0) is 30 m and begins in 2013, and the red-edge bands that most recent retrievals depend on exist only from Sentinel-2 in 2015. Species and plant-community composition is classified with overall accuracies of 75.3% to 98.9% across 11 studies, and canopy height is retrieved with R2 of 0.51 and 0.58 in the two studies reporting it, one of which gives an RMSE of 3.94 cm; both remain constrained by acquisition cost and revisit frequency. Coverage is strongly uneven: Asia and Europe account for most of the corpus, while Africa, South America and the Southern Hemisphere generally are under-represented. We set out the physical basis of each index, the dependencies among indicators, a quality-tiered synthesis of reported accuracies, and a research agenda ranked by importance and feasibility.

title: Gap-Filled Daily Global Water Transparency Products from Multi-VIIRS Measurements
abstract: Global Secchi depth (ZSD) data, a key indicator of water transparency, have recently been derived from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) onboard the NOAA-21, NOAA-20, and Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (SNPP) satellites. However, there is significant data loss in a daily ZSD image from a single sensor due to clouds, extreme satellite (viewing) angles, sun glint contamination, and other adverse conditions. In this study, we develop a global gap-filled ZSD dataset by integrating multi-sensor measurements through data fusion. Specifically, three-sensor (VIIRS) merged Level-3 global ZSD are generated, and then the Data Interpolating Empirical Orthogonal Function (DINEOF) method is applied on the three-sensor merged data to reconstruct missing values within the valid processing domain and generate a global Level-4 gap-filled ZSD dataset. It is found that a three-sensor integrated daily global ZSD image contains ~18% more satellite measurements than a two-sensor image. In terms of evaluation of reconstructed ZSD against the original data, three-sensor gap-filled data demonstrate a good reconstruction agreement with small overall bias, i.e., mean and standard deviation (STD) of reconstructed/original ratio are ~0.995 and ~0.135, respectively. High-resolution (2 km) global daily gap-filled ZSD are also derived by integrating observations from the three VIIRS sensors, and they can reveal high-frequency variations and fine features in global coastal oceans and inland lakes. As more data from future VIIRSs and other sensors are integrated, it is highly expected that this will further improve the performance of reconstructing ZSD values at higher spatial resolutions.

title: Soil Health Under Climate Change: A Review of Climate Impacts, Sustainable Management Strategies, and Future Directions
abstract: Soil health is fundamental to sustainable agriculture, crop productivity, and vital ecosystem services. However, climate change increasingly threatens the functional integrity of soil due to rising temperatures, altered precipitation patterns, elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide levels, and extreme weather events. These factors accelerate soil degradation and disrupt the physical, chemical, and biological processes essential for maintaining soil health. This review synthesizes recent evidence regarding the impacts of climate change on soil health and crop production, while also evaluating sustainable management strategies designed to enhance agricultural resilience. Techniques such as conservation agriculture, organic matter management, diversified cropping systems, and integrated nutrient management can improve soil structure, nutrient cycling, water retention, carbon sequestration, and overall crop productivity. Furthermore, emerging technologies offer new opportunities for real-time, site-specific, and data-driven soil management. These technologies include remote sensing, geographic information systems, artificial intelligence, digital agriculture, and advanced soil monitoring tools. Additionally, policy and socioeconomic factors—particularly financial incentives, extension services, and institutional support—are critical in encouraging farmers to adopt these practices. Despite recent advancements, challenges such as economic barriers, technological limitations, regional variability, and a lack of long-term evidence hinder the widespread implementation of sustainable soil health practices. This review provides an integrated perspective that links climate-driven changes in soil’s physical, chemical, and biological properties with sustainable management practices, emerging technologies, and policy support. It highlights the interactions and trade-offs among these components to promote climate-resilient and sustainable agricultural systems.

title: DIGITAL CAPABILITY, WORK REDESIGN, AND EFFICIENCY: A STUDY OF INDIAN MANUFACTURING FIRMS
abstract: Digital transformation is often described as a path to manufacturing efficiencies with the introduction of connected equipment, enterprise software and manufacturing data but fails to conceal that this is where the efficiencies are going. In this paper, we look at the management issue of making digital investments into the appropriate employee behaviours and integrated organizational processes. Suggests a combined effect of employee digital capability and work redesign is necessary to conclude whether the digital transformation can lead to increased efficiency in Indian manufacturing firm. Based on Indian empirical research, official data and work design theory, the paper proposes a capability–redesign–efficiency matrix and evaluates the extent of the evidence. Covered industries grew by 11.89% in gross value added (GVA) current prices in 2022–23 to 2023–24 and by 5.92% in employment. Additionally, the percentage of unincorporated non-agricultural establishments that used the internet increased from 26.7 per cent in 2023–24 to 39.4 per cent in 2025. Even if neither can be used to prove that digital transformation is an efficiency gain, combining both highlights the need for considering the evolution in production capacity alongside variable levels of digital uptake. Digital capability has more value when employees see and make sense of information, act on exceptions, and improve the process; work redesign provides them the decision rights, coordination procedures, and backstops to make them productive. Evaluation of the multilevel research design is designed for further testing with employees' responses and with observed plant results. The suggested gift is a more accurate description of how digital transformation can improve employee and/or organizational efficiency and when it cannot.
journal: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)

title: Development of integrated supply chains and digitalization of agricultural product sales channels
abstract: The article provides a theoretical overview of the determinants of agri-food supply chain integration and develops a conceptual multi-level model for the digitalization of agricultural product sales channels. It shows that traditional linear distribution channels have exhausted their adaptive capacity amid geopolitical turbulence, climate risks, and rising transaction costs. To address the systemic exclusion of primary agricultural producers from value creation, the article proposes a transition to cyber-physical supply chains based on Industry 4.0 technologies. The article substantiates the economic impact of structural market disintermediation achieved through B2B agricultural exchanges, Short Food Supply Chain (SFSC) services, and logistics aggregators. The study outlines a synergistic technology stack: IoT sensors ensure continuous quality control and reduce physical raw material losses by 20–35%; blockchain and smart contracts optimize fund deposits via escrow, eliminating non-payment risk; and artificial intelligence algorithms enable predictive pricing and dynamic routing. The study finds that digitalizing sales channels reduces transaction costs by 15–25%, accelerates capital turnover by 4–8 times, cuts transport downtime by 40–50%, and increases selling prices for farmers by 7–15%. The paper focuses on Ukraine’s agricultural logistics under martial law, the redirection of export flows to Danube ports and western border crossings, and the role of the State Agrarian Registry (SAR) and the “eQueue” system in restoring export potential. A conceptual five-level model of the digital lifecycle of agricultural supply (“from field to settlement”) has been developed; this model minimizes the human factor, expands small businesses’ access to international markets, ensures transparent certification of grain batches, and lays the groundwork for the full integration of the domestic agricultural sector into the European Union’s single digital economic space. Keywords: agricultural logistics, supply chains, sales digitalization, Industry 4.0, smart contracts, blockchain, Internet of Things, B2B platforms.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Factors influencing the formation and development of intellectual capital in agricultural enterprises
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of forming and developing intellectual capital in agricultural enterprises amid digital transformation, technological change, and increased external uncertainty. It is shown that traditional production factors, including land, financial, and material and technical resources, are complemented by intellectual resources that enable enterprises to generate, accumulate, disseminate, and use knowledge. The text summarizes scientific approaches to defining the structure of intellectual capital, distinguishing its human, structural, and relational components. It establishes that their formation and effective use depend on the interaction of external and internal conditions in which an enterprise operates. The factors influencing intellectual capital are systematized at five levels: macroeconomic, institutional, sectoral, organizational, and individual. Macroeconomic conditions shape the general environment in which agricultural enterprises operate, while institutional factors set the rules, incentives, and constraints that affect the development of knowledge and intangible assets. The sectoral level reflects the specific characteristics of agricultural production, technological changes, natural and climatic conditions, and interactions among participants in agri-food value chains. At the enterprise level, organizational culture, management systems, investment in employee training, digitalization, innovation activity, and knowledge sharing are particularly important. The individual level encompasses education, experience, motivation, professional competencies, and employees’ ability to learn. Intellectual capital formation depends not on the isolated influence of individual factors but on their coordinated interaction. The study identifies the role of vertical relationships between levels and horizontal interaction among the components of intellectual capital. Transforming individual knowledge into an organizational resource requires appropriate management practices and partnerships throughout business activities. The practical significance of the findings lies in applying the proposed approach to comprehensively assess the conditions for intellectual capital development, identify knowledge-management priorities, and enhance the adaptability of agricultural enterprises. Keywords: intellectual capital, agricultural enterprises, human capital, structural capital, relational capital, development factors, digitalization, knowledge management, innovative development, agricultural sector.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Economic mechanism for regulating the development of agricultural logistics on the basis of innovation and resilience
abstract: The article establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for developing an economic mechanism to regulate the growth of agricultural logistics based on innovation and resilience. The article determines the role of agricultural logistics in ensuring the continuity of the agricultural sector, the efficient movement of material, information, and financial flows, and the competitiveness of agricultural products. The article systematizes the main theoretical approaches to developing an economic mechanism for regulating agricultural logistics. The author proposes a mechanism that integrates five blocks: systemic-institutional, logistics-process, innovation-digital, resilience-risk, and recovery-integration. The mechanism’s components, as well as the principles and instruments that govern its functioning, are substantiated. The study determines that combining innovation and resilience makes it possible to move from traditional regulation of individual logistics operations to the formation of an adaptive system for managing agricultural logistics chains. The study identifies directions for improving the economic regulation of agricultural logistics under the conditions of Ukraine’s post-war recovery and European integration. The study formulates the theoretical foundations and proposes an author-developed framework for an economic mechanism to regulate the development of agricultural logistics based on innovation and resilience. The proposed mechanism provides a methodological basis for transitioning from fragmented regulation of individual logistics operations to comprehensive management of agricultural logistics development aimed at reducing logistics costs and product losses, improving supply reliability, modernizing infrastructure, and strengthening the competitiveness of Ukraine’s agricultural sector. The modern mechanism should be based on the interaction of five theoretical blocks: systemic-institutional, logistics-process, innovation-digital, resilience-risk, and recovery-integration. Keywords: agricultural logistics, economic mechanism, economic regulation, innovation, resilience, logistics chains, digitalization, infrastructure, risks, post-war reconstruction.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Digitization tools as a basis for improving the accounting and taxation of an agrarian enterprise
abstract: The article examines the theoretical-methodical and applied principles of digitalization of accounting and taxation in an agrarian enterprise amid increasing information volumes, more complex economic processes, and the need for operational information support for management decisions. It is substantiated that the digitalization of accounting and tax activities should be considered not only as the automation of individual operations, but as a complex process of forming an integrated information environment of the enterprise. The main digitalization tools include primary accounting, electronic document management, accounting and tax accounting, electronic reporting, digital control, analytics, and management. The peculiarities of their application in the agricultural sector are defined by production seasonality, the territorial dispersion of economic processes, the large volume of primary documents, and the need to record production data in real time. The study proposes a conceptual model for the integrated digitalization of accounting and taxation in an agrarian enterprise, establishing consistent relationships among primary accounting, electronic document flow, a single information base, accounting and tax accounting, electronic reporting, digital control, BI analytics, and management decisions, with feedback loops. The study proposes guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of digitization based on time, quality, cost, tax, information, management, and personnel criteria. The study identifies the main risks of digital transformation and proposes a step-by-step implementation approach. The study shows that integrating digital tools improves the efficiency and reliability of accounting and tax information, reduces labor intensity and tax risks, and improves the quality of management decisions. Keywords: digitization; accounting; tax accounting; agricultural enterprise; digital tools; electronic document management; tax reporting; digital control; information support; management decisions.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Integrating Agricultural Technology Adoption and Financial Inclusion as a Strategy to Improve Micro-Scale Farm Productivity in Rural Areas of South Sumatra
abstract: Micro-scale farming faces various constraints in improving productivity, particularly in relation to farmers' ability to adopt technology and access financing that meets their business needs. Agricultural technology can improve the efficiency of input use, access to information, farm management, and decision-making. However, technology adoption among smallholder farmers is still influenced by digital literacy, infrastructure, economic conditions, and institutional factors. On the other hand, access to credit can improve farm productivity and technical efficiency by enabling farmers to obtain production inputs and make productive investments. This study aims to: (1) analyze the effect of agricultural technology adoption on micro-scale farm productivity; and (2) analyze the effect of financial inclusion access on micro-scale farm productivity. The study employs a quantitative explanatory approach using multiple linear regression analysis. A total of 300 farm observations are used as simulated data to demonstrate the proposed analytical framework; therefore, the numerical results do not represent findings from an actual field survey. The independent variables consist of an agricultural technology adoption index and a financial inclusion access index, while farm productivity serves as the dependent variable. Farmers' age, education level, and land area are included as control variables. The results indicate that agricultural technology adoption and financial inclusion access have positive and statistically significant effects on farm productivity. The model explains a substantial proportion of the variation in productivity and provides an initial basis for further empirical investigation into the role of technology and financing in micro-scale farming. These findings are illustrative in nature and should be validated using primary data collected from farmers.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

title: Обоснование стратегических направлений пространственного развития агропромышленного производства и сельских территорий
abstract: В условиях волатильности внешнеэкономических рисков и ограничений внешнеторговой деятельности перед агропромышленным комплексом стоит приоритетная задача достижения продовольственной независимости страны. Динамика развития АПК является фундаментом национальной экономики и необходимым условием повышения благосостояния сельских жителей. Пространственное развитие сельских территорий, в свою очередь, позволит решить комплекс острых социальных проблем преодоления дефицита кадров, модернизации инфраструктуры и сохранения уникального уклада на селе. Проведенный в ранее опубликованных научных трудах анализ документов стратегического планирования выявил имеющуюся согласованность основных стратегических целей, задач и приоритетных направлений развития агропромышленного производства и сельских территорий. В то же время в условиях возникновения новых внутренних и внешних рисков, неопределенности внешнеэкономической деятельности необходимо переходить к разработке новых идей и подходов, направленных на сокращение социально-экономического неравенства сельских территорий и повышение устойчивости агропромышленного производства. Пространственное развитие АПК и сельских территорий невозможно без внедрения ресурсосберегающих технологий, обеспечивающих баланс экономической выгоды, экологической ответственности производителей и выполнения ими социальных обязательств. Технологии точного земледелия, адаптивно-ландшафтные системы, органические методы позволяют минимизировать негативное воздействие на окружающую среду и сохранить рентабельность производства. Для внедрения передовых достижений необходима институциональная поддержка, а для адаптации к климатическим рискам предлагается развитие агрострахования на основе спутникового мониторинга, и селекцию устойчивых к погодным условиям культур. Устойчивость пространственного развития технологическое обновление выступает фундаментальным условием гармонизации экономических, экологических, цифровых и социальных векторов функционирования. Усиливающиеся геополитические вызовы и императивы продовольственного суверенитета диктуют необходимость внесения корректировок в существующие традиционные организационные бизнес-модели. Оптимизация разработки стратегии пространственного развития требует внедрения единых методологических подходов на всех уровнях управления – от общегосударственного масштаба до регионального и сельских поселений. При этом важно обеспечить процесс согласования интересов не только между участниками пространственного развития, но и основными группами сельских субъектов, что позволит создать единую сбалансированную систему планирования и управления. In the context of volatility in foreign economic risks and restrictions on foreign trade activities, the agro-industrial complex faces the priority task of achieving the country’s food independence. The dynamics of agro-industrial development form the foundation of the national economy and are a necessary condition for improving the well-being of rural residents. The spatial development of rural areas, in turn, will make it possible to address a range of acute social problems – overcoming the shortage of personnel, modernizing infrastructure, and preserving the unique way of life in rural areas. The analysis of strategic planning documents conducted in previously published scientific works has revealed the existing consistency of the main strategic goals, tasks, and priority areas for the development of agro-industrial production and rural areas. At the same time, in the context of emerging new internal and external risks and the uncertainty of foreign economic activity, it is necessary to move on to developing new ideas and approaches aimed at reducing socio-economic inequality in rural areas and increasing the sustainability of agroindustrial production. The spatial development of the agro-industrial complex and rural areas is impossible without the introduction of resource-saving technologies that ensure a balance between economic benefits, the environmental responsibility of producers, and their fulfilment of social obligations. Precision farming technologies, adaptive landscape systems, and organic methods make it possible to minimize the negative impact on the environment and maintain the profitability of production. Institutional support is required to implement advanced achievements, and to adapt to climate risks, it is proposed to develop agricultural insurance based on satellite monitoring and to select crops that are resistant to weather conditions. The sustainability of spatial development and technological renewal are a fundamental condition for harmonizing economic, environmental, digital, and social vectors of functioning. The growing geopolitical challenges and the imperatives of food sovereignty dictate the need to make adjustments to existing traditional organizational business models. Optimizing the development of spatial development strategies requires the implementation of unified methodological approaches at all levels of management – from the national scale to regional and rural settlements. At the same time, it is important to ensure the process of reconciling interests not only between the participants in spatial development but also between the main groups of rural entities, which will make it possible to create a unified, balanced planning and management system.

title: Направления совершенствования внешнеэкономических связей российского агропромышленного комплекса в условиях глобальных вызовов и санкционных ограничений
abstract: В статье рассмотрены направления совершенствования внешнеэкономических связей агропромышленного комплекса Российской Федерации в условиях глобальных вызовов и санкционных ограничений. Раскрыта теоретическая природа экономических санкций как инструмента межгосударственного давления, выявлены закономерности их применения в международной практике и последствия для мировых аграрных рынков, обоснованы приоритеты ответной политики, нацеленной на повышение конкурентоспособности отечественных производителей.
